{"assumptions":["K compact and convex in a locally convex Hausdorff space","K metrizable for the measure to live on ext K itself"],"created_at":"2026-08-29T02:26:24.139081+00:00","domain":"functional analysis / convexity","id":"claim_0a8ceaa5f37b374709515e490798b2dbcdf330a9987e8089bd7542bf2dd180cd","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let K be a compact convex subset of a locally convex Hausdorff topological vector space, and suppose K is metrizable. Then the set ext K of extreme points of K is a G_delta set, and for every x in K there is a Borel probability measure mu on K, concentrated on ext K, whose barycenter is x: phi(x) = integral phi dmu for every continuous linear functional phi. Without metrizability, the Bishop-de Leeuw theorem gives a probability measure that vanishes on every Baire set disjoint from ext K. The Krein-Milman theorem, that K is the closed convex hull of ext K, is the qualitative counterpart. Uniqueness of the representing measure for every x characterises the Choquet simplices.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Zero-mean fixed finite-rank GP, supplied feature norms <=R, independent Gaussian noise variance s>0","At most n context labels; all input locations and context length jointly independent of latent GP and noises; iid tasks","Full original posterior is the target; only the predictor clips context labels at the explicit deterministic B"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:46:14.074691+00:00","domain":"Gaussian process predictive approximation; context truncation","id":"claim_0aac28c997e413b6e870c7d366e02430c9ded09828abe71420cb34a1f75fae4a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"OWNER RESULT DRAFT, proof (unaudited), C007 v1; no novelty claim.
Let a fixed zero-mean finite-rank Gaussian process have a supplied feature map phi with ||phi(x)||<=R, independent Gaussian observation noise of variance s>0, and at most n context observations. All context/query input locations and context length are jointly independent of the GP and all noises. Context labels may be correlated and are not bounded or conditioned. Put V=s+R^2. Given the full original context W, let P_W=N(m,v) be the exact noisy posterior predictive. Clip each context label to [-B,B], B>0, and recompute the mean m_B with the same design; v is unchanged. Suppose a Gaussian predictor h_B=N(mhat,vhat), depending only on clipped context and supplied features, has vhat>=s and KL(N(m_B,v)||h_B)<=eps_c for every possible context and design. Then on the ORIGINAL unconditioned task law,
E_W KL(P_W||h_B) <= 2 eps_c + (2 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/s^3) exp(-B^2/(4V)).
In particular, for eps>0, eps_c=eps/4 and B=sqrt(4V log(max(e,4 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/(s^3 eps)))) make the expected KL at most eps. If nR=0 the bias is zero. This does not assert that N(m_B,v) is the conditional law given clipped labels. The supplied-feature comparator exists by the separately audited C002 construction; this clipping lemma itself awaits independent review.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.911750+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0aaecc49d44d87907f247a5d4649f0d44cb4b47482a6a7ec68426e9191e0ff9a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 1 (Criterion for $\Xstar_T$ {\cite[Lemma~4.1) of arXiv:2608.24294, 'Existence of densities and atoms for the running maximum of time-inhomogeneous jump diffus'] {NakagawaSuzuki2024}}]
Fix $p>1$ and $\Theta=(h,v)\in \Hb_{\infty-}\times \Vb_{\infty-}$.
For each $n\ge1$, let $\{X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process, and let $\{X_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process.
Write
\[
\Xstarn_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X^{(n)}_s,
\qquad
\Xstar_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X_s.
\]

Assume that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E[|\Xstarn_T|^p]<\infty$, and for every $t\in[0,T]$ we have $X^{(n)}_t\in W^{1,p}_\Theta$ with
\[
\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|D_\Theta X^{(n)}_s|^p\Big]<\infty;
\]
\item for each $n\ge1$, the process $\{D_\Theta X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ admits a right-continuous version;
\item $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|X^{(n)}_s-X_s|^p\Big]=0$.
\end{enumerate}
Assume moreover that $D_\Theta X$ admits a right-continuous version and satisfies
\[
\Pbb\big(D_\Theta X_t\neq 0 \text{ on }\{t\in(0,T]: X_t=\Xstar_T\}\big)=1.
\]
Then the law of $\Xstar_T$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\R$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

The fixed-step bounds also cover D=0. All norms are Euclidean. Source: Zijian Liu and Zhengyuan Zhou, On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Shuffling Gradient Methods, Theorem 4.4 and its full version Theorem C.1.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T11:58:53.978374+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ab65f335e4846d89753e7dca87d1223","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Exact rank three for the bounded-density conjecture: what is proved and what is open. (1) The step 'a rank-three coarea bound ||p_S||_inf <= K ||rho||_inf^{2/3} for S = sum_{j<=3} lambda_j Y_j^2' is false for general bounded densities rho on R^3: a density rho <= B that puts mass 2hB A(s) on the shell {|S - s| < h} gives p_S about B A(s) near s, where A(s) = d/ds vol{S <= s} = 2 pi s^{1/2}/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2 lambda_3) for a definite form, unbounded as s grows; a bound needs regularity of rho beyond its supremum. (2) Orthonormal 3D projections of product densities have that regularity on spheres: their spherical means satisfy M_{y0}(r) <= 6/(pi r) uniformly in the centre, and definite rank-three forms have density <= 82 for every linear term. (3) The marginal bound is sharp and law-free: the projection onto a k-dimensional subspace of a vector with independent coordinates of densities <= 1 has density <= min{(n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2}} (Livshyts, Paouris and Pivovarov 2016); Ball's cube slicing is the uniform case and Rudelson-Vershynin give (CK)^d with an unspecified absolute C. (4) Indefinite exact rank three is bounded with any c-pivot, when every leverage is at most 1/2 (<= 12), for a leak-free hub with the linear term in the range (<= 278), and for a leaking hub with a spread light frame up to a factor log(1/eps); the no-pivot indefinite case with a hub (a hub plus a small cross term) is open and is the single-hub core of the general conjecture.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.211852+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ac6c86f902d62b5037f21bb5d2b9e94b3dc420f9686cffab5c2fcd0a8d5005a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Fix constants $C',c', K>0$. 
Let $X$ be a nonnegative random variable such that $\E X \leq r$ and, for some $\sigma \in (0,K]$, 
\[
\P(X>u ) \leq C' e^{- c' u^2/\sigma^2}\,.
\]
Then for each $\lambda>0$, there exist constants $C_\lambda, c_\lambda>0$ (depending also on $c',C'$, and $K$) such that
\[
  \E e^{\lambda X}-1 \leq C_\lambda r + C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
\]
\begin{proof}
On the event $\{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}\}$, the mean value theorem yields
\[
  \E[(e^{\lambda X} - 1) \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq \E[\lambda e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}} X \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda r\,,
\]
where the $\sigma$ independence in the last bound comes from $\sigma\leq K$.
On  $\{X > \sigma^{1/2}\}$, we write
\begin{multline}
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] - (e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}}-1)\P(X>\sigma^{1/2})
  \\
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \int_0^x \partial_u (e^{\lambda u}) \d u ~\d \P_X(x)  
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \P(X>u) \lambda e^{\lambda u} \d  u  \leq C_\lambda \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} e^{-c'\frac{u^2}{\sigma^2} + \lambda u} \d u\,.
\end{multline}
Now, for $u\geq \sigma^{1/2}$ and $\lambda>0$, there exists $\sigma_\lambda>0$ such that for all $\sigma \in (0,\sigma_\lambda]$, we have 
$
  \lambda u \leq \tfrac{c' u^2}{2\sigma^2}$.
For such $\sigma$, it follows from \eqref{eq:layer-cake} that
$
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
$
For $\sigma >\sigma_\lambda$, note that the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:layer-cake} can be bounded by a constant $C_\lambda'>0$ times the Laplace transform of a Gaussian with variance $K^2/2c'$
to get 
$\E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda$,
possibly enlarging $C_\lambda$ from before.
We finish by multiplying by $e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma} e^{c_\lambda/\sigma_\lambda}$, which is larger than $1$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f is continuous on a closed cylinder around (t_0,y_0)","f is Lipschitz in y, uniformly in t, on that cylinder"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T14:20:41.451641+00:00","domain":"ordinary differential equations","id":"claim_0ad98344cc4c4b7f94070b09639fced6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f: [t_0-a,t_0+a] x B(y_0,b) -> R^n be continuous, where B(y_0,b) subset R^n is the closed ball of radius b around y_0, and suppose f is Lipschitz in its second argument uniformly in the first: there is L >= 0 with |f(t,y_1)-f(t,y_2)| <= L|y_1-y_2| for all t in the interval and y_1,y_2 in B(y_0,b). Let M = max|f(t,y)| over this compact domain and h = min(a, b/M). Then the initial value problem y'(t) = f(t,y(t)), y(t_0)=y_0, has a unique solution y on [t_0-h, t_0+h]. (When M = 0, read b/M as infinity, so h = a.) Continuity alone does not give uniqueness: y' = 2 sqrt(|y|), y(0) = 0 has infinitely many solutions. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:05:52.473602+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0af724e628d0e824651e9ac4a5be49262c17a0896236d3cc1aac725ea1ccb05b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:push-forward of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Let $\\varphi_{X}:\\mathbb{R}\\rightarrow[0,1]$ be the Borel-measurable map defined by $a\\mapsto \\ensuremath{\\mathbb{P}} \\left[ X\\geq a \\right]$, and then for each Borel set $E\\subseteq [0,1]$, let $\\alpha(E)$ be the Lebesgue measure of the inverse image $\\varphi_{X}^{-1}(E)$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.501965+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0afdafd4b352c5fcad844d588f8048f7a3634622f9b8b5964f08fe8ff6f0d068","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theo 22 (Explicit threshold, compact-support branch and onset amplitude) of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Let $0<\alpha<1$ and $n\ge2$. Consider the problem
\[
\begin{cases}
	-u''=\lambda u+m_n(x)u^\alpha,& -1<x<1,\\
	u(-1)=u(1)=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Define
\[
\lambda_{c,n}:=
\frac{\pi^2}
{\left((1-\alpha)+\dfrac{1+\alpha}{n}\right)^2}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\pi^2}{4}
<
\lambda_{c,n}
<
\lambda_n^*.
\]
At $\lambda=\lambda_{c,n}$ there exists an even positive flat solution
$u_{c,n}$ satisfying $u_{c,n}(\pm1)=u_{c,n}'(\pm1)=0$. For every
$\lambda\in(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$ there exists a unique even
non-negative solution in the above class whose connected support is
\[
\operatorname{supp}u_{\lambda,n}
=
[-b_{\lambda,n},b_{\lambda,n}]
\Subset(-1,1),
\]
where
\[
b_{\lambda,n}
=
\frac{1}{1-\alpha}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{\lambda}}
-\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right).
\]
For $x\ge0$ the solution is
\[
u_{\lambda,n}(x)
=
\begin{cases}
	A_{\lambda,n}\cos(\sqrt{\lambda}\,x),
	& 0\le x\le\dfrac1n,\\[2mm]
	\displaystyle
	\left(
	\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
	\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
	\sin^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}
	\left[
	\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\sqrt{\lambda}\,
	(b_{\lambda,n}-x)
	\right],
	& \dfrac1n\le x\le b_{\lambda,n},\\[3mm]
	0,
	& b_{\lambda,n}\le x\le1,
\end{cases}
\]
and it is extended evenly to $(-1,0)$. Moreover,
\[
A_{\lambda,n}
=
\|u_{\lambda,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)}
=
\left(
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{n}\right).
\]
For each fixed $n$, the mapping $\lambda\longmapsto A_{\lambda,n}$
is strictly decreasing on $(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$, and
$A_{\lambda,n}\longrightarrow0\hbox{ as }\lambda\uparrow\lambda_n^*$. If
\[
A_n:=\|u_{c,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)},
\]
then
\[
A_n=
\left[
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\left(
(1-\alpha)+\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right)^2
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{n(1-\alpha)+(1+\alpha)}
\right),
\]
and
\[
\lambda_{c,n}\uparrow
\lambda_{c,\infty}:=
\frac{\pi^2}{(1-\alpha)^2},
\]
while
\[
A_n\longrightarrow
A_\infty:=
\left[
\frac{2(1-\alpha)^2}
{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
>0.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\frac{\lambda_{c,n}}{\lambda_n^*}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover, $H_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})=M_n(u_{\lambda,n})<0$, and therefore
$E_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})>0,\ E_\lambda''(u_{\lambda,n})<0$. Thus, these
explicit solutions have the variational character of the
branch $u_{\lambda,n}^-$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:47:21.707737+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0afe512151e2d3f26c24edcfb8cfe78cf1808841191a2423e834dc778bac441e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem Voiculescu of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $A_1 = U_1 \text{} \ensuremath{\operatorname{diag}} (a^{(1)}_1, \ldots,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:20:15.584552+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b1191ef09950f6ad3cb62bb13960127422f720ada59bb83e0e3f4b160c62b41","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:scaled-murmuration of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $k\geq 2$ be fixed.  Let $P\neq 2$ be a prime, and suppose that $P$, $X$, and $Y$ tend to infinity.
Assume that
\[
Y=(1+o(1))X^{1-\delta_1},
\qquad
P^k\ll X^{1+\delta_2},
\]
where
\[
0<2\delta_2<\delta_1<\frac18,
\qquad
(k-1)\delta_2<1.
\]
Put
\[
\eta=\frac{\delta_1}{2}-\delta_2,
\qquad
y=\frac{P^k}{X}.
\]
Let
\[
A=\prod_p\left(1+\frac{p}{(p+1)^2(p-1)}\right),
\]
\[
B=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{p}{(p^2-1)^2}\right),
\]
and
\[
C(r)=\prod_{p\mid r}
\left(1+\frac{p^2}{p^4-2p^2-p+1}\right).
\]
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{multline*}
\frac{
\displaystyle
\sideset{}{'}\sum_{N\in[X,X+Y]}
\ \sum_{f\in H_{\mathrm{new}}(N)}
P^{k/2}\lambda_{\operatorname{sym}^k f}(P)\,\varepsilon(f)
}{
\displaystyle
\sideset{}{'}\sum_{N\in[X,X+Y]}
\ \sum_{f\in H_{\mathrm{new}}(N)}1
}
\\
=
\frac{12}{\pi D_0}
\left(
A\sqrt y
+
B\sum_{1\leq r\leq 2\sqrt y}
C(r)\sqrt{4y-r^2}
-\pi y
\right)
+
O_{k,\varepsilon}\left(
X^{-\eta+\varepsilon}
+X^\varepsilon\frac{\sqrt y}{P}
+\frac{1+y}{P}
\right).
\end{multline*}
Here the prime indicates that the sum is restricted to squarefree integers $N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X compact, T continuous.","The two limits in eps are monotone so they exist in [0, infinity];","separated and spanning counts interleave by r(n,eps) <= s(n,eps) <= r(n, eps/2), which is why the two definitions agree."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:04:29.025418+00:00","domain":"dynamical systems, entropy","id":"claim_0b2a19515f9b50a6070dee1dd7534cd4a246344088b2dfd716b30980eb13ccc5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T : X -> X continuous. Define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max over 0 <= k < n of d(T^k x, T^k y). A set E is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if distinct points of E are at d_n-distance greater than eps; a set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if every point of X is within d_n-distance eps of some point of F. Let s(n,eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n,eps)-separated set and r(n,eps) the smallest cardinality of an (n,eps)-spanning set. Then the topological entropy is h_top(T) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log s(n,eps) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log r(n,eps), and this agrees with the open-cover definition of Adler, Konheim and McAndrew. The quantity does not depend on the metric, only on the topology, and is invariant under topological conjugacy.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:20:07.894149+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b2a637fb99f9bae87ccc005dd98fb1ea111fd8fcbee067b2e1bcaac567e6a2f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma sylvester_equation_weight_operator of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] Let $\mathbf{X} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ and $\varepsilon > 0$.
    Let the SVD of $\mathbf{X}$ be given by $\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^{\top}$,

    For $i \in [\max \left( d_1 , d_2 \right)]$,
    set
    $\lambda_i := \max \left( \sigma_i, \varepsilon \right)$ with the convention of $\sigma_i = 0$ for $i > d$.
    Define the vectors
    $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_1 := (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_{d_1}) \in \R^{d_1}$
    and

    Then,

    its image via the harmonic-mean weight operator  $\W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{Z})$ with core matrix (eq:harmonic:mean of the paper) is the unique solution of the Sylvester equation
    \begin{equation}

    where $\mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{U}} = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag(\boldsymbol{\lambda}_1) \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}^{\top}$

{"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0064-infrared-bound-for-nearest-neighbour-percolation-in-every-dimension-d","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.042777+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b65f9440e44a1939a7c37c4a3d79566b822d1d97ca4449343b4b1d8ecf71796","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine the small parameter of the lace expansion and whether a different expansion parameter exists for d in {7,...,10}. Result: The lace expansion converges when the triangle diagram at p_c is small, which for nearest-neighbour percolation is controlled by the random-walk quantities: the triangle at p_c is bounded by a constant times (2d)^{-1} times sum over n of the return probabilities, i.e. by beta_d = O(1/d); the NoBLE refinement replaces 1/d by a numerically computed constant and the bootstrap closes for d >= 11 because the computed bound on the triangle at d = 10 exceeds the threshold. Below d = 11 there is no small parameter: the triangle diagram is of order 1 but finite for d > 6, and finiteness alone does not make the expansion converge; convergence needs smallness. An alternative is to bootstrap from d = 11 downward using a continuous interpolation in the dimension (long-range or spread-out interpolation), but the interpolated models at d = 10 are spread-out models, whose infrared bound is already known, and the interpolation does not return to the nearest-neighbour model at d = 10 without passing through a non-small regime. So the obstruction is structural: the method requires a small parameter and there is none for nearest-neighbour d in {7,...,10}. A rigorous partial statement: the infrared bound holds for the nearest-neighbour model in d in {7,...,10} on any lattice whose triangle diagram at p_c is below the NoBLE threshold, which fails for Z^d but holds for some non-Z^d lattices of higher coordination number (e.g. the body-centred or the D_d-type lattices in d = 7, 8 where the coordination number is larger); I did not verify the threshold numerically for those lattices. Obstruction: No small parameter for nearest-neighbour Z^d with 7 <= d <= 10.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:27.580584+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b8185d657d046e082a7b6c18e617f82ef2c43b55fb618f9ff5d5ee03cb237cf","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 20 (Girsanov is not tight) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Let $\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}$ and $\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}$ be the laws of the full and the directed (single-parent-conditioned) systems on a time interval $[0,\tau]$. The Radon--Nikodym density is
\[
\log\frac{d\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}}{d\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}}=\int_0^\tau\langle b^{-1}\Delta_t,dW_t\rangle-\frac12\int_0^\tau\|b^{-1}\Delta_t\|^2\,dt,
\]
where $\Delta_t=\gamma\,\sigma\big(s^{(v)}_t-\theta_{vu}\big)$ is the back-reaction drift. On the cascade timescale $\|\Delta_t\|=\Theta(1)$ whenever the child is active, so the quadratic-variation term is $\Theta(\tau)$ and the density is not tight toward $1$ as $G_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BS}}T$. Hence Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red} cannot be obtained by a change of measure showing $d\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}/d\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}\to1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.527213+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bb8e071126343b77b34535612ee300a284954dd91f4b90b2d41362908fc0d9e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 5 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)]$ be a path of length $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. 
    \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] Define
    $$ l_{1} = \max \big\{ k -j \ : \ 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k) \big\}. $$
This is the maximum length of loops in $\lambda$. Among the pairs $(j,k)$ that attain the maximum on the right-hand side of the definition of $l_{1}$ above, let $(j_{1},k_{1})$ be the one with the smallest $j$:
\begin{itemize}
\item let 
$$\Lambda (1) = \Big\{ (j, k) \, : \, 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k), \ \ k-j = l_{1} \Big\},$$
\item set 
$$ j_{1} = \min \big\{ 0 \le  j \le m \, : \, \exists k \in [j, m] \, \text{ such that } \, (j,k) \in \Lambda (1) \big\},$$
\item choose $k_{1}$ so that 
$(j_{1}, k_{1}) \in \Lambda (1). $
\end{itemize}
That is, $(j_{1},k_{1})$ is the leftmost pair $(j,k)$ such that $\lambda(j)=\lambda(k)$ and $k-j=l_{1}$.

\item[(ii)]
 We define $\lambda_{1}$ to be the path obtained from $\lambda$ by removing this maximal loop. That is, $\lambda_{1}$ is a path of length $m - k_{1} + j_{1}$ defined by 
$$ \lambda_{1} = [\lambda (0), \cdots, \lambda (j_{1}), \lambda (k_{1} +1), \cdots \lambda (m) ] = \lambda [0, j_{1}] \oplus \lambda [k_{1}, m]. $$
Note that $\lambda = \lambda_{1}$ if and only if $\lambda$ is a simple path. For notational convenience, we abbreviate $\lambda$ as $\lambda_0$.

\item[(iii)] Apply the procedures (i) and (ii) above to $\lambda_{1}$ in the same way. Denote the resulting path by $\lambda_{2}$. Repeating the same procedure, $\lambda_{3}, \lambda_{4}, \cdots$ are obtained.

\item[(iv)] Define $q$ by
$$ q = \min \Big\{ l \ge 0 \ : \ \text{ $\lambda_{l}$ is a simple path} \Big\}.$$
 The largest-loop-first (LLF) loop-erasure of $\lambda$ is given by 
 $$ \text{LE}^{\ast} (\lambda) = \lambda_{q}. $$

\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.160341+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bce53c2a54a877341b0ab6914a27bb4ca63a6faae2fb61944aae563360a55f7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 4 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any constant $\delta > 0$, there exists $c = c(\alpha, L, \delta) > 0$ such that with probability $1-e^{-cN}$,
    \begin{align}
        
        \bigg|\frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N} - 1\bigg| &\le \delta\,,\\
    
        \bigg|\frac{\E[ \|\hat{\by}\|^2 | \bG]}{N} - 1\bigg| &\le
        \frac{\delta}{2}\,.
    \end{align} 
Moreover, conditional on any realization of $\bG$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-y-cond-conc} the following holds. Let $\hat{\bx} = N^{1/2} \bar{\bx}  / \|\bar{\bx}\|$ (we set this arbitrarily to $\bone \in \R^N$ if $\bar{\bx} = \bzero$). Let $\bXi'$ be an independent copy of $\bXi$ and $\hat{\by}' = \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi')$. Then
    \beq
        
        \lt|\frac{\|\hat{\by}\|^2}{N} - 1\rt|\,,
        \frac{|(\hat{\bx},\hat{\by})|}{N},
        \frac{|(\hat{\by},\hat{\by}')|}{N} \le \delta
    \eeq
   with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$.

\begin{proof}
    Since $\bG \mapsto \|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $L$-Lipschitz, $\|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $O(1)$-subgaussian by gaussian concentration of measure.
    Combined with $\E \|\bar{\bx}\|^2 = N$ this implies \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}.
    We next argue that the function
    \[
        f(\bG) = \E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}
    \]
    is also $L$-Lipschitz. Indeed,
    \[
        \nabla f(\bG)
        = \frac{\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi))(\bG,\bXi) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}}\,,
    \]
    and thus
    \[
        \|\nabla f(\bG)\|^2
        = \frac{\|\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]\|^2}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le \frac{\E[ \|\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|_\op^2 \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le L^2\,.
    \]
    Thus $\E[ \|\hat{\by}\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}$ is also $O(1)$-subgaussian.
    Combined with $\E \|\hat{\by}\|^2 = N$ this proves \eqref{e:fp-y-cond-conc}. 
    The first inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly to \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}, applying gaussian concentration on $\bXi$ conditional on $\bG$.
    The second inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} holds by gaussian concentration because $\bXi \mapsto (\hat{\bx},\hat{\by}) / N$ is $L/N^{1/2}$-Lipschitz and $\E[\hat{\by} | \bG] = \bzero$. 
    The third inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly, conditioning further on a realization of $\hat{\by}$ such that $\|\hat{\by}\| \le 2N^{1/2}$ (which holds with probability $1-e^{-cN}$).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:29:28.004370+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0be3138574ffaada721bb9e1ba66473c719d7e17a3eee97388a92c6a47fcaa1c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 (Radial order-statistic representation) of arXiv:2608.24964, 'Common-Center Geometry and Certified Radial Reconstruction for Energy-Form Full Conformal '] Assume $I_1,\ldots,I_m$ are each star-shaped about the same point $c$.  For
\[
u\in\mathbb S^{d-1},
\]
define
\[
R_j(u)=\sup\{r\ge0:c+ru\in I_j\}\in[0,\infty].
\]
Let
\[
R_{(1)}(u)\le\cdots\le R_{(m)}(u)
\]
be the ascending order statistics.  For $0\le\varepsilon<1$ and
\[
1\le k=\lfloor(m+1)\varepsilon\rfloor\le m,
\]
the radial function of $\Gamma^\varepsilon$ about $c$ is
\[
R_\varepsilon(u)
=

\[

R_1\equiv+\infty.
\]
Thus finite power-distance radial reconstruction begins at $m\ge2$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["product measure on a finite product of totally ordered two-point spaces (or a measure satisfying the FKG lattice condition)","both functions increasing, or both decreasing","square integrability"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542860+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bf9a3e418fbc58529078909919960e7533413ef78f5b985e45f4917e302a72f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let P be a PRODUCT probability measure on {0,1}^E with E finite (the infinite case follows by approximation). Call f : {0,1}^E -> R increasing if f(omega) <= f(omega') whenever omega_e <= omega'_e for every e. Then for increasing f and g in L^2(P), E[f g] >= E[f] E[g]. In particular, for INCREASING events A and B, P(A and B) >= P(A) P(B), and for two DECREASING events the same inequality holds. The hypothesis that both functions are monotone IN THE SAME DIRECTION is the whole content; nothing is claimed for events of mixed or no monotonicity. The result extends beyond product measures to any measure satisfying the FKG LATTICE CONDITION mu(x or y) mu(x and y) >= mu(x) mu(y), which covers the random-cluster and ferromagnetic Ising measures; that extension is the FKG inequality proper, Harris's version being the product case. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:29:21.917044+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c01392a1bd9c746e686d9a5483d0fcac5dfd5992ca13f504729f5d405f12239","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Extended mapping) of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, let $d\in\mathbb N$,
and let
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\colon \mathbb R^n\to \mathbb R^k$ be a measurable mapping
such that
\[
0<\sigma_{f_j}^2:=\operatorname{Var}_\mu(f_j)<\infty
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Let
\[
\hat f_j
=
\sigma_{f_j}^{-1}
\biggl(f_j-\int_{\mathbb R^n} f_j\,d\mu\biggr)
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\},
\]
and set
$\hat f:=(\hat f_1,\ldots,\hat f_k)$.
Assume also that
\[
\hat f^{\mathbf m}:=\hat f_1^{m_1}\ldots \hat f_k^{m_k}\in L^2(\mu)
\quad \forall \mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_k)\in\mathbb Z_+^k
\quad\text{with}\quad
1\le |\mathbf m|\le d^{k-1}.
\]
We define the \emph{extended mapping} of order $d$ by
\[
F_\mu^d(f)
=
\bigl(\hat f^{\mathbf m}\bigr)_{1\le |\mathbf m|\le d^{k-1}},
\]
and set
\[
\Sigma_\mu^d(f):=\operatorname{Cov}_\mu \bigl(F_\mu^d(f)\bigr).
\]
In other words, $\Sigma_\mu^d(f)$ is the matrix, in the monomial basis, of the quadratic form
\[
Q\mapsto \operatorname{Var}_\mu\bigl(Q(\hat f)\bigr),\quad Q\in\mathcal P_{d^{k-1}}(\mathbb R^k),\quad

{"assumptions":["mu has compact support of positive diameter D.","t>D^2.","The source's kernel-level criterion for free Brownian unimodality."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.365295+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ca5188ff0c8e88bf00b55cc6acb52134e15e6f99743df668c6f966aee5a39ec","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the criterion reproduces the source's worked example, and every algebraic step was confirmed symbolically] This is the upper bound in the campaign answer to Problem 3.3 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A probability measure is unimodal if, for some mode m, it is an atom at m plus an absolutely continuous measure whose density is nondecreasing to the left of m and nonincreasing to the right. Write boxplus for additive free convolution. For t>0 let S(0,t) be the centered semicircle law of variance t, with density sqrt(4t-x^2)/(2pi t) on |x|<=2sqrt(t). Let mu be compactly supported with positive diameter D=sup{|x-y|: x,y in supp(mu)}. Then mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=D^2. Proof route: by the source's Lemma 3.1 (Biane's description), non-unimodality at time t gives some R>0 and a separating local minimum u_0 of xi_R with xi_R(u_0)<=1/t. The stationary-kernel lower bound, rescaled to diameter D, gives xi_R(u_0)>=1/D^2, so t<=D^2. At t=D^2, equality would hold in that lower bound. This forces mu to be the symmetric two-point law with atoms at u_0±D/2 and R^2=3D^2/4, which is unimodal at t=D^2 by the source's Example 2.1. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

solution $(v,B, p)$ of \eqref{eq:mhd} on $[0,T_*]\times\Rn$ with data

 p=\Riesz_i\Riesz_j
 \big(v^iv^j-\Binf^ib^j-b^i\Binf^j-b^ib^j\big),
\]
where $\Riesz_i$ are the Euclidean Riesz transforms;
\item writing $X=\mathrm{id}+w$, the solution is carried by a Lagrangian flow
$X:[0,T_*]\times\Rn\to\Rn$ with $X(0,\cdot)=\mathrm{id}$, uniformly bi-Lipschitz
and volume-preserving, $\det dX\equiv1$, such that $v=(\partial_tX)\circ X^{-1}$ and

moreover there is a spatially exact spacetime field
$\Ufield\in H^{s-1,1}_{\breg}(\Rst)$ such that
$\Ufield=dw$ on $[0,T_*]\times\Rn$ and, for constants fixed by

the constant of the linear estimate \eqref{eq:linear}),
\begin{equation}
 \|\Ufield\|_{H^{s-1,1}_{\breg}}

 \sup_{t\in[0,T_*]}\|dw(t)\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}\le\delta;

here $\delta$ is chosen so that the second bound implies

conserved on $[0,T_*]$;

initial data for which $v$ and $B-\Binf$ belong to

{"assumptions":["m a positive integer","The exact real symmetric 3-by-3 matrix family displayed above","Frobenius metric for the full Gram matrix; scalar Schur complement in its last coordinate","No identification of m with a realizable network depth"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T17:46:43.579570+00:00","domain":"probability and Gaussian conditioning","id":"claim_0d0af2cc485fae31c86ec03a77b28a1438b145446a35de781b46983c6a934c15","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"PROOF (UNAUDITED); elementary matrix example, no novelty claimed. For every integer m>=1, let rho=1-m^(-2), Y=[[1,rho],[rho,1]], b(t)=(1/(2m)+t)(1,-1)^T, and G(t)=[[Y,b(t)],[b(t)^T,1]], for 0<=t<=1/(8m). Every G(t) is positive definite of rank 3 with unit diagonal. {"assumptions":["transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator with a finite fixed-point set","the object asked for is a periodic ITINERARY, a symbol sequence, not a periodic orbit","m = 3 for the affirmative half; the m = 4 case is open"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_0d1240b9b017496fe1d07198e8276e9848accae193a3447d35c49891e4cf5c60","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: unreviewed - author-checked against the source's exact wording; verification unreviewed] For a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator the ITINERARY of a trajectory is the sequence of fixed-point neighbourhoods it visits; Rozikov (2009, p. 4) asks whether some trajectory has a periodic itinerary. CLAIM, in two halves. (i) YES at m = 3, by an example already in the literature: for the cyclic Volterra operator with a = b = c = 1, matrix A = [[0,1,-1],[-1,0,1],[1,-1,0]], whose leading 2x2 minor is 1 so the operator is transversal and whose fixed-point set - the three vertices and the centre - is finite, the itinerary of every non-fixed interior point is periodic, 1 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> ..., with sojourns 12, 51, 1073, ... growing geometrically by the heteroclinic-cycle mechanism of Ganikhodzhaev and Zanin (2004). (ii) OPEN at m = 4: in the proof of Theorem 5 of Ganikhodjaev and Zanin (arXiv:1205.3841) the trajectory passes between the epsilon-neighbourhoods of the vertices along the routes 1-4-3-2-1, 1-4-2-1 or 1-4-3-1, and a simulated cyclic-type m = 4 map produced the mixed finite prefix 1,4,3,2,1,4,2,1. A finite prefix cannot show that an itinerary is not periodic (every finite word extends to a periodic one), and one trajectory cannot answer an existence question in the negative, so the m = 4 case is not settled here. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:09.850320+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0d13ae038fd9406c6117e2c0470b7b3883dd66014b46ac803d003bab28e95a0c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 1 (Log-concavity, PF$_2$, and TP$_2$) of arXiv:2605.18751, '\mytitle'] A positive function \(a:J\to(0,\infty)\) on an interval \(J\subseteq E\) is \emph{log-concave} if \(\log a\) is concave on \(J\). In the discrete case this is equivalent to \(\Delta^2\log a(k)\le0\) for every admissible \(k\in J\) and in the continuous case it is equivalent to \((\log a)''(x)\le0\) wherever the second derivative exists.

For a sequence \(b=(b_k)_{k\in\Z}\), we say that \(b\) is a \emph{P\'olya frequency sequence of order 2} (PF$_2$) if \(b_k\ge0\) for all \(k\), the support \(\{k:b_k>0\}\) is an interval in \(\Z\), and \(b\) is log-concave on its support.  A probability distribution \(F\) on \(\N_0\) is PF$_2$ if its mass sequence, extended by zero outside its support, is PF$_2$.

A nonnegative kernel \(M:I\times J\to[0,\infty)\) on two totally ordered sets is \emph{totally positive of order 2} (TP$_2$) if
\[
M(i,j)M(i',j')\ge M(i,j')M(i',j)
\]
whenever \(i\le i'\) and \(j\le j'\). See~\cite{Karlin1968} for the general total positivity theory.","status":"unverified"}

Facts: (1) the minimal polynomial of zeta_n over Q is the n-th cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(x) = prod over 1 <= k <= n with gcd(k, n) = 1 of (x - zeta_n^k), which has integer coefficients and is irreducible over Q (Gauss for n prime, Kronecker/Dedekind in general), so [Q(zeta_n) : Q] = phi(n), Euler's totient; (2) Q(zeta_n)/Q is a Galois extension with Galois group canonically isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^*, the automorphism sigma_a sending zeta_n to zeta_n^a; in particular it is abelian, and by the Kronecker-Weber theorem every finite abelian extension of Q lies in some cyclotomic field; (3) the ring of integers of Q(zeta_n) is Z[zeta_n]; (4) a prime p not dividing n is unramified and splits into phi(n)/f primes of residue degree f, where f is the order of p in (Z/nZ)^*; a prime p dividing n ramifies, totally so in Q(zeta_{p^k}) where p is the phi(p^k)-th power of a prime, and p O_K = (1 - zeta_{p^k})^{phi(p^k)}; the discriminant of Q(zeta_{p^k}) is +- p^{p^{k-1}(pk - k - 1)}, and in general the primes ramified in Q(zeta_n) are exactly the primes dividing n (for odd n; 2 ramifies only when 4 divides n); (5) Q(zeta_n) contains the quadratic field Q(sqrt(p^*)) with p^* = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p for each odd prime p dividing n (Gauss sums), which is one route to quadratic reciprocity; (6) the maximal real subfield is Q(zeta_n + zeta_n^{-1}) of degree phi(n)/2 for n > 2; (7) the class number h_n of Q(zeta_p) is 1 exactly for the primes p <= 19; Kummer proved Fermat's last theorem for regular primes (p not dividing h_p) using the arithmetic of Z[zeta_p].         e^{-t} \, dt\\
      &= \underbrace{\left. \left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^m \left(-e^{-t}\right)
          \right|^{t=\infty}_{t=0}}_0\\
      &\quad + \int_0^\infty m\left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^{m-1} \left(\frac{x}{m} \, e^{xt/m}\right)
      e^{-t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m\left(x/m\right)}{1} \int_0^\infty \left(e^{xt/m}-1\right)^{m-1}
            e^{-(1-x/m)t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m \left(m-1\right) (x/m)^2}{1-x/m} \int_0^\infty \left( e^{xt/m}-1\right)^{m-2}
            e^{-(1-2x/m)t} \, dt\\
      &\ \,\vdots\\
      &= \frac{m!\left(x/m\right)}{\left(m/x - 1\right)^{\underline{m-1}}} 
            \int_0^\infty e^{-(1-x)t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m!}{\left(m/x-1\right)^{\underline{m}}} = \binom{m/x - 1}{m}^{-1},
      \quad 0 < x < 1.
    \end{align*}
    The right-hand side is a rational function of $x$, say
    $f(x) / g(x)$ where $f(z)$ and $g(z)$ are real polynomials in $z$.
    Then $f(z) \, g(z)^{-1}$ is a well-defined object in the ring 
    of formal power series $\mathbb{R}[[z]]$ and we can
    restate our result for $\phi_H(z)$;
    see Section~\ref{language}.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:54:57.568626+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0db0898f2916195f042f88ecc11d3171ae1c4b8f02152a2dfd052c928461981f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:hypLP of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields and associated function space'] \begin{itemize}

\[

and the rows and columns are ordered by any linear extension of

\[
 G_\lambda(p_\lambda)

In particular,
\[
 D_m:=\det E_m\in R_{\mathrm{ev}}\setminus\{0\}

is a Laurent unit times a product of cyclotomic polynomials, and
\[

 \in\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathscr P_m}(R_{\mathrm{ev}}).
\]

If $F=\sum_\lambda b_\lambda G_\lambda\in

\[
 \mathbf v_m(F)=\bigl(F(p_\mu)\bigr)_{\mu\in\mathscr P_m},
 \qquad

\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf v_m(F)=E_m\mathbf b_m(F).
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every ideal $J\subseteq R_{\mathrm{ev}}$,
\[
 F(p_\mu)\in J\quad(\mu\in\mathscr P_m)

{"assumptions":["H and K are complex Banach spaces","A and B are BOUNDED linear operators on H and K respectively","sigma(A) and sigma(B) are disjoint compact subsets of C","C is a bounded operator from K to H","Gamma is a cycle in the resolvent set of B winding once around sigma(A) and not at all around sigma(B)"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.091249+00:00","domain":"operator theory, Sylvester equations, Riesz functional calculus","id":"claim_0ddcfb960219b5d37190ff5731d811c9cbc7554da88e7737e484070a46e2973a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"CAUTION ON THE NAME: this is the other result commonly called 'Rosenblum's argument' - the contour-integral solution of the Sylvester equation; the scattering-theory Hilbert-Schmidt estimate is a different theorem of the same author, so a citation naming Rosenblum must be matched to its context. STATEMENT: let H and K be complex Banach spaces, A a bounded operator on H, B a bounded operator on K, and suppose their spectra are disjoint: sigma(A) intersect sigma(B) is empty. Then for every bounded operator C from K to H the equation A X - X B = C has a UNIQUE bounded solution X from K to H, and it is given by X = (1 / (2 pi i)) times the contour integral over Gamma of (A - z)^(-1) C (B - z)^(-1) dz, where Gamma is a finite union of positively oriented rectifiable Jordan curves lying in the resolvent set of B, encircling sigma(A) once and sigma(B) not at all. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) disjointness of the spectra is what gives both existence and uniqueness. With A = B and C = 0 the equation A X - X A = 0 is solved by every operator commuting with A, so uniqueness fails badly; and with A = B = 0 on a one-dimensional space the equation is unsolvable for nonzero C. (ii) It is the SPECTRA, not the norms, that matter: no smallness of C is assumed, the solution depends linearly on C, and the bound on X is controlled by the length of Gamma and by the size of the two resolvents on Gamma - a bound that blows up as the spectra approach each other, which is the quantitative content usually needed in perturbation arguments. (iii) The theorem as stated is for BOUNDED A and B; for unbounded operators the analogous statement requires separate hypotheses (sectoriality, semigroup generation), and the contour formula must be justified anew. (iv) Finite-dimensional corollary: for matrices, A X - X B = C is uniquely solvable precisely when A and B have no common eigenvalue.","status":"unverified"}

# Target 1: two-cycle exclusion and necessary overshoot for periodic GD

Version 1, proof unaudited. This excludes possible third fates; it does not
classify all factored-GD trajectories or prove convergence.

Consider the factored model of claim 010 with any eta>0. More generally the
argument applies to any real update
 v_+=v+eta F(v,kq),
 k_+=k+delta q, q_+=q+delta k,
 delta=eta v G(v,kq),
where G is strictly positive at every finite point and F(0,s) has a unique
zero p_bar. The softmax logistic model satisfies these conditions.

1. Every orbit of period dividing two with k^2-q^2!=0 is a fixed point.
   It lies on v=0,kq=p_bar. This holds at every fixed step size.
2. Every nonstationary finite periodic orbit with k^2-q^2!=0 at one (hence
   every) iterate must contain an iterate with delta^2>=2. Equivalently,
   any periodic orbit on which |eta vG|<sqrt(2) throughout is stationary.

Neither statement excludes balanced-plane cycles, long cycles with large
overshoot, unbounded nonconvergent orbits, or nonperiodic bounded invariant
sets. This is a special obstruction result, not a scored global classification.

## Proof of two-cycle exclusion

Let U=k+q and D=k-q. Their exact simultaneous updates are
 U_+=(1+delta)U, D_+=(1-delta)D.
The nonzero imbalance is C=UD, so U,D are both nonzero initially.
For a returning two-step orbit, with a=delta_0,b=delta_1,
 (1+a)(1+b)=1, (1-a)(1-b)=1.
Expansion and addition yield 2ab=0; subtraction yields 2(a+b)=0.
Over the reals this forces a=b=0. Since eta>0 and G>0, v_0=v_1=0.
The factors therefore do not move. The head update then forces
F(0,kq)=0, hence kq=p_bar. This is a fixed point, as claimed.

## Proof of the overshoot requirement

The exact imbalance update is C_+=(1-delta^2)C. If an r-step orbit returns
with C_0!=0, no intermediate C can vanish, and
 product_{t=0}^{r-1}(1-delta_t^2)=1.
If every delta_t^2<2, every absolute factor is <=1, strictly less than 1
whenever delta_t!=0. The product can have absolute value 1 only if every
delta_t=0. Then every v_t=0, the factors stay fixed, and F(0,kq)=0.
Thus any nonstationary periodic orbit requires at least one delta_t^2>=2.

## Relation to the remaining gap

The flow's invariant imbalance is unavailable in GD, but its multiplicative
replacement still excludes every nonbalanced two-cycle, including at steps
beyond the normal-stability threshold of claim 013. A loss of an attracting
normal multiplier therefore does not by itself provide a two-cycle witness.
The unresolved step is controlling general, possibly large factor updates
well enough to show eventual entry into one of claim 010's escaping regions,
or finding a third fate that persists off the balanced planes.


# Target 1: exact balanced two-cycle and its transverse multiplier

Version 1, proof unaudited. Boundary check for claim 014, not a positive-volume
counterexample to an almost-everywhere theorem.

Fix any n>=2 and any distinct positive kappa_i. Put
 b_i=2 cosh(kappa_i)^2/kappa_i,
 a_i=b_i tanh(kappa_i).
These satisfy 0<a_i<b_i. In the usual coupled factored model
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), all links have
 h_i(-1)=0, h_i'(-1)=2.

For EVERY fixed eta>0, simultaneous Euclidean GD on the average logistic
loss has an exact two-cycle
 (v,k,q)=(2/eta,1,-1) <-> (2/eta,-1,1).
At both points the loss is log 2, the product is -1, and k^2-q^2=0.
The two-step Jacobian has a transverse multiplier 9 normal to k=-q.
Thus the nonzero-imbalance assumption in 014 is necessary. This cycle
does not establish a positive-measure basin or rule out almost-everywhere
endpoint convergence.

## Proof

At either displayed state every h_i(kq)=0, so g_i=1/2, F=0 and
G=mean_i g_i h_i'=1. The head therefore stays fixed and
delta=eta vG=2. The factor update sends
 (k,q)->(k+2q,q+2k).
It exchanges (1,-1) and (-1,1). The cycle is nonstationary and has exact
period two; the loss remains log(1+exp(0))=log 2. The construction uses
different nonlinear scales, rather than requiring repeated identical examples.

The full factor-sum identity is U_+=(1+delta)U, U=k+q. At U=0 its
linearization gives dU_+=(1+delta)dU=3dU; the term U d(delta) vanishes.
After two steps dU_{++}=9dU, an exact normal multiplier even when v and
the product vary in the perturbation. No stability assertion at a unit
multiplier is involved.

The same constructed family has finite stationary points at v=0,kq=-1,
whereas the displayed periodic points have v=2/eta>0. Hence a classification
of every finite initialization by stationary points and escaping selections
alone would be false at any positive constant step. The exceptional balanced
plane must be allowed, as it is in claim 012's flow statement (which is a
different dynamical system).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["rows independent and identically distributed (the pairs bootstrap resamples rows, not residuals, so heteroscedasticity is allowed)","finite fourth moments and a converging empirical second-moment matrix (Freedman 1981); the predictor is a fixed measurable map of the sample, applied identically to every resample"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T12:03:52.456149+00:00","domain":"regression / resampling","id":"claim_0e4e01deefe6a25c51c622bfa99085bafd98403f8cc1a516a140a42803b61b73","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a least-squares predictor yhat(x) = x' beta_hat fitted on n rows, the textbook variance at a new point x is sigma^2 x'(X'SX)^(-1) x (sigma^2 times the leverage), and the hat matrix H = X(X'SX)^(-1)X'S has trace equal to the number of parameters. Both statements require X'SX to be invertible. On a design that is rank-deficient - here, an ensemble whose members include exact duplicates, so the member-prediction Gram of every output is singular by the number of duplicates - the leverage is undefined: the trace of the hat matrix drops to the rank (21 instead of 24 on the s104 Y1 cell of the EMIT pool), and inverting through a tiny ridge assigns any new point that leaves the duplicates' span an arbitrarily large leverage (a load 11.8 times the whole prediction error on that cell), which is a property of the ridge, not of the predictor actually used. The pairs bootstrap sidesteps this: resample the n rows with replacement B times, refit the predictor exactly as it is fitted in production (with its own ridge or pseudo-inverse and its own constraints), and take the empirical variance of the B predictions at x. Under Freedman's (1981) conditions for the pairs (correlation-model) bootstrap - independent rows, finite fourth moments of the regressors and errors, and a design whose empirical second-moment matrix converges - the bootstrap variance of a linear predictor is consistent for its sampling variance, and it remains well defined on a singular design because every resample is fitted by the same regularised map as the original. It is the right variance estimator when the estimator's regularisation, rather than an invertible Gram, determines its behaviour; it also applies unchanged to a constrained estimator (a long-only stack) for which no closed form exists. Cost: B refits per cell; B = 8 was enough to rank rows and cells in the RMT ensemble program (the ranking, not the level, was used).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Finite public Gaussian family with common positive spherical variance; d>=1","Finite prescribed set of nonnegative OU time-point pairs; epsilon>0","No prescribed Lipschitz constant, gradient constraint, or OU-consistency assumption for estimated fields","Adaptive application assumes identical public input, uniform finite query cap, and a finite selected set of query-randomness seeds","Finite-seed masking does not establish continuously randomized query hardness"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T17:55:25.688168+00:00","domain":"diffusion score-oracle models and adaptive query lower bounds","id":"claim_0e651190fbfa6f03b770cb3ff6afd9c955530ace92f76294c324253c623d80f8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; C18 v1 status SKETCH, independent audit pending, no novelty claim; not a certified theorem. Proposed diagnostic: for a finite public Gaussian family N(mu_theta,v0 I_d), d>=1 and v0>0, every finite set of OU time-point pairs (t_j,x_j), t_j>=0, and epsilon>0 admit instance-specific jointly smooth estimated fields b_theta equal to zero on those pairs with E_{OU_t(P_theta)} ||b_theta-s_theta,t||^2 <= epsilon^2 for every t>=0. Each field has some finite global spatial Lipschitz constant uniform over t; no prescribed, polynomial, or efficient-computability bound is supplied. Construction: choose smooth time bumps h_j and small spatial bumps g_j, set chi=1-product_j(1-h_j g_j), and b_theta=(1-chi)s_theta. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-06T07:26:44.650115+00:00","domain":"matrix analysis, Schatten norms and singular values","id":"claim_0eb30ff7577661040f84ccd987fc3f1b12ba0d9cd878123591ce0282549634d9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a complex m by n matrix A, s_1(A) >= s_2(A) >= ... >= 0 are its singular values (padded with zeros to min(m, n) entries). For 1 <= p < infinity the Schatten p-norm is ||A||_{S_p} = (sum_i s_i(A)^p)^(1/p), and ||A||_{S_infinity} = s_1(A), the spectral norm. Zero singular values do not change the value. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:47.651197+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ecba4327d83e6bcf5f0e9ab526d9f8854fb6f5e939a15167f6eb56dad9c0344","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 1 of arXiv:2605.07050, 'Universality of the fluctuations of the free energy in generalized Sherrington--Kirkpatric'] Suppose that $\sqrt{N} W_{ij}$ $(1 \leq i<j \leq N)$ are i.i.d., symmetric, and strictly sub-Gaussian random variables with variance $1$. Suppose that $\sqrt{N} x_k$ $(1 \leq k \leq N)$ are i.i.d., symmetric, and strictly sub-Gaussian random variables with variance $1$, independent of $\sqrt{N} W_{ij}$. Let
\beq 
	Z_N \equiv Z_N(\beta) = \E_{\caX} \left[ \exp \left( \beta N \sum_{i<j} W_{ij} \frac{x_i x_j}{\| \bsx \|^2} \right) \right], \qquad F_N \equiv F_N(\beta) = \frac{1}{N} \log Z_N.
\eeq
(When $\| \bsx \| = 0$, we define $x_i x_j / \| \bsx \|^2 = 0$ for all $i, j$.) Then, for any $\beta \in (0, 1)$,
\[
	F_N(\beta) \to F(\beta) := \beta^2 /4
\]
and
\[
	N(F_N(\beta) - F(\beta) ) \Rightarrow \caN(m_F, V_F),
\]
as $N \to \infty$, i.e., $N(F_N(\beta) - F(\beta) )$ converges in distribution to the Gaussian with mean $m_F$ and the variance $V_F$ as $N \to \infty$. Here,
\[
	m_F = \frac{1}{4} \log (1- \beta^2) + \frac{\beta^2 (1-m_4)}{4} + \frac{\beta^4 (w_4-3)(m_4^2 -3)}{48}
\]
and
\[
	V_F = -\frac{1}{2} \left( \log (1- \beta^2) + \beta^2 - \frac{\beta^4 (w_4-3)}{4} \right),
\]
where we let $w_4 = N^2 \E[W_{ij}^4]$ and $m_4 = N^2 \E [x_1^4]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:31:20.617754+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ecea1fce8c4e2cec4a6817b7844a061b379885829e70a321e5265f3f096c679","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $G_1,G_2$ be locally compact Hausdorff groups and $f$ a map from $G_1$ to $G_2$.
    Consider that $G_1$ and $G_2$ are equipped with LR-coarse structure.
    Then the following six assertions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a continuous group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is controlled.
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a continuous anti-group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is controlled.
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a topological closed embedding group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is coarse. 
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a topological closed embedding anti-group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is coarse. 
        \item Assume that  $f$ is an isomorphism of topological groups. Then $f$ is a coarse equivalence. 
        \item Assume that  $f$ is an anti-isomorphism of topological groups. Then $f$ is a coarse equivalence. 
    \end{enumerate}
    In particular, for a group and its closed subgroup, the inclusion map is coarse. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Hall's condition is that for any subset of sets from the collection, the total unique elements they contain is at least as large as the number of sets in the subset. Let $(X,\mathrm{d},\mathcal{H}^n)$ be an $\mathrm{RCD}(-1,n)$ metric measure space, and let $1\leqslant k\leqslant n$. Let $\delta>0$, $r>0$. We say that $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_k):B_r(x)\to \mathbb R^k$ is a {\rm $\delta$-splitting map} if there is a constant $C=C(n)$ such that the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $u_i$ is harmonic on $B_r(x)$ for every $i=1,\ldots,k$.
        \item $|\nabla u_i|\leqslant C$ for every $i=1,\ldots,k$.
        \item We have, for every $i,j=1,\ldots,k$,
        \[
        \fint_{B_r(x)} |\nabla u_i\cdot \nabla u_j-\delta_{ij}|\ensuremath{\mathrm d}\mathcal{H}^n \leqslant \delta.
        \]
        \item We have, for every $i=1,\ldots,k$ 
        \[
        r^2\fint_{B_r(x)} |\operatorname{Hess} u_i|^2\ensuremath{\mathrm d}\mathcal{H}^n \leqslant \delta
        \]
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:10:05.696938+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0f62a485064f4ddc5c8aea041a707695acf30404e3840c5841e402fe175692dd","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] Let $N,d\geq1$ and  $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \R^d$.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)] $0 \notin \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$ if and only if
        there is $v \in \R^d$ with $\langle q_m, v \rangle > 0$ for all
        $m$.
        \item[(ii)] $0 \in \Int \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$ if and only if
        there is \emph{no} $v \neq 0$ with $\langle q_m, v \rangle \ge
        0$ for all $m$.
        \item[(iii)] If $q_1, \dots, q_N$ are in general linear position, then
        either $0 \notin \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$ or $0 \in \Int
        \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$.
        \item[(iv)] Let $N \ge d+1$ and $0 \in \partial \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$.
        If there is exactly one $d$-element set $I\subseteq [N]$ such that
        the vectors $(q_i)_{i \in I}$ are linearly dependent, then the points $q_i$, $i \in I$,
        are affinely independent,
        $0 \in \relint \Conv(q_i : i \in I)$, and there is a unique unit
        vector $\nu$ such that $$\langle q_i, \nu \rangle = 0 \text{ for } i \in I
        \quad
        \text{and}
        \quad
        \langle q_m, \nu \rangle > 0 \text{ for }\, m \notin I.$$

    \end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

For a two-sided nearest-neighbor iid walk with p in [1/2,1], q=1-p, independent iid fair sign scenery, and n>=4, prescribe Y_t=+1 at t=0 or 1 mod4 and -1 at t=2 or 3 mod4 for 0<|t|<=n; the t=0 color is NOT observed. Put A_n=p^(2n)+q^(2n) and D_n=16[p^(2n-2)q^2+q^(2n-2)p^2]. Then P(C0=+1 | this exterior)=A_n/(2A_n+D_n). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:55:27.265312+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0f8096492788892d5587c57e7fb8200627e06850fb3fd50cf9e2750d9523e4bc","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition AvoidBB of arXiv:2410.23899, 'Tightness for interlacing geometric random walk bridges'] Fix $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in W_k^{\circ}$, $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and $f: [a,b] \rightarrow (-\infty, \infty]$ and $g: [-\infty, \infty)$ be two continuous functions. The latter means that either $f: [a,b] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is continuous or $f = \infty$ everywhere and similarly for $g$. We also assume that $f(t) > g(t)$ for all $t \in [a,b]$, $f(a) > x_1$, $f(b) > y_1$, $g(a) < x_k$ and $g(b) < y_k$. 

With the above data we define the $(f,g)$-avoiding Brownian line ensemble on the interval $[a,b]$ with entrance data $\vec{x}$ and exit data $\vec{y}$ to be the $\llbracket 1 , k \rrbracket$-indexed line ensemble $\mathcal{Q}$ on $\Lambda = [a,b]$ whose law is the same as that of $\{B_i\}_{i = 1}^k$ (with law $\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{free}}^{a,b, \vec{x}, \vec{y}}$), conditioned on the event
$$E = \{f(r) > B_1(r) > B_2(r) > \cdots > B_k(r) > g(r) \mbox{ for all $r \in [a,b]$} \}.$$
We denote the law of $\mathcal{Q}$ by $\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x},\vec{y},f,g}$, and expectations with respect to this measure by $\mathbb{E}_{\operatorname{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x},\vec{y},f,g}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["each F_n nondecreasing, right-continuous, with values in [0,1]","no tightness is assumed, and without it the limit can be defective"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.752559+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0fba1416669badf1de8ab735445eeb6c5d50526da69885c6f0c2f43871a867fd","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (F_n) be a sequence of distribution functions on R, that is nondecreasing right-continuous functions with values in [0,1]. Then there exist a subsequence (F_{n_k}) and a nondecreasing right-continuous F : R -> [0,1] such that F_{n_k}(x) -> F(x) at every continuity point x of F. The limit F need NOT be a distribution function: mass can escape to plus or minus infinity, and with F_n the distribution function of the point mass at n one gets F identically 0. This is exactly the gap that tightness closes: the family is tight, meaning sup_n (1 - F_n(M) + F_n(-M)) -> 0 as M -> infinity, if and only if every such subsequential limit is a proper distribution function, which is Prokhorov's theorem on R. Nothing is assumed about the F_n beyond monotonicity, right-continuity and the range [0,1] - no continuity, no tightness, no common support. [standard; e.g. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 3.2.6]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:15:45.375658+00:00","domain":"general topology","id":"claim_0fc6ca3efccfbfb81740d50ff4b42e6d92b545e1d6116f465b8a720d7d0ba797","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"A topological space X is compact if every open cover of X has a finite subcover: whenever X is the union of a family of open sets {U_i : i in I}, there are finitely many indices i_1, ..., i_n such that X is the union of U_(i_1), ..., U_(i_n). A subset K of a space is compact if it is compact in the subspace topology; equivalently, every cover of K by sets open in the ambient space admits a finite subfamily covering K. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:41:28.175431+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0fe92c2c3a66065cf6b5bdef344e3592858a429adda497c795705a803f8618aa","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition $(r-2)_*$-BP of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $T$ be a $K_r$-tree
and $S\subset V(T)$ a set of {\it seeds}, 
which we consider to be initially {\it infected}. 
Then, in each step of the process, either 
\begin{itemize}
\item {\it (usual step)} some vertex $v$ with at least $r-2$ 
infected neighbors becomes infected; or else
\item {\it (special step)} if no such $v$ exists, but 
for some internal edge $e$, there are two cliques $H_i\neq H_j$ 
containing $e$ such that $H_i$ has $r-4$ infected vertices 
and $H_j$ has $1$ infected vertex,  
and all $r-3$ of these vertices are not in $e$, 
then  we infect an arbitrarily chosen vertex $u\in e$; and 
otherwise, 
\item {\it (terminal step)} if neither type of step is possible, 
then the process terminates. 
\end{itemize}
We call this process {\it $(r-2)_*$-BP} 
on $T$, 
and let $\langle S;T\rangle_*$ denote the set of 
eventually infected vertices in $T$ started with 
the seed set $S$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:37:33.910787+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_102666e82e9e76f7e09da78626d9abe77aa7299d69a63249634afccb3ce8a949","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"The spiked covariance model (Johnstone, 2001) is the family of $p \\times p$ population covariance matrices $\\Sigma = \\sigma^2 (I_p + \\sum_{k=1}^{r} \\theta_k u_k u_k^T)$ with orthonormal vectors $u_1, \\dots, u_r$, spike sizes $\\theta_1 \\ge \\dots \\ge \\theta_r > 0$, and a fixed rank $r$ that does not grow with $p$. The data are $n$ independent rows $x_i \\in \\mathbb{R}^p$ with covariance $\\Sigma$ (Gaussian in the sharpest results; finite fourth moments suffice for the eigenvalue statements), and the object studied is the sample covariance $S = \\frac{1}{n} \\sum_i x_i x_i^T$ in the proportional regime $p, n \\to \\infty$ with $p/n \\to \\gamma \\in (0, \\infty)$. All but $r$ population eigenvalues equal the noise level $\\sigma^2$ (the bulk); the model asks which spikes are visible in $S$ and how far the sample eigenvalues and eigenvectors are from the population ones. With $\\theta_k = 0$ for all $k$ the sample spectrum follows the Marchenko-Pastur law with ratio $\\gamma$ and variance $\\sigma^2$, whose support is $[\\sigma^2 (1 - \\sqrt{\\gamma})^2, \\sigma^2 (1 + \\sqrt{\\gamma})^2]$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.544132+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_102b0c94f0a077a9bc16e235659cb9aebd39afc61d193efcf1bc836f9ab10399","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 33 (Monotonicity of the edges) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix a finite graph $G$ and some $\beta\in[0,\infty)$.
    Let $E'\subset E$ and $uv\in E\setminus E'$.

    For any $\tau'=(\alpha',\omega',\eta')\in\Pi_{G'}$, write
    $\mu^{\omega_{uv}}_{\tau'}$ and $\mu^{\eta_{uv}}_{\tau'}$ for the laws of $\omega_{uv}$ and $\eta_{uv}$ in the conditional measure
    \(
        \mu_{G,\beta}[\blank|\{\tau|_{G'}=\tau'\}]
    \).
    Then
    \[
        \tau'\preceq\tau''
        \qquad
        \implies
        \qquad
        (
        \mu_{\tau''}^{\omega_{uv}}\leqstoch\mu_{\tau'}^{\omega_{uv}}
        \quad\text{and}\quad
        \mu_{\tau'}^{\eta_{uv}}\leqstoch\mu_{\tau''}^{\eta_{uv}}

Moreover, $\mu^{\omega_{uv}}_{\tau'}$ only depends on the values of $\alpha_u$, $\alpha_v$,

{"assumptions":["U and V are open subsets of R^n of the same dimension n","phi : U -> V is a bijection, continuously differentiable, with continuously differentiable inverse (equivalently injective C^1 with nonvanishing Jacobian determinant and image V)","Lebesgue measure and Lebesgue measurable functions are used on both sides","f is measurable and either nonnegative or integrable"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090563+00:00","domain":"real analysis, measure theory, integration in R^n","id":"claim_1047e7e34c38c2168c64f635d6e025f096e2d64b3ad9dc9fbd5d8a3856bb2cb5","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let U and V be open subsets of R^n and let phi : U -> V be a C^1 DIFFEOMORPHISM: phi is a bijection of U onto V, phi is continuously differentiable, and its inverse is continuously differentiable. (By the inverse function theorem it is equivalent to assume phi is injective, C^1, onto V, with det Dphi(x) nonzero for every x in U.) Let Dphi(x) denote the Jacobian matrix. Then for every Lebesgue measurable f : V -> [0, +infinity], the integral of f(y) dy over V equals the integral of f(phi(x)) |det Dphi(x)| dx over U, both sides being simultaneously finite or infinite; the same identity holds for complex-valued f, with f integrable over V if and only if (f composed with phi) times |det Dphi| is integrable over U. Taking f an indicator gives the measure statement: the Lebesgue measure of phi(E) equals the integral of |det Dphi| over E, for every measurable E contained in U. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the determinant is required. The density is |det Dphi|; the sign records orientation and belongs to the theory of differential forms, not to Lebesgue integration. (ii) Injectivity cannot be dropped without paying for multiplicity: for a general C^1 map the correct statement is the area formula, the integral of f(phi(x)) |det Dphi(x)| dx over U equals the integral over V of f(y) N(y) dy, where N(y) is the number of preimages of y in U; N identically 1 is exactly injectivity. (iii) Smoothness cannot be relaxed to 'differentiable almost everywhere'. One needs the Luzin (N) property, that null sets map to null sets, which C^1 and Lipschitz maps have: in dimension one the Cantor function is continuous and nondecreasing with derivative 0 almost everywhere, yet it maps a null set onto a set of measure 1, and the naive substitution formula is false for it. (iv) The hypothesis is a diffeomorphism between OPEN sets; for maps defined on closed or lower-dimensional sets the statement must be routed through the area or coarea formula.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:41:28.165285+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_10481ef2ca34f8c3e5d918c755a8fb020f38f279aafadc53589ce33814706e5b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Order of TWGs of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] The {\it order} $\vartheta(T)$ of a TWG 
$T$ for $e$ is defined inductively. 
If $T$ consists of a single edge then $\vartheta(T)=0$, otherwise
\[
\vartheta(T)
=1+\sum_{f\in E(H^{(e)}\setminus e)}\vartheta(T_f),
\]
where $H^{(e)}$ is the root of $T$.
If $\vartheta(T)=k$, then we call $T$ a {\it $k$-TWG}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.840473+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1058192005b327e28fcdebe84783f3b749482fd64fc92d01bddef62c5a66ea64","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 (Gaussian tail and conditional excess limit) of arXiv:2607.20714, 'High Minima of Gaussian Processes: Overshoots and Minimizer Locations'] Let $\boldsymbol X$ be a centred Gaussian vector in $\mathbb R^n$ with
positive definite covariance matrix $\Sigma$, and let $\boldsymbol p$ be
the minimizer of the following problem:
\[
 \sigma_*^2=\min_{\boldsymbol v\geq0,
             \,\boldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol v=1}
             \boldsymbol v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma\boldsymbol v.
\]
Put
\[
 I=\{i:p_i>0\},\qquad J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus I,
 \qquad  
 \qquad \boldsymbol\theta=\Sigma_{II}^{-1}\boldsymbol1_I.
\]
Then
\[
 \boldsymbol\theta=\frac{\boldsymbol p_I}{\sigma_*^2}>0,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol r_J=\Sigma_{JI}\Sigma_{II}^{-1}\boldsymbol1_I\geq\boldsymbol1_J,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol1_I^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\theta=\frac1{\sigma_*^2}.
\]
Write $r_j$ for the $j$th component of $\boldsymbol r_J$.
Let
\[
 P=\{j\in J:r_j=1\},\qquad N=\{j\in J:r_j>1\},
\]
and let $G_P$ be centred Gaussian with covariance matrix
\[
 \Gamma_P=\Sigma_{PP}-\Sigma_{PI}\Sigma_{II}^{-1}\Sigma_{IP}.
\]
Set $c_P=\Pp\{G_P>0\}$, with $c_P=1$ when $P$ is empty.  If
$M=\min_{1\leq i\leq n}X_i$, then, as $u\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \Pp\{M>u\}\sim
 \frac{c_P}{(2\pi)^{|I|/2}\det(\Sigma_{II})^{1/2}
                  \prod_{i\in I}\theta_i}
 u^{-|I|}\exp\left\{-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma_*^2}\right\}.
 
\end{equation}
Let $(\xi_i)_{i\geq1}$ be independent unit exponential random variables.
If $P$ is nonempty, let $G_P^+$ have law
$\mathcal L(G_P\mid G_P>0)$ and be independent of $(\xi_i)_{i\geq1}$.
Furthermore, as $u\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal L\left(
 \left(
   (u(X_i-u))_{i\in I},
   (X_j-u)_{j\in P},
   \frac{\boldsymbol X_N}{u}
 \right)
   \ \middle|\ M>u\right)
 \Longrightarrow
 \mathcal L\left(
   (\xi_i/\theta_i)_{i\in I},
   G_P^+,
   \boldsymbol r_N
 \right).
 
\end{equation}
The $G_P^+$ and $\boldsymbol r_N$ blocks are omitted
when $P$ and $N$, respectively, are empty. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.199654+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1071a2338358110494cec48ce2da366826450939e1b46a3f99b8559e9fb42441","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 133 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $t\notin \oJ$ (recall Lemma~\ref{l:bad.J}) and parameters as in \eqref{eq:order-of-limits}: 
    \[\bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    \leq  
    o_{\trK}(1)
    \]
for $ \trrr_t\equiv \trrr(t,X^\plus(t))$. 

\begin{proof}
Let $\bar{P}(t)$ be the temporal smoothing of $tp'(t)$. Then for $t\notin\bar{J}$ we have
	\[
    \bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    =
    \bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \bar P(t)|\Big]
    +\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    = O(\lambda)
    +\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|
    \Big]\,.
    \]
Let $\bar{P}^N$ be the temporal smoothing of $t(p^N)'(t)$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:limit.coefs} that $\bar{P}^N$ converges pointwise to $\bar{P}$, and $\trrr^N$ converges pointwise to $\trrr$. It follows by the bounded convergence theorem that we also have convergence in expectation, so
	\[
	\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
	=\bE\Big[|\bar P^N(t) - (\trrr^N)_t|\Big] + o_N(1)\,.
	\] 
We then note that $\bar{P}^N-\trrr^N$ is the smoothing (via Definitions~\ref{d:sp.smooth} and \ref{d:t.smooth}) of 
	\begin{align} \nonumber
	A^N(t,\vy)
	&\equiv t(p^N)'(t)-\rrr^{\plus,N}(t,\vy)
	= t(p^N)'(t)-\sum_{B^\frozen \subseteq B^{\frozen,\coarse}}
    \frac{|B|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
    \rrr^{\trunc,N}(t,B) 
    \\
	&\qquad= \bigg(
	1-\frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|} 
	\bigg)
	t(p^N)'(t)
	+ \sum_{B^\frozen \subseteq B^{\frozen,\coarse}} \frac{|B|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
	\bigg(
	t(p^N)'(t) -
	\rrr^{\trunc,N}(t,B)\bigg)\,,
	
	 \end{align}
where the correspondence between $\vy$ and $B^{\frozen,\coarse}$ is as described around \eqref{e:review.P}. For the first term in
\eqref{e:P.N.r.frozen.twoterms}, at any fixed time $t$, we have
\[\bE\bigg[ 1-\frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|} \bigg]
    = 1 - \sum_{B^{\frozen,\coarse}}
    \frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}{M^\frozen}
    \frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
    = 1 - \frac{M}{M^\frozen}
    = o_{\trK}(1)\,,
\]
by recalling the choice of $M^\frozen$ from Definition~\ref{d:froze}. For the second term in \eqref{e:P.N.r.frozen.twoterms},  we argued in the proof of Proposition~\ref{p:budget-constraints-without-frozen}\ref{it:Ising-budget-constraint} that the total fraction of particles ever frozen is with high probability at most $o_{\trK}(1)$, so this term is also small on average at any fixed time for the process $Y$. Altogether this shows
	\beq
	\bE\Big[ |A^N(t,\vY^{\frozen,N,\RomI:\RomIII}(t)) |\Big]
	= \int_{\R^3} |A^N(t,\vy)| \varrho_{N,t}(d\vy)
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,.
	\eeq
Let $\tilde{A}^N$ be the spatial smoothing of $A^N$, via Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth}. Let $\tvY^{\frozen,N}(t)\equiv \vY^{\frozen,N}(t)+\xxx$, and denote the projection onto the sum of the first three coordinates as
 $\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N} = \tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N,\RomI}+\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N,\RomII}+\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N,\RomIII}$. Then
	\begin{align*} &\bE\Big[ |\tilde{A}^N(t, \tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N}(t)) |\Big]
	= \int_{\R} |\tilde{A}^N(t,y)| \overline{\varrho_{N,t}*\sphi}(y)\,dy \\
	&\qquad = \int_{\R} \bigg|
	\int_{H(y)} \int_{\R^3} \sphi(\vy-\vx) A^N(t,\vx)
		\,\rho_{N,t}(d\vx)\,d\vy \bigg| \,dy \\
	&\qquad\le  \int_{\R^3}
	|A^N(t,\vx)| \bigg( \int_{\R^3}
		 \sphi(\vy-\vx) \,d\vy\bigg)
		\,\rho_{N,t}(d\vx) =  \int_{\R^3}
	|A^N(t,\vx)|\rho_{N,t}(d\vx) \le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\end{align*}
using the previous estimate \eqref{e:AN.small.finiteN}. This shows that the bound \eqref{e:AN.small.finiteN} can be passed to the spatially smoothed quantity $A^N$. Similarly, let $\bar{A}^N$ be the temporal smoothing of $\tilde{A}^N$, via Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth}. Then
	\begin{align*}
	&\bE\Big[ |\bar{A}^N(t,\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N}(t))| \Big]
	=\int_{\R} |\bar{A}^N(t,y)| \overline{\varrho_{N,t}*\sphi}(y)\,dy\\
	&\qquad\le \int_{\R}  
	\bigg( \int_{\R}\tphi(t-s) |  \tilde{A}^N(s) |\,ds  \bigg) \,
	 \overline{\varrho_{N,t}*\sphi}(y)\,dy \\
	&\qquad=
	\int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\bigg[ \int_{\R} | \tilde{A}^N(s) | 
	 \overline{\varrho_{N,s}*\sphi}(y)
	 \,dy \bigg] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:06:06.299765+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_1078611bccc031a28b58a0008adc81dceb3a33555eeca0c8a88acf99100cfb16","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:Buse_basic_properties of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] [Busa-Sepp-Sore-22a] 
On the space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb P)$, there exists a process
\[
\Bigl(W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t): \xi \in \mathfrak{X}, (x,s;y,t) \in \mathbb{R}^4\Bigr)
\]
such that for each fixed $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$, $\xi \in \Xi^c$, and $x \mapsto W^\xi(0,t;x,t)$ is a Brownian motion with diffusion coefficient $\sqrt 2$ and drift $2\mathcal P(\xi)$. Furthermore, the process satisfies the following properties on a single event of probability one:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
\item{\rm(Continuity)}  The $\mathbb{R}^4 \times \mathfrak{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ function  $(x,s;y,t;\xi) \mapsto W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t)$ is  continuous. Furthermore, if $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^4$ is a compact set, then for all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$ and sequences $\xi_n \to \xi$, there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ so that for all $n \ge N$, we have 
\[
W^{\xi_n}(x,s;y,t) = W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t),\quad \text{for all }(x,s;y,t) \in K.
\]
 \item {\rm(Additivity)}  For all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$ and $p,q,r \in \mathbb{R}^2$, 
    $W^{\xi}(p;q) + W^{\xi}(q;r) = W^{\xi}(p;r)$.   In particular, \\ $W^{\xi}(p;q) = -W^{\xi}(q;p)$ and $W^{\xi}(p;p) = 0$.
    \item {\rm(Monotonicity along a horizontal line)}
     Whenever $\xi_1< \xi_2$ in $\mathfrak{X}$, $x < y$, and $t \in \mathbb{R}$,
    \[
  W^{\xi_1}(x,t;y,t) \le W^{\xi_2}(x,t;y,t).
    \]
    \item \rm{(Divergence to $\pm \infty$)} 
    For all $\xi_1 < \xi_2$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$,
    \[
\lim_{x \to \pm \infty} W^{\xi_2} (0,0;x,t) -W^{\xi_1}(0,0;x,t) = \pm \infty.
\]
    \item {\rm(Eternal solution)} For 
    all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$, $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$, and $s < t$,
    \begin{equation}
    W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t) = \sup_{z \in \mathbb{R}}\{W^{\xi}(x,s;z,s) +
 \mathcal{L}(z,s;y,t)\}.
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["d>=2 integer; real harmonics orthonormal for probability surface measure","P_l(1)=1; fixed dimension throughout","polynomials have finitely many coefficients"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:42:45.052423+00:00","domain":"Hermite interpolation; positive zonal kernels; spherical universal optimality","id":"claim_109875adfd105aaef59be23afb39e3a4e35c93b1540b5f44db1f9edd648408b7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Fix an integer d>=2 and normalized uniform surface measure sigma on S^(d-1). Let H_l be the real degree-l spherical harmonics, h_l=dim H_l, and Y_(l,1),...,Y_(l,h_l) any orthonormal basis in L2(sigma). Let P_l be the degree-l polynomial orthogonal to lower-degree polynomials for weight (1-t^2)^((d-3)/2) on [-1,1], normalized by P_l(1)=1. Then sum_(j=1)^(h_l) Y_(l,j)(x)Y_(l,j)(y)=h_l P_l(<x,y>). In particular P_l(<x,y>) is a positive semidefinite kernel: for any finite x_i on the sphere and real c_i, sum_(i,j)c_i c_j P_l(<x_i,x_j>)>=0. For a real polynomial u=sum_l a_l P_l, its zonal kernel u(<x,y>) is positive semidefinite if and only if every a_l>=0. The product of two such polynomials again has nonnegative P_l coefficients. If every coefficient through the respective degrees is strictly positive, the product also has every coefficient through its degree strictly positive. Here d=2 uses the normalized Chebyshev polynomials, and d>=3 the Gegenbauer polynomials rescaled to value 1 at 1. Positive semidefinite kernels allow zero quadratic forms; strictly positive coefficients do not mean strict positivity of every finite Gram matrix.","status":"unverified"}
