{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:00.757321+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_33a83e61eaaf480d6f7b88238d9983fa6a10d838a9ab4da6384ddc5fd7b8c381","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Conjecture 1 (Batchelor Scale Conjecture) of arXiv:2512.04297, 'Mixing at the Batchelor Scale for White-In-Time Flows'] For $u$ given by a 2-dimensional stochastic Navier--Stokes equation \\cite[Systems 1]{bedrossian2021PTRF} or a 3-dimensional hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equation \\cite[Systems 2]{bedrossian2021PTRF}, the dissipation rate $\\lambda^\\kappa$ is of order 1 for small $\\kappa$, that is\n$$ -\\infty<\\liminf_{\\kappa \\to 0} \\lambda^\\kappa \\leq \\limsup_{\\kappa \\to 0} \\lambda^\\kappa < 0.$$ (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the factors are independent","entries i.i.d. centered Gaussian, variance 1/n","square factors of equal dimension","the largest-singular-value claim needs strong convergence, which is stronger than convergence of the spectral distribution"],"created_at":"2026-08-20T03:43:30.216158+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_33a8efc37836202fed9468a5983040948a4b1e47488753c7edb06802b1e30ddb","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $G_1,\\dots,G_p$ be independent $n \\times n$ matrices with i.i.d. $\\mathcal{N}(0,1/n)$ entries. The limiting singular value distribution of the product $G_p \\cdots G_1$ is the Fuss-Catalan law of order $p$, whose upper edge is $(p+1)^{(p+1)/2}p^{-p/2}$. For $p=1$ this is $2$, recovering the square Gaussian case; for $p=2$ it is $3^{3/2}/2=\\sqrt{27/4}=2.5980\\ldots$; for $p=3$ it is $3.0792\\ldots$. Moreover the largest singular value itself converges to that edge, not merely the bulk. This last point matters and is strictly stronger: convergence of the spectral distribution locates the edge but by itself does not exclude an outlier above it, so a bound that needs no outlier cannot be justified by the Fuss-Catalan law alone.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Z has i.i.d. mean-zero unit-variance entries with finite fourth moment (orthogonally invariant, e.g. Gaussian, for the sharpest vector statements)","rank(X) = r fixed, its nonzero singular values fixed on the noise scale","m/n -> beta in (0, 1]; the loss is Frobenius"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:37:33.911379+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_33ac0767a68834a907f3d5ea4c4652965bbd6ad4e44964080117e92a26c8252f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $Y_n = X_n + \\sigma Z_n$ where $Y_n$ is $m \\times n$ with $m/n \\to \\beta \\in (0, 1]$, $Z_n$ has i.i.d. entries of mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment, and $X_n$ has fixed rank $r$ with singular values $\\sigma\\sqrt{n}\\, x_1, \\dots, \\sigma\\sqrt{n}\\, x_r$ (so the $x_k$ are the signal singular values on the scale of the noise, $x_k > 0$ fixed). Write the singular values of $Y_n$ on the same scale, $y_k := s_k(Y_n) / (\\sigma \\sqrt{n})$. THEOREM (Gavish and Donoho, 2017). (i) For each $k \\le r$: if $x_k > \\beta^{1/4}$ then $y_k \\to \\sqrt{(x_k^2 + 1)(x_k^2 + \\beta)} / x_k$, and if $x_k \\le \\beta^{1/4}$ then $y_k \\to 1 + \\sqrt\\beta$ (the bulk edge); every other singular value of $Y_n$ converges to the bulk. (ii) Among all estimators of the form $\\hat X = \\sum_k \\eta(y_k)\\, \\sigma\\sqrt{n}\\; \\hat u_k \\hat v_k^T$ that keep the sample singular vectors and replace each singular value by a function $\\eta$ of it, the one minimizing the asymptotic Frobenius loss $\\lim \\|\\hat X - X_n\\|_F^2 / (\\sigma^2 n)$ is $$\\eta^*(y) = \\frac{1}{y}\\sqrt{(y^2 - \\beta - 1)^2 - 4\\beta} \\quad \\text{for } y \\ge 1 + \\sqrt\\beta, \\qquad \\eta^*(y) = 0 \\quad \\text{for } y < 1 + \\sqrt\\beta.$$ (iii) The asymptotic loss of $\\eta^*$ is strictly smaller than that of hard thresholding at any threshold and of soft thresholding at any threshold whenever some $x_k > \\beta^{1/4}$; on a pure-noise matrix ($r = 0$) $\\eta^*$ returns the zero matrix. The rule selects the rank (the number of $y_k$ above the edge $1 + \\sqrt\\beta$) and the amount of shrinkage of each retained component from the data, without cross-validation; with $\\sigma$ unknown it is combined with the median estimate $\\hat\\sigma = y_{\\mathrm{med}}/\\sqrt{n \\mu_\\beta}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:09.854732+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_33bb960c34aaa11f8121d7722b37c454c0d3c47f55ab16e4191bf499c3f3c53a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.20026, 'Quasihelix properties\\ of selected Volterra Gaussian processes'] Let $\gamma\in[0,1)$. Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[1)]
\item Let $\alpha\in(-1/2+\gamma/2,1/2+\gamma/2)$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[$(i)$]
There exists a constant $C(\alpha,\gamma)>0$ such that, for any $0\le s<t$,
\[
\ex\big(U^{(2)}(t)-U^{(2)}(s)\big)^2
\le C(\alpha,\gamma)(t-s)^{2\alpha+1-\gamma}.
\]

\item[$(ii)$]
The process $U^{(2)}$ is a local
$(\alpha+\frac12,\alpha+\frac{1-\gamma}{2},0,T)$-generalized quasihelix for any $T>0$.
\end{enumerate}

\item If $\alpha\in[1/2+\gamma/2,1)$, then the process $U^{(2)}$ is a local
$(\alpha+\frac12,\alpha,0,T)$-generalized quasihelix for any $T>0$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.495384+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_340d9decfe1f007dd6ce9f49d9302740e6338fdd6a9686dda0c41a9c2c01228d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 34 (Finite-dimensional inverse for the negative raw branch) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:double-moment-inverse}
Let \(X,Y,Z,W>0\) satisfy
\begin{equation}\lab{eq:inverse-moment-region}
 X+Y+Z<W<(\sqrt X+\sqrt Y+\sqrt Z)^2.
\end{equation}
There are unique \(S,A,B,D>0\) such that
\begin{align}
 X&=A+\frac{A^2}{S},&
 Y&=B+\frac{B^2}{S},&
 Z&=D+\frac{D^2}{S},\lab{eq:inverse-three-moments}\\
 W&=A+B+D+\frac{(A+B+D)^2}{S}.\lab{eq:inverse-fourth-moment}
\end{align}
Consequently, \(T=-S\) and \(F=-(S+A+B+D)\) give the unique solution
of these moment equations in the raw-parameter branch \(T<0\), \(F<0\).
The scalar equation determining \(S\) has a nonvanishing derivative at its
root.

Moreover, let \(w,w'>0\), let \(u,u'>0\), and suppose
\[
 a^2=w^2+u^2,\qquad b^2=(w')^2+(u')^2,\qquad
 \theta=\frac{u}{w^2}=\frac{u'}{(w')^2}.
\]
If
\begin{align*}
 X_n&=a^2n,&Y_n&=b^2n,\\
 Q_n&=n^{21}+O(n^{20}),\\
 Z_n&=Q_n-2u'n^{11}+O(n^{10}),&
 W_n&=Q_n+2un^{11}+O(n^{10}),
\end{align*}
then \eqref{eq:inverse-moment-region} holds for all sufficiently large \(n\),
and the corresponding solution satisfies
\begin{equation}\lab{eq:inverse-raw-asymptotics}
 S_n=\theta^{-2}n+O(1),\qquad
 A_n=w^2n+O(1),\qquad
 B_n=(w')^2n+O(1).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:13:49.971829+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_340e082d40e3c67119e2b8e18d01a4edc01332ad451a5e2e17fa94a8e3d2aba1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:sections of arXiv:2411.07157, 'Rough differential equations in the flow approach'] Given $\tau \in \mathfrak{T}$, we define $\text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\tau] \subset \prod_{\underline{\tau} \in \tau} \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\tau}]$ 
by setting 
\begin{equs}
\text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\tau]
\eqdef
\big\{ 
\big(F_{\underline{\tau}}\in \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\tau}] : \underline{\tau} \in \tau\big): \enskip 
\forall \underline{\tau}, \underline{\tau}' \in \tau\;\text{and}\; f \in \mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\tau},\underline{\tau}')\,,\; \mathbf{f} F_{\underline{\tau}} =  F_{\underline{\tau}'}
\big\}\,.
\end{equs}
We define $\text{${\mcb{C}}$}[\tau]\subset \prod_{\underline{\tau} \in \tau} \text{${\mcb{C}}$}[\underline{\tau}]$ analogously. 

Moreover, for $\underline{\tau} \in \tau \in \mathfrak{T}$, let $\iota_{\tau,\underline{\tau}}: \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\tau] \rightarrow \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\tau}]$ be the ``fiber'' map $\big(F_{\underline{\tau}'}\in\mathcal{H}^{\underline{\tau}'} : \underline{\tau}' \in \tau\big) \mapsto F_{\underline{\tau}}$. 
Observe that $\iota_{\tau,\underline{\tau}}$ has a left inverse given by the ``section'' map $\pi_{\tau,\underline{\tau}}: \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\tau}] \rightarrow \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\tau]$ defined by setting
\[
\text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\underline{\tau}]\ni F_{\underline{\tau}}\mapsto\pi_{\tau,\underline{\tau}}F_{\underline{\tau}}\eqdef\Big(\frac{1}{|\mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\tau},\underline{\tau}')|}
\sum_{f \in \mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\tau},\underline{\tau}')} \text{$\mathbf{f}$} F_{\underline{\tau}} : \underline{\tau}'\in\tau\Big)\in \text{${\mcb{B}}$}[\tau]
\,.
\] 
We use the same notation for the analogous maps between $\text{${\mcb{C}}$}[\underline{\tau}]$ and $\text{${\mcb{C}}$}[\tau]$. 

Note that $|\mathrm{Iso}(\underline{\tau},\underline{\tau}')|$ actually does not depend on the choice of $\underline{\tau},\underline{\tau}'\in\tau$. In the sequel, we therefore just write $|\mathrm{Aut}(\tau)|\eqdef |\mathrm{Aut}(\underline{\tau})|$ for any $\underline{\tau}\in\tau$.

Finally, for $\underline{\tau} \in \tau$ we sometimes write $\iota_{\underline{\tau}} \eqdef \iota_{\tau,\underline{\tau}}$ and $\pi_{\underline{\tau}} \eqdef \pi_{\tau,\underline{\tau}}$ to lighten subscripts.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. nonnegative weights on Z^d","existence holds in case (a) d=2 with no hypothesis, case (b) F(0) < p_c, case (c) F(0) > p_c with E tau_e < infinity; case (d) F(0) = p_c with d > 2 is OPEN","F continuous is a SUFFICIENT condition for uniqueness","the statement is about FINITE geodesics only"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542657+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3439799dcf869b96ef8603273809d352afd98579ca6a151dff8f1d66fd0af028","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d with weight law F. EXISTENCE of a finite geodesic between every pair of vertices, almost surely and simultaneously over all pairs, is known in each of the following cases, and the case division matters. (a) d = 2 and F ARBITRARY: Wierman and Reh proved that for any passage time distribution, with probability one there is a geodesic between any two points of Z^2. (b) Any d, with F(0) < p_c(d): existence follows from standard subcritical estimates. (c) Any d, with F(0) > p_c(d) and E[tau_e] < infinity: existence was proved by Zhang. (d) The remaining case F(0) = p_c(d) with d > 2 is STILL UNRESOLVED in general, though existence is known for distributions with F(0) = F(delta) = p_c for some delta > 0 in sufficiently high dimensions. So it is WRONG to say that geodesics need F(0) < p_c; that condition is sufficient and convenient, not necessary, and supercritical zero-weight percolation does not by itself destroy existence. UNIQUENESS is a separate matter: a continuous F is a SUFFICIENT condition for the model to be uniquely geodesic, since two distinct finite paths then have equal passage time with probability zero and there are countably many pairs of paths. With atoms - a two-valued weight law, say - ties are genuine and multiple geodesics occur with positive probability. All of the above is about FINITE geodesics; the existence, direction, uniqueness and coalescence of semi-infinite geodesics is a separate and largely open subject whose known results require differentiability or curvature assumptions on the limit shape. [Wierman and Reh (1978); Kesten, Aspects of First Passage Percolation, (9.23); Zhang; verified against Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, Section 4.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:31:49.844542+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_343f93727fc15914326f1ba88eeac6b98ee395a33c7c9486b4201a9d20a1a38e","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:expectation-taylor of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma>0$, and put $D=d\gamma$. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact. Suppose that real random variables $X,Y,M$ satisfy, for some $p,q$,
\begin{equation}
p>\max\{2,D\},\qquad q>\max\{1,D\},\qquad
2q\left(1-\frac1p\right)>1,
\end{equation}
and $X\in L^p$, $Y,M\in L^q$. Suppose, uniformly for $b\in K$ and $1\le j\le d$,
\begin{equation}
U_j(t,b)=tb_jX+\frac{t^2b_j^2}{2}Y+R_j(t,b),
\qquad |R_j(t,b)|\le C_K|t|^3M.
\end{equation}
Then, with
\[
F(u):=\prod_{j=1}^d|1+u_j|^\gamma,
\qquad A(b):=\sum_jb_j,
\qquad B(b):=\sum_jb_j^2,
\]
one has, uniformly for $b\in K$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb E F(U(t,b))
&=1+\gamma tA(b)\mathbb E X\\
&\quad+\frac{t^2}{2}\left\{\gamma B(b)\mathbb E Y+
\left[\gamma(\gamma-1)B(b)+\gamma^2(A(b)^2-B(b))\right]\mathbb E X^2\right\}
+o(t^2).\notag
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:33:43.759824+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3472fd236dc83d0eed23eedeeca7a44ca517b29fa69ffa200a45069897a480ef","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn cor:conditional-ldp of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] (Conditional LDP)

Assume $Q_n$ is a sequence of random symmetric zero-diagonal $v$-tensors.
We say that $ N_n(Q_n,\phi,{{\bf X}})$ satisfies a \emph{conditional LDP} with speed $n$ and a deterministic good rate function $J(\cdot):\mathbb{R} \to [0,\infty]$, if the level sets of $J(\cdot)$ are compact, and for any Borel set $F\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}_{Q_n} \Bigg(
 - \inf_{x \in F^\circ} J(x) - \varepsilon 
 \le \frac{1}{n} \log \mathbb{P}\big( N_n(Q_n,\phi,{{\bf X}}) \in F \big|\, Q_n\big)
 \le - \inf_{x \in \overline{F}} J(x) + \varepsilon
\Bigg)\xrightarrow{n\to\infty} 1,
\end{align}
where $\mathbb{P}_{Q_n}$ denotes the probability
over the randomness of $Q_n$. Moreover, $F^\circ$ and $\overline{F}$ denote the interior and the closure of $F$, respectively.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.354793+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3476ca2b2d66e332b342e3b77d62e015071a36e4b7a149dab3b5a797c97a4393","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 216 (constraints on $(\bbb,\vvv,\uuu,\rrr,\www)^{\frozen,\coarse,N}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For the coefficients defined by \eqref{e:b.plus.coarse}--\eqref{e:w.plus.coarse},
with high probability,
the following hold simultaneously for all $0\leq d\leq d_{\max}-1$:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item 
     
    The ``domain constraint'': for all 
    $B^{\frozen,\coarse} \in \mathcal{C}^\frozen(q_d)$,
    \beq
    \vvv^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d,B^{\frozen,\coarse}) 
    \ge 
    q_d p'(q_d)
    \frac{\uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d,B^{\frozen,\coarse})^2 }
    {\rrr^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d,B^{\frozen,\coarse})}
    - \frac{\eta^2}{2}\,.
    \eeq
(If $\uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}$ and $\rrr^{\frozen,\coarse,N}$ are both zero, we interpret the ratio on the right-hand side as zero.)
 \item
 
The ``budget constraint'' for the spherical perceptron:
    \beq
    
    \bE_{\bG^N}
    \bigg[ \Cost\Big(
        \bbb^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
        \vvv^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
            \uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)
        \Big) \bigg]
    \le \frac{1}{\alpha} 
    + \epsilon^\circ
 .
    \eeq
\item 
The ``budget constraint'' for the Ising perceptron:
    \beq
    
    \bE_{\bG^N}\bigg[ \Cost\Big(
        \bbb^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
        \vvv^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
        \uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)
        \Big) \bigg]
    \le \frac{\bE_{\bG^N}[
    \www^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)^{1/2}]^2}{\alpha} 
    + \epsilon^\circ\,.
    \eeq
\item  The ``diffusivity'' for the Ising perceptron:
    \[\Big|\bE(\www^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)) -1\Big|
    \le\epsilon^\circ\,.\]
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Assertions
\eqref{it:spherical-budget-constraint-plus-coarse}--\eqref{it:Ising-w-constraint-plus-coarse} follow straightforwardly from Jensen's inequality. For assertion \eqref{it:domain-constraint-plus-coarse}, note 
from \eqref{e:indicator.qd.less.than.qT},
 \eqref{e:def.r}, and \eqref{e:P.plus.hist}
that Proposition~\ref{p:budget-constraints-HIST}\ref{it:domain-constraint-plus-HIST} can be rewritten as
	\[
	\vvv^{\frozen,N}(q_d,B^\frozen) 
    \ge  q_d p'(q_d) 
    I(B^\frozen)
	\frac{\uuu^{\frozen,N}(q_d,B^\frozen)^2}
		{\rrr^{\frozen,N}(q_d,B^\frozen)}
    - \frac{\eta^2}{2}\,,
	\]
where we again interpret a $0/0$ ratio as zero, and
	\[I(B^\frozen)\equiv \ind\bigg\{|B^\frozen \cap[M]| \ge 
		\frac{M}{\BUCKETS^2}
		\bigg\}\,.\]
If $I(B^\frozen)=0$ for all $B^\frozen\in B^{\frozen,\coarse}$,
then the bound \eqref{e:domain.plus.coarse} follows.
Otherwise, consider a discrete probability measure $\pi$, and random variables $v_j,u_j,r_j$ which are zero on a set of indices $Z$, and otherwise satisfy
	\[
	v_j \ge A' \frac{(u_j)^2}{r_j} - a'\]
Assume $\pi_+ \equiv 1-\pi(Z)\in(0,1]$. Then Jensen's inequality gives
	\[
	\frac{\sum_j \pi_j v_j}{\pi_+}
	\ge \frac{1}{\pi_+}
	\sum_{j\notin Z} \pi_j \bigg\{
	A' \frac{(u_j)^2}{r_j} - a'\bigg\}
	\ge A'
	\bigg(\frac{1}{\pi_+}\sum_j \pi_j u_j\bigg)^2\bigg/
	\bigg(
	\frac{1}{\pi_+}\sum_j \pi_j r_j
	\bigg) - a'
	\]
and rearranging gives
	\[
	\sum_j \pi_j v_j
	\ge
	A' \bigg(\sum_j \pi_j u_j\bigg)^2\bigg/
	\bigg(\sum_j \pi_j r_j
	\bigg)
	-a'\pi_+\,.
	\]
If we apply the above inequality with the probability measure $\pi$
over buckets $B^\frozen\in B^{\frozen,\coarse}$ with probabilities 
$\pi(B^\frozen)=|B^\frozen|/|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|$, then we obtain the desired conclusion.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["one-dimensional, nearest-neighbor random walk in an i.i.d. random environment","existence of kappa in (0,2) solving E[rho^kappa]=1 for the environment's local odds ratio rho","transience of the walk, or the appropriate directional condition for the regime under study","technical non-lattice or non-degeneracy conditions on the environment law needed for the stable-law convergence"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.989782+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_34a6da748207f4cd112326dff5e5e3f10da84d0a5a8d231a18afecb144c6023f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For one-dimensional nearest-neighbor random walk in an i.i.d. random environment in the subballistic or intermediate regime, parametrized by an index kappa solving E[rho^kappa]=1 for rho the local odds ratio of the environment, hitting times of successive integers admit a classical Kesten construction as a branching process with migration: individuals reproduce according to an environment-dependent offspring law with an added immigration/emigration term reflecting the local environment. The Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer theorem shows that for kappa in the relevant range below 2, the hitting time of level n, normalized by n^{1/kappa}, converges to a kappa-stable distribution, via a result on the total population size of the associated branching-with-migration process, which itself has heavy-tailed, stable-scaling behavior. This gives the precise non-Gaussian scaling limits characterizing anomalous, subdiffusive or index-dependent, behavior in one-dimensional random walk in random environment, a phenomenon absent for simple random walk. It does not extend to higher dimensions, since the explicit branching correspondence is a genuinely one-dimensional, nearest-neighbor phenomenon, and it requires the environment to be i.i.d. with a moment condition admitting a solution kappa in the relevant range. Typical failure: Extending the branching-process-with-migration correspondence and its kappa-stable scaling conclusion to multi-dimensional random walk in random environment, or to environments with dependence rather than i.i.d. structure, where no analogous exact combinatorial bijection to a branching process is known; the Kesten construction is a special, essentially exact identity in one dimension that does not generalize by analogy, so claiming kappa-stable scaling outside the one-dimensional i.i.d. setting requires an entirely separate justification. Canonical reference: Kesten, Kozlov and Spitzer, 1975, Compositio Mathematica.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:57:28.718634+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_34cae7d05f40ab5f2257cb8f4278c2117e6ef4f4496d8e64353f3b697f82b6ef","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2609.01166, 'Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions'] The rates above can be transferred to the case of finite-time observations, provided that exponential ergodicity holds.
To observe that, let \(\V\) be a potential for which the corresponding nonlinear dynamics satisfy
\begin{equation}
\chi^2(P_t\Vert\Pi_0)
\leq
\eta_t
:=
C_{t_0}e^{-\rho_\chi(t-t_0)},
\qquad t\geq t_0,
\end{equation}
for some \(t_0\geq0\), \(C_{t_0}<\infty\), and \(\rho_\chi>0\), where \(P_t\) and \(\Pi_0\) denote the laws with densities \(p_t\) and \(\pi_0\), respectively. For the OU potential~\eqref{eq:ou-potential}, the inequality~\eqref{eq:chi2-transfer-assumption} holds under the assumptions of~\cite{belomestny-morozova-ou}, with
\(
C_{t_0}=\chi^2(P_{t_0}\Vert\Pi_0).
\)
Let \(X_1^{T_n},\ldots,X_n^{T_n}\) be independent observations from \(P_{T_n}\) for some \(T_n>0\), and let \(G_{M_n}\) be the event on which~\eqref{eq:full-mle-oracle-transfer} holds. Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:oracle}, it holds that
\[
P_{T_n}^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
\leq
\delta+n\tau_0(M_n)
+
\frac12\sqrt{(1+\eta_{T_n})^n-1}.
\]
Indeed,
\[
1+\chi^2(P_t^{\otimes n}\Vert\Pi_0^{\otimes n})
=
\left(1+\chi^2(P_t\Vert\Pi_0)\right)^{n}
\leq
(1+\eta_t)^n,
\]
and therefore
\(
\TV(P_t^{\otimes n},\Pi_0^{\otimes n})
\leq
0.5\sqrt{(1+\eta_t)^n-1}.
\)
The claimed bound follows from
\(
P_{T_n}^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
\leq
\Pi_0^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
+
\TV(P_{T_n}^{\otimes n},\Pi_0^{\otimes n})
\)
and
\(
\Pi_0^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
\leq\delta+n\tau_0(M_n).
\)
Consequently, if
\(
n\eta_{T_n}\longrightarrow0
\)
and
\(
n\tau_0(M_n)\longrightarrow0,
\)
then the stationary oracle inequality and the rates in~\eqref{eq:kl-rate} remain valid for observations from \(P_{T_n}\). Under~\eqref{eq:chi2-transfer-assumption}, it is sufficient to choose, for any \(\varepsilon>0\),
\(
T_n
\geq
t_0+(1+\varepsilon)\rho_\chi^{-1}\log n,
\)
which guarantees
\(
n\eta_{T_n}
\leq
C_{t_0}n^{-\varepsilon}
\longrightarrow0
\)
as \(n\to\infty\).
Since by Lemma~\ref{lem:explicit-tails}
it holds that
\(
\tau_0(M)\lesssim e^{-c_a(M-v_\star)},
\)
taking
\(
M_n=v_\star+C_{\mathrm{tr}}\log n
\)
with \(c_aC_{\mathrm{tr}}>1\) yields the overall error \(\delta+o(1)\) and hence the desired rate. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.745954+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_34eded4e47fda8bfa953967f1708fed3055331411980a025ddafe2c472a1c787","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Within our coupling of the collection times (Definition~\ref{def:coupling}),
  $T_{m,0}$ is independent of $T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}$ and this difference
  has \textsc{mgf}
  \[
    M_{T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}}(t) = I_{m, p}(t), \quad t \leqslant 0.
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    If $T_{m, 0} = k$, then the value of $T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}$
    is a deterministic function of the initial clumsiness $\{ U_{L(i,k)} \}_{i \in [m]}$,
    the future updates $\{ C_n \}_{n > k}$,
    and the future clumsiness $\{ U_n \}_{n > k}$. Call this function $f$.
    We will make $f$ explicit. Consider an initial clumsiness vector
    $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_m)^\top \in [0, 1]^m$,
    coupon updates $\mathbf{y} = (y_n)_{n > 0} \in [m]^\mathbb{N}$,
    and future clumsiness $\mathbf{z} = (z_n)_{n > 0} \in [0, 1]^\mathbb{N}$.
    Then define
    $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y})$ as the most recent update of coupon $i$
    no later than $n$,
    \[
      L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) \coloneqq
      \sup\{ k \leqslant n \mid y_k = i \}, \quad
      i \in [m], \quad n \geqslant 0,
    \]
    where naturally $\sup\emptyset = -\infty$ and $L'(i, 0; \mathbf{y}) = -\infty$.
    Define
    \begin{align*}
      f(\mathbf{x}; \mathbf{y}; \mathbf{z})
      \coloneqq \inf \{ n \geqslant 0 \mid {} &\text{for all $i \in [m]$,}\\
          &\text{if $x_i > 1-p$ or $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) > 0$,}\\
          &\text{then $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) > 0$
          and $z_{L'(i, n; \mathbf{y})} \leq 1-p$}
          \}.
    \end{align*}
    Thus, for any integers $\ell \geqslant m$ and $x \geqslant 0$,
    \begin{align*}
      \PP\left( T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \right)
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m}
        \PP\left( T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \mid T_{m,0} = k\right)
        \PP(T_{m,0} = k)\\
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, k)}, \dots, U_{L(m, k)};
      C_{k+1}, C_{k+2}, \dots;
      U_{k+1}, U_{k+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)\\
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, \ell)}, \dots, U_{L(m, \ell)};
      C_{\ell+1}, C_{\ell+2}, \dots;
      U_{\ell+1}, U_{\ell+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)\\
      &= \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, \ell)}, \dots, U_{L(m, \ell)};
      C_{\ell+1}, C_{\ell+2}, \dots;
      U_{\ell+1}, U_{\ell+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \underbrace{
        \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)
      }_1\\
      &= \PP\left(T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \mid T_{m,0} = \ell\right).
    \end{align*}
    The third line uses our i.i.d.~assumptions from
    Definition~\ref{def:coupling}.
    This proves the independence of $T_{m,0}$ and $T_{m,p} - T_{m, 0}$.
    Hence the factorisation
    $M_{T_{m,0}}(t)\,M_{T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}}(t) = M_{T_{m,0}}\,I_{m,p}(t)$.
    These quantities are non-zero; divide both sides to conclude the proof.
    
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.551748+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_34fd9fae7b41cda5283a1108094a574e2c1ee96b6cfe04afedd622806387eefe","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2604.01978, 'Homogenized Transformers'] Fix $i,j\in[n]^2$ and define
\(
R_{ij}(t)\coloneqq \langle x_i(t),x_j(t)\rangle.
\)
We have
\begin{equation}
\de R_{ij}(t)
=
\de M_{ij}(t)
+
\cD_{ij}(t)\,\de t,
\end{equation}
where the local martingale part is
\begin{equation}
\de M_{ij}(t)
=
\int_\Uptheta
\left(\langle G_i(t,\bm{\theta}),x_j(t)\rangle+\langle x_i(t),G_j(t,\bm{\theta})\rangle\right)
\,\mathsf{W}(\de\bm{\theta},\de t),
\end{equation}
and the drift is
\begin{align}
\cD_{ij}(t)
&=
\frac1d\left(d-2+R_{ij}(t)^2\right)\,s_{\mu(t)}(x_i(t),x_j(t))\nonumber\\
&-
\frac{(d-1)}{2d}\,R_{ij}(t)\left(s_{\mu(t)}(x_i(t))+s_{\mu(t)}(x_j(t))\right),
\end{align} 
where $\mu(t) = \mu_{X(t)}$ and 
\begin{align*}
s_\mu(x)&\coloneqq \E\left\|\mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x)\right\|^2,\nonumber\\
s_\mu(x,x')&\coloneqq \E\left\langle \mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x),\mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x')\right\rangle.
\end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.060981+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3515ce152b34b5963b7d05c50c165f2995ae5c14e1dc2fc693ff1e6b2b6c5437","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $X$ be an $\R^d$-valued conservative Markov process reversible with respect to a
probability measure $\mu$, and let $Q$ be a nonnegative, nonconstant
observable.  Suppose that conditions \textbf{(I)}-\textbf{(V)} above
hold.  Let
\[
    \theta\in\lambda'((0,\infty)),
    \qquad
    \lambda'(\beta_\theta)=\theta,
\]
and put
\[
    v_\theta=-\lambda''(\beta_\theta)>0,
    \qquad
    I_Q(\theta)
       =\lambda(\beta_\theta)-\beta_\theta\theta.
\]
Then, for every fixed initial state $x$ and every fixed $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
    \bbP_x(A_T\leq\theta T+z)
    \sim
    \frac{
      \psi_{\beta_\theta}(x)
      \langle\psi_{\beta_\theta},\mathbf 1\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}
    }{
      \beta_\theta\sqrt{2\pi v_\theta T}
    }
    \exp\!\left(
       -I_Q(\theta)T+\beta_\theta z
    \right).
\]
Whenever the estimates in \textbf{(III)} are locally uniform in the
initial state, this asymptotic is locally uniform in $(x,z)$.

Moreover, for every $S<\infty$,
\[
    \mathcal L_{\bbP_x}
       \bigl((X_t)_{0\leq t\leq S}\mid A_T\leq\theta T\bigr)
    \longrightarrow
    \mathcal L_{\bbP_x^{(\beta_\theta)}}
       \bigl((X_t)_{0\leq t\leq S}\bigr)
\]
in total variation.  The corresponding fixed-width conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-width-window} holds as well.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:05:28.080749+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_357284b985ff888d2c1c29af9510420130262d1665162bbe9a236df7a5cd3cbf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem maintheorem2 of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] Let $G_n=(V_n,E_n)$ be a sequence of random graphs and choose a root $\overset{\rightarrow}{o}_n$ uniformly among the vertices.
    Suppose that the sequence of rooted weighted random graphs $(G_n,o_n)$ converges locally to an (vertex-rooted) Unimodular Bienaymé-Galton-Watson (UBGW) tree $(\mathbb{T},o)$ with reproduction law $\pi$. Assume further that the ratio $\frac{2|E_n|}{|V_n|}$ converges in probability to the expectation of $\pi$ and that the hypothesis of Theorem~(maintheorem of the paper) holds on the UBGW tree. Now assign i.i.d weights $(w_n(e))_{e \in E(G_n)}$ of distribution $\omega$ on the edges of $G_n$. We have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exists a sequence $(M_n)_n$ of matchings of $G_n$ such that $(G_n,o_n,M_n)$ converges locally to $(\mathbb{T},{o},\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}})$ given by Theorem~(maintheorem of the paper).
        In particular, we have that:

         \[
        \lim_{n \to \infty} 
        \left(  \mathbb{P}\left( \exists v \sim o_n, \{o_n,v\} \in M_n\right),\mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{v\sim o_n}w_n(o_n,v)\mathbbm{1}_{\{o_n,v\} \in M_n}\right]\right) = \perfE(\mathbb{T},o,\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}}),
        \]
        
        \item Reciprocally, for any sequence $(M_n)_n$ of matchings of $G_n$, take $(a,b)$ to be any subsequential limit of
        \[ \left(  \mathbb{P}\left( \exists v \sim o_n, \{o_n,v\} \in M_n\right),\mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{v\sim o_n}w_n(o_n,v)\mathbbm{1}_{\{o_n,v\} \in M_n}\right]\right) ,\]
        then we must have that 
        \[ (a,b)\overset{\mathrm{lex}}{\leq} \perfE(\mathbb{T},o,\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}}).
        \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:05:57.775770+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_357be920cebc25df1b12d2f4b8713fb02fa8d3e42906c8aafe3699e7e255236f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 21 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX,\norm{\cdot})$ be a quasi-normed space.
    Let $\SC\subset \XX$ satisfy \ConditionZetaTextAlphaC{(\alpha,C_0)}.

        \mu(A)
        := \mu\bigl[ (\SC_n)_{n\in \NN},\alpha,C_0\bigr](A)

               \frac{Y_n}{C_0 \cdot n^{\alpha}} \in A
           \biggr), 
        \quad A \in \Borel(\XX),
    \end{equation*}

    and for every $n$ the random vector $Y_n$ is uniformly distributed on $\SC_n$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.493719+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_35a1649f0eed818661ecf26f6be089586b8e06b79355699ab61f4a8e20abb80a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 15 (Double hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{def:double-hive}
For \(\nu\in\Spec_n\), write
\[
\nu^\vee=(-\nu_n,\ldots,-\nu_1).
\]
A double hive with exterior boundary
\((\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi)\) and middle side \(\nu\) is a pair of hives
\[
(h_1,h_2)\in
H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu)\times H_n(\eta,\phi^\vee;\nu^\vee),
\qquad
\phi^\vee=(-\phi_n,\ldots,-\phi_1),
\]
viewed as glued along the common middle side, with opposite orientations on
the two copies of that side.  The corresponding double hive polytope is
\[
\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi^\vee)
:=
\bigcup_{\nu\in\Spec_n + \R \one}
H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu)
\times
H_n(\eta,\phi^\vee;\nu^\vee).
\]
A quadruply augmented double hive is obtained by additionally choosing
Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns on the four exterior boundary components with matching spectra.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["F_q finite with q = p^m","sum_i deg f_i < n (total degrees); the bound is sharp, as the norm form shows","Chevalley's form needs the f_i to vanish at the origin"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:05:27.626667+00:00","domain":"number theory and algebra","id":"claim_35ee79c9fa9041171e62a639c4595448b33224c480be67a60335a1ce17158a8a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let F_q be the finite field with q = p^m elements (p prime) and let f_1, ..., f_r be polynomials in F_q[x_1, ..., x_n] with sum_i deg f_i < n. WARNING (1935): the number N of common zeros of f_1, ..., f_r in F_q^n is divisible by p. CHEVALLEY (1935): if in addition every f_i has zero constant term (so 0 is a common zero), then there is another common zero; in particular a homogeneous form of degree d in more than d variables has a nontrivial zero over F_q, so finite fields are quasi-algebraically closed (C_1 fields). Strengthenings: Ax (1964) showed q^b divides N with b = ceil((n - sum deg f_i) / max deg f_i) (Ax-Katz); the theorem gives the Erdos-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem (among 2n - 1 integers some n have sum divisible by n) by applying it to two forms of degree p - 1 in 2p - 1 variables.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Primary-source scope record, not a new polynomial-gap theorem","Matrix sensing application assumes 1/20-RIP on all rank-at-most-2k matrices","The actual row has iid Gaussian rank-one measurements and m at least C d log^3 d"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T20:04:21.099115+00:00","domain":"sampling and nonconvex learning","id":"claim_35f9c193fc020fba4b06d0f0b693bea38742862f79e20a892b24d653fe16ba68","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"# Moitra-Risteski: relevant decomposition, uncovered phase-retrieval hypotheses

T321 Target 2. Literature applicability finding, not a new proof of Target 2.
Source: Fast Convergence for Langevin Diffusion with Manifold Structure,
arXiv:2002.05576, primary PDF saved under papers/.

Section 2, PDF page 3, requires the matrix-sensing operator to satisfy
(19/20)||M||_F^2 <= ||A(M)||_2^2 <= (21/20)||M||_F^2
for every matrix M of rank at most 2k. This is an operator-wide assumption,
not concentration for a fixed deterministic M.

For phase retrieval take k=1 and A_ph(M)_j=(a_j^T M a_j)/sqrt(m), so the
squared residual is precisely the normalized empirical quartic loss.
For every nonzero measurement a_i, set u=a_i/||a_i|| and M=uu^T. Then
rank(M)=1, ||M||_F=1 and

 ||A_ph(M)||_2^2=(1/m)sum_j(a_j.u)^4 >= ||a_i||^4/m.

Thus the upper RIP inequality would force
m >= (20/21)max_i||a_i||^4. The witness is allowed to depend on the sample,
because RIP quantifies over EVERY rank-one matrix. This is the exact
deterministic fourth-moment obstruction already relevant to this row,
applied to the paper's stated hypothesis; it is not presented as new.
For Gaussian measurements, ||a_1||^2/d tends to 1 in probability. Therefore
for m=C d log^3 d with fixed C, this necessary inequality fails with
probability tending to 1 as d grows. Multiplication by any fixed scalar
normalization of A_ph does not remove the growing d/log^3 d obstruction.
No claim is made here about operators obtained by data-dependent weighting,
truncation or a changed loss; those require their own arguments.

Section 4.1, Theorem 4, PDF page 7, is nevertheless a relevant generic
decomposition framework: along-level and across-level Poincare control,
control of changing conditional density/Jacobian, and finite-time retention
near the minimizer manifold combine into convergence to a restricted law.
These are hypotheses to establish, not consequences of benign landscape
alone. Our C007 is a different polar decomposition with the same unresolved
need for one conditional spectral-gap estimate.

Section 4.2, Theorem 5, PDF pages 7-8, assumes the matrix measurement
conditions above, a sufficiently large beta, and an absolutely continuous
initial law supported near one minimizer component. The target p_i is
defined just before the theorem as the Gibbs law restricted to points
closer to component E_i than the other component. The theorem's displayed
TV error includes an additive epsilon, as well as a decaying chi-square
term. It is not a statement of the full unrestricted even Poincare constant
for the empirical rank-one measurement model at beta~d/epsilon_loss.
The TV accuracy epsilon in the paper must not be identified silently with
the row's optimization/loss tolerance epsilon_loss.

The discussion on PDF page 9 explicitly leaves reaching the prescribed
initialization by unmodified Langevin for future work, while explaining
that optimization can supply such an initialization in the stated models.
Even if a warm-start sampling guarantee were imported, an additive-error
TV guarantee alone is not a variational Poincare inequality for the full law.

NEXT: adapt the near-well decomposition and retention estimates using the
actual rank-one measurement geometry, without imposing false global RIP;
then control the rest of the quotient to obtain the full polynomial gap.
No claim of a solved parameter range or a scored frontier move is made.
The rank-one diagnostic is analytic and unaudited, not a numerical bound
or a Lean-certified assertion.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:07:56.656926+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3602a942d36037448d060dcd4dbbb50334b9b3583ef08c8588a2ae0bde45bc33","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:BESQflow of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\delta \in {\mathbb R}$.  We call ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  driven by $\mathcal W$ a collection ${\mathcal S}$ of continuous processes $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in {\mathbb R},a\ge 0}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
for each $(a,r)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}$, the process $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)$ is almost surely the strong solution of the following SDE  
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a) = 
a + 2 \int_r^x  {\mathcal W}([0,{\mathcal S}_{r,s}(a)], \, \mathrm{d} s) + 
\delta (x-r) 
,\, x\ge r
\end{equation}
 and which, in the case $\delta<0$, is absorbed when hitting $0$.
 \item Almost surely,
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item for all $r\in {\mathbb R}$ and $a\ge 0$, $ {\mathcal S}_{r,r}(a)=a$,
 \item for all $r\le x$, $a\mapsto  {\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a)$ is c\`adl\`ag,
 \item (Perfect flow property) for any $r\le x \le y$ and $a\ge 0$, $\mathcal S_{r,y}(a)=\mathcal S_{x,y}\circ \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)$. 
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}

We call killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$ the flow obtained from the ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow by absorbing at $0$ the flow line $\mathcal S_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at time $\inf\{x>r\,:\,\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0\}$. 

We call general ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  a  ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow or a  killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["entries of Z i.i.d., mean zero, variance one (finite second moment suffices for the almost-sure convergence in the Bai-Silverstein form)","the spectral distribution of Sigma converges weakly to H; p/n -> c in (0, infinity)","Sigma and Z independent (Sigma may be random)"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T16:00:40+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_3625ab2a19639ec1e18b098bfb508774dc8680a3563d30345ceda3df84ad0c18","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $X = Z\\Sigma^{1/2}$ be $n \\times p$ with $Z$ having i.i.d. entries of mean $0$ and variance $1$, $\\Sigma$ positive semidefinite, and let $S = \\frac{1}{n}X^T X$. Then almost surely the empirical spectral distribution of $S$ converges weakly to a nonrandom probability measure $F = F^{c, H}$, characterised as follows: with $\\underline F = (1 - c)\\delta_0 + cF$ (the limiting spectral distribution of the $n \\times n$ companion $\\frac{1}{n}XX^T$) and $\\underline m(z) = \\int \\frac{d\\underline F(t)}{t - z} = -\\frac{1 - c}{z} + c\\,m_F(z)$, for every $z \\in \\mathbb{C}^+$ the value $\\underline m(z)$ is the unique solution in $\\mathbb{C}^+$ of $$z = -\\frac{1}{\\underline m} + c\\int \\frac{\\tau\\, dH(\\tau)}{1 + \\tau\\,\\underline m}.$$ Equivalently, $m_F$ solves $m_F(z) = \\int \\frac{dH(\\tau)}{\\tau\\,(1 - c - c z\\, m_F(z)) - z}$. For x0 ∈ Ω define the superdifferential D^+u(x0) = { p ∈ R^n : limsup_{x→x0} ( u(x) - u(x0) - p·(x-x0) ) / |x - x0| ≤ 0 } and the subdifferential D^-u(x0) = { p : liminf_{x→x0} ( u(x) - u(x0) - p·(x-x0) ) / |x-x0| ≥ 0 }. Then: (a) p ∈ D^+u(x0) if and only if there exists φ ∈ C^1(Ω) with Dφ(x0) = p such that u - φ has a local maximum at x0; symmetrically for D^-u(x0) and local minima. (b) Hence, for continuous F, u is a viscosity subsolution of F(x,u,Du) = 0 iff F(x, u(x), p) ≤ 0 for every x ∈ Ω and every p ∈ D^+u(x), and a viscosity supersolution iff F(x,u(x),p) ≥ 0 for every x ∈ Ω and every p ∈ D^-u(x). (c) u is differentiable at x0 if and only if D^+u(x0) and D^-u(x0) are both nonempty, and in that case D^+u(x0) = D^-u(x0) = {Du(x0)}.","status":"unverified"}

In d >= 3 paths of two walks need not intersect, and the known partial result (Kalikow's 0-1 law: P_0[A_l union A_{-l}] in {0,1}) does not exclude the mixed event. A candidate counterexample structure in d >= 3 would be an i.i.d. environment where the walk is guided to +l or -l depending on a local feature it meets first; the i.i.d. assumption and the fact that the walk visits infinitely many independent regions make such a persistent memory implausible but not provably impossible: the walk in direction +l sees fresh environment forever, and the event that it turns around is a tail event of the walk but not of the environment. I checked that the natural martingale argument (P_omega(A_l) as a function of the environment at the current position) fails because P_omega(A_l) is not measurable with respect to a finite region. No result. Obstruction: Planarity is essential to the d = 2 proof; no substitute in d >= 3.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:50:30.562372+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_376f73ec0e4a8fa79094fd56bcc2e399117f8992563f9193bea8b6347e7d3bba","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] Let $p>d+2$, let $\P_0\in\Pc(\Xc\times\R^d)$, and let
\[
b:\R_+\times\Xc\times\R^d\longrightarrow\R^d
\]
be a Borel-measurable vector field. Assume that there exists a weak solution to
\[
dY_t
=
b(t,X,Y_t)\,dt+\sqrt{2} \,dB_t,
\qquad
(X,Y_0)\sim\P_0,
\qquad
(X, Y_0) \independent B,
\]
where $\independent$ denotes the indepenance. 
For $T>0$ and $R>0$, define
\begin{equation} 
C_1(R,T,b)
:=
\int_0^T
\left\{
\E\Big[
|b(t,X,Y_t)|^p\mathbf{1}_{\{|Y_t|\le R\}}
\Big]
+
\int_{\Xc} \int_{B(0,R)} |b(t,x,y)|^p\,dy\,\mu(dx)
\right\}
dt.
\end{equation}
Assume that $C_1(R,T,b)<\infty$ for every $R>0$. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
    \item 
    For every $t\in(0,T]$, the law
    \[
    \P_t:=\Lc(X,Y_t)
    \]
admits a density with respect to $\mu \otimes \mathrm{L}$,
    still denoted by $\tilde{\P}_{t,x}(y)$. 
    Moreover, for every $R>0$ and every
    $t\in(0,T]$, there exists a constant $K_{T,R}>0$ such that
    \begin{equation} 
    \big\|
    \tilde{\P}_t\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|y|\le R\}}
    \big\|_{\L^p(\mu\otimes \mathrm{L} ) }
    \le
    K_{T,R} \bigl(1+C_1(R,T,b)\bigr).
    \end{equation}

    \item 
    Assume furthermore that the second marginal of $\P_t$ is given by
    \[
    \Lc(Y_t)=\nu(dy)=e^{-V(y)} \,dy, \quad \forall \, t \in \R_+.
    \]
    For every bounded Borel function $\phi:\Xc\to\R$, define
    \[
    w_\phi(t,y):=\E[\phi(X)\mid Y_t=y].
    \]
    Equivalently, for $\nu$-a.e.\ $y$,
    \begin{equation} 
    w_\phi(t,y)
    =
    \int_{\Xc} \phi(x)\,\tilde{\P}_{t,x}(y)\,\mu(dx)\,e^{V(y)}.
    \end{equation}
    Then, for every $R>0$ and every $\delta>0$, there exist constants
    $\alpha,\beta,K>0$, depending only on $C_1(R,T,b)$, $R$, and $\delta$, such
    that for all $y,y'\in B(0,R)$ and all $t,t'\in[\delta,T]$ satisfying
    $|t-t'|\le1$,
    \begin{equation} 
    |w_\phi(t',y')-w_\phi(t,y)|
    \le
    K\|\phi\|_\infty
    \Big(
    |y-y'|^\alpha + |t-t'|^\beta
    \Big).
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. nonnegative edge weights on the nearest-neighbour edges of Z^d, d >= 2","E[min of 2d independent copies of tau_e] < infinity (implied by E[tau_e] < infinity); without it the limit exists only in probability","positivity of mu is NOT part of this theorem and holds exactly when F(0) < p_c"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542493+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_377aff255f0c4f83a8772b658e8326b0c3e89f3f2873cda60908dbe935ed4d02","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d with edge-weight law F supported on [0, infinity). Let Y be the minimum of 2d independent copies of tau_e - the smallest weight among the edges at a vertex. If E[Y] < infinity then the limit mu(e_1) = lim_{n -> infinity} T(0, n e_1)/n exists almost surely and in L^1 and is a deterministic constant in [0, infinity), and the same holds along every lattice direction, defining mu on Z^d and by homogeneity and convexity on all of R^d, invariant under the symmetries of the lattice; mu is either identically 0 or a genuine norm. Three companion facts, each with its own status. (i) WITHOUT the moment condition the limit still exists IN PROBABILITY, by Kesten, Cox-Durrett and Wierman, and when the moment condition does hold the two limits agree. (ii) 0 <= mu(e_1) <= E[tau_e], the upper bound by taking the direct path and applying the law of large numbers - so the finiteness of E[tau_e] gives the bound but is NOT needed for existence. (iii) POSITIVITY is a separate theorem and is not part of this one: mu(e_1) > 0 IF AND ONLY IF F(0) < p_c(d), the bond percolation threshold, and mu(e_1) > 0 if and only if mu(x) > 0 for every nonzero x. When F(0) >= p_c the zero-weight edges percolate, one can travel arbitrarily far in time o(n), and mu vanishes identically. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:11:09.317791+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_379223428004d7efd78d22695193deeb16dd036ad798e8757d892ce06ac2b383","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:restriction-to-a-subset of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] \mbox{}\\
  Let $(X_n,T_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$ be a continuous-time jump process on $G$.
  Recursively, we take $\sigma_0:=0$ and for $n\in{\mathbb N}$, on the event
  $\{\sigma_{n-1}<\infty\}$, we define 
  $\sigma_n:=\inf\{l>\sigma_{n-1}:X_l\neq X_{\sigma_{n-1}}\}$ to be the index
  of the next jump to a different location. 
  The process with self-loops removed is defined by 
  $(X^{\neq},T^{\neq})=(X^{\neq}_n,T^{\neq}_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\sigma_n},\sum_{l=\sigma_n}^{\sigma_{n+1}-1}T_l)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$
  on the event $\{\sigma_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$. 

  Let $\emptyset\neq J\subseteq\Lambda$. We set recursively $\tau_0=0$, 
  $\tau_n=\inf\{ l>\tau_{n-1}: X_l\in J\}$
  for $n\in{\mathbb N}$. In other words, on the event $\{X_0\in J\}$, 
  $\tau_n$ denotes the number of jumps up to the $n$-th return to $J$. 
  The restriction of the process to $J$ is defined
  on the event $\{\tau_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$ by
  $(X^J,T^J)=(X_n^J,T_n^J)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\tau_n},T_{\tau_n})_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$.

  The notation $(X^{J\neq},T^{J\neq})$ means that both operations have
  been applied to the process $(X,T)$, first the restriction to $J$ and
  then self-loop removal.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:12:19.464074+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_37f9e23eb13e2294349f0aaf2da4b0ccc2ed76095064b4331de2e8d3720977fc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 12 (Consistency of the Lipschitz-case powers) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $p=\alpha-1\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textup{Initial value perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=x_0+W_t+Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt x_0+W_t+Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=|x_0-\wt x_0|^p.
\]
Thus the initial error exponent $p=\alpha-1$ is exact.

\item \textup{Drift perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=bt,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt b t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=T^p|b-\wt b|^p.
\]
Since $B=T|b-\wt b|$, this is exactly $B^p$.

\item \textup{Brownian diffusion perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=aW_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt a W_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =m_p T^{p/2}|a-\wt a|^p,
\]
where $m_p=\E|N(0,1)|^p$. Since $A=T^{1/2}|a-\wt a|$, this is $m_p A^p$.

\item \textup{Stable jump coefficient perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=\sigma Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt\sigma Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =\E|Z_1|^p T^{p/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|^p.
\]
Since $S=T^{1/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|$, this is $\E|Z_1|^pS^p$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, when $\wt\eta=1$, the powers $|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}$, $B^{\alpha-1}$, $A^{\alpha-1}$ and $S^{\alpha-1}$ agree with the exact scaling of the four elementary perturbation mechanisms.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.095757+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_38430903f04739b9e46f1d610337b43c6cb71b7bdfc1a0a2a320a758f0a6e1a3","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $\Phi$ be a $\sigma$-continuous non-negative stationary
  isotropic ID valuation with independent increments and vanishing
  deterministic part. Then there exist a non-negative infinitely
  divisible random variable $\xi$ and independent non-negative
  stationary isotropic ID valuations $\Psi_m$, $m=1,\dots,d$, with
  independent increments, such that
  \begin{displaymath}
    \Psi(K)
    =
    \xi\1_{K\neq\emptyset}
    +
    \sum_{m=1}^d\Psi_m(K),
    \qquad K\in\Kd,
  \end{displaymath}
  is weakly equivalent to $\Phi$. Moreover, $\Psi_m$ is
  $m$-stable in argument for every $m=1,\dots,d$.
  
  More precisely, there exist non-negative measures
  $b_0,\dots,b_d$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfying \eqref{eq:theta-levy}
  such that
  \begin{equation}
    
    \nu(\sC_K\times A)
    =
    \sum_{m=0}^d V_m(K)b_m(A),
    \qquad K\in\Kd,
  \end{equation}
  for every Borel $A\subset(0,\infty)$, where
  $V_0(K)=\1_{K\neq\emptyset}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:25:06.200908+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3868ed49fdf830327ebcf31c5da52e30f470519cbe34592632474628329eb581","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] Fix real numbers $\alpha\ge 1$ and $T>0$, and integers $n\ge0$ and $n_0>0$. $\cW(n,T)=\setcond{m\ge n}{\tau(n,m)\le T}$.  Then, for every $m\in\cW(n,T)$,
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0+1
        \le
        e^{T/\alpha}(n+n_0+1).
        
\end{equation}

If $m_\vee=\max\cW(n,T)$ and $\alpha_{n+1}\le T/2$, then the end time satisfies
\begin{equation}
        \frac{T}{2}
        \le
        \tau(n,m_\vee)
        \le
        T.
        
\end{equation}

If either $T=1/4$ and $n+n_0\ge8$, or
$T=1/5$ and $n+n_0\ge10$, then
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0

        \quad \forall m\in\cW(n,T).
        
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.360578+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_3886ad8530baeb3a3681c5a268cbb86bf82b63c3a3aa5a6382e8733a6fb1dffa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 256 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In both the spherical and Ising settings, there exists $c>0$ and $C = C(\alpha) > 0$ such that the following holds.
    Let $\cA^\circ$ be a $L$-Lipschitz algorithm with $L\ge 1$.
    Let $\chi^\circ \equiv \chi_{\cA^\circ}$ and $q_0 \equiv \chi^\circ(0)$, and suppose $q_0 < 1$.
    Then, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA$ such that the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item $\chi \equiv \chi_{\cA}$ satisfies $\chi(0) = q_0$ and
    \[
        \chi'(0) \ge  \frac1{L^2}\,.
    \]
In fact, we can take
    \[
        \chi(p) = \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p)+ \frac{q_0 + (1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\item 
The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ approximates the original algorithm $\cA^\circ$ in the sense that
    \[
        \frac{1}{N} \E\Big[\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\|^2\Big]
        \le \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\end{enumerate}
We remark that the above error should be considered small, since we will prove later in Lemma~\ref{l:sM.Lip.1.trivial} that a sequence of algorithms with $q_0$ tending to one can only achieve the gaussian distribution.

\begin{proof} 
Let $\dot{\bg}$ be a standard gaussian in $\bbR^N$ independent of $\bg^{\aux}$, and
let $\bv$ be a deterministic element of $S_N$ with 
 $(\bv,\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})) = 0$. The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ is defined by
    \[\cA(\bG, (\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) 
        = \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}
            \bigg\}^{1/2}
        \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) 
        + \bigg(\frac{q_0}{1-q_0}\bigg)^{1/2} \frac{\bv}{L}
        + \frac{\dot{\bg}}{L} \,.
    \]
Then the gradient of $\cA$ can be bounded as
    \begin{align*}
        \|\nabla\cA
            (\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg})) \|^2
        &= \|\nabla_{\bG,\bg^{\aux}}
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) \|^2
        + \|\nabla_{\dot{\bg}} 
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg})) \|^2 \\
        &\le \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0) L^2}   \bigg\} L^2 
            + \frac1{L^2}
        \le L^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Since $\bv$ is deterministic and orthogonal to $\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$,
 $\dot{\bg}$ is independent of $(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$, and $\bbE[\|\dot{\bg}\|^2] = N$, we have
    \[\frac{\bbE[
             \|\cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg}))\|^2]}{N}
    =\bigg\{ 1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg\}
    	+\frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2}
	+\frac{1}{L^2}
    = 1\,,
    \]
where the last step follows from the trivial inequality $1-q_0\le1\le L^2$.  The above two displays show that $\cA$ is an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}. Moreover, recalling the abbreviations $\chi\equiv\chi_\cA$ and $\chi^\circ\equiv\chi_{\cA^\circ}$, for any $0\le p\le1$ we have
    \[\chi(p) 
    = \bigg(1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p) + \frac{q_0+(1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,,
    \]
which implies $\chi(0)=q_0$.
   As noted above, $\chi^\circ$ is nondecreasing, which implies $\chi'(0)\ge 1/L^2$. This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.CHI}. 

Next, since $|a^{1/2}-b^{1/2}| \le |a-b|^{1/2}$ for all $a,b\ge0$, we can bound
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{N} \E\bigg[\Big\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\Big\|^2\bigg]
        &= \bigg(1 - \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg)^2
        + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2} \\
        &\le \frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2}
        = \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \end{align*}
This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.APPX}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu satisfies the FKG lattice condition, automatic for independent product measures but requiring verification for dependent Gibbs measures","f, g, or the events A, B, are both increasing, or both decreasing, with respect to the same partial order","the state space is finite or otherwise compactified so that all expectations involved are well defined"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.973188+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_38b7645fc7da6a9d085dab2a80793f9ef28cf412f7ea823995207adfbe1333e1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let mu be a probability measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) for all x, y, a condition automatically satisfied by any product measure on {0,1}^E, in which case the conclusion is called the Harris inequality. Then for any two increasing (or two decreasing) functions f, g in L^2(mu), E[fg] >= E[f]E[g]; equivalently, for increasing events A, B, mu(A ^ B) >= mu(A) mu(B), so increasing events are positively correlated. This is the basic monotone-coupling tool throughout percolation and interacting particle systems, lower-bounding joint probabilities of increasing events, such as several disjoint crossings occurring together, by the product of their individual probabilities, and it justifies a wide range of comparison and sprinkling arguments. It does not give any upper bound on the correlation, which requires separate and generally harder tools such as the van den Berg-Kesten inequality for disjoint occurrence; it does not apply to a mix of an increasing and a decreasing event without flipping a sign; and the strength of the positive correlation is not quantified beyond nonnegativity. Typical failure: Applying FKG to a pair of events where one is increasing and the other decreasing without flipping the sign, which reverses the direction of the inequality; or invoking FKG for a non-product Gibbs measure, such as a random-cluster model outside the ferromagnetic regime with cluster weight q<1, without checking the lattice condition, which is known to fail there. Canonical reference: Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre, 1971, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Harris, 1960, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society.","status":"unverified"}

We write $Q_{e,+}(\\cdot)=Q_e(\\cdot\\mid +1),  Q_{e,-}(\\cdot)=Q_e(\\cdot\\mid -1).$ The associated graphical channel is the channel from \\(\\{-1,+1\\}^V\\) to \\(\\prod_{e\\in E}\\mathsf Y_e\\) defined as follows: given \\(x=(x_v)_{v\\in V}\\in\\{-1,+1\\}^V\\), the edge observations \\((Y_e)_{e\\in E}\\) are conditionally independent, and for \\(e=\\{i,j\\}\\), $Y_e \\sim Q_e(\\cdot\\mid x_i x_j).$ We say that the edge channel \\(Q_e\\) is symmetric if there exists a measurable involution $T_e:\\mathsf Y_e\\to \\mathsf Y_e, T_e^{-1}=T_e,$ such that for every \\(A\\in\\mathcal A_e\\), \\[ Q_e(A\\mid +1)=Q_e(T_e(A)\\mid -1). \\] Equivalently, since \\(T_e\\) is an involution, \\[ Q_e(T_e(A)\\mid +1)=Q_e(A\\mid -1), \\qquad A\\in\\mathcal A_e. \\] The graphical channel is called symmetric if \\(Q_e\\) is symmetric for every \\(e\\in E\\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Ω ⊂ R^n open; derivatives taken in the distributional sense"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492362+00:00","domain":"Sobolev spaces, functional analysis for PDE","id":"claim_38c3cd05223b169021fe1f60a1ce84a3a15d39f588dd388ecea15bbf6fdb3634","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and k ≥ 1 an integer. W^{k,p}(Ω) is the set of u ∈ L^p(Ω) all of whose distributional derivatives D^α u with |α| ≤ k lie in L^p(Ω): for each α there is g_α ∈ L^p(Ω) with ∫_Ω u D^α φ dx = (−1)^{|α|} ∫_Ω g_α φ dx for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω); one writes D^α u = g_α (the weak derivative, unique a.e.). The norm is ||u||_{W^{k,p}} = ( Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ||D^α u||_{L^p}^p )^{1/p} (maximum over α for p = ∞). W^{k,p}(Ω) is a Banach space, separable for p < ∞ and reflexive for 1 < p < ∞. H^k(Ω) := W^{k,2}(Ω) is a Hilbert space with ⟨u, v⟩ = Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ∫_Ω D^α u D^α v dx. W^{k,p}_0(Ω) is the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{k,p}(Ω) (functions 'vanishing on the boundary' together with derivatives of order < k); H^1_0(Ω) := W^{1,2}_0(Ω). The Sobolev conjugate of p < n is p* = np/(n − p), i.e. 1/p* = 1/p − 1/n.\n\nFacts: C^∞(Ω) ∩ W^{k,p}(Ω) is dense in W^{k,p}(Ω) for p < ∞ and any open Ω (Meyers–Serrin); restrictions of C^∞(R^n) functions are dense when Ω is bounded with Lipschitz boundary; W^{k,p}_0(R^n) = W^{k,p}(R^n); for bounded Ω, W^{1,p}_0(Ω) is a proper closed subspace of W^{1,p}(Ω) (nonzero constants are excluded by the Poincaré inequality). On an interval, W^{1,p} functions have absolutely continuous representatives; in dimension n ≥ 2 a W^{1,p} function with p ≤ n can be unbounded and discontinuous. For a bounded Lipschitz domain, W^{1,∞}(Ω) is the space of Lipschitz functions on Ω̄.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:09:41.192539+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_38c908d6d617590f98221d7a1608eff9bf05db02ce35b5c55d59b799004eb09e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In computational complexity theory, NP-complete problems are the hardest of the problems to which solutions can be verified quickly. Somewhat more precisely, a problem is NP-complete when:It is a decision problem, meaning that for any input to the problem, the output is either \"yes\" or \"no\". Each input to the problem is associated with a collection of short solutions, which might or might not validly solve the input. The output is \"yes\" when at least one of these solutions is valid, and \"no\" when none of them are. The validity of each solution can be verified quickly, and a brute-force search algorithm can find a valid solution by trying all possible solutions. The problem can be used to simulate every other problem for which we can verify quickly that a solution is valid. Hence, if we could find valid solutions of some NP-complete problem quickly, we could quickly find valid solutions for every other problem in which a given solution can be easily verified.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["pointwise form: u ∈ C^2(Ω) (or H^2_loc, a.e.)","integrated form: Ω bounded with Lipschitz boundary, u ∈ C^2 up to the boundary or u ∈ H^2(Ω)","eigenvalue formula: additionally u = 0 on ∂Ω and −Δu = λu in Ω"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492269+00:00","domain":"elliptic PDE, Rellich and Pohozaev identities, Dirichlet eigenvalues","id":"claim_39490348519396f0628002960648e225d47916ef40d2fa4016bd80557364979d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Pointwise identity. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, x the position vector, and u ∈ C^2(Ω). Then, everywhere in Ω,
   div( (x·∇u) ∇u − (1/2)|∇u|^2 x ) = (x·∇u) Δu − ((n−2)/2) |∇u|^2.
The same holds almost everywhere for u ∈ H^2_loc(Ω) (all terms are then in L^1_loc). Replacing x by x − x_0 for any fixed x_0 gives the same identity (translation invariance).

Integrated form (Rellich). Let Ω be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, ν the outward unit normal, dS surface measure, and u ∈ C^2(Ω̄), or u ∈ H^2(Ω) with the boundary integrals read through the L^2(∂Ω) traces of ∇u. Then
   ∫_Ω (x·∇u) Δu dx = ((n−2)/2) ∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx + ∫_∂Ω [ (x·∇u)(∂_ν u) − (1/2)|∇u|^2 (x·ν) ] dS.

Dirichlet case. If in addition u = 0 on ∂Ω (trace sense), then the tangential gradient vanishes on ∂Ω, ∇u = (∂_ν u) ν there, and the boundary term collapses to (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS. If moreover −Δu = λu in Ω, then
   λ ∫_Ω u^2 dx = (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS,
the Rellich formula expressing a Dirichlet eigenvalue by a boundary integral; equivalently 2λ||u||^2_{L^2(Ω)} = ∫_∂Ω (x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 dS. For a domain star-shaped with respect to the origin (x·ν ≥ 0 on ∂Ω) the right side is nonnegative term by term. The same computation with −Δu = f(u), u = 0 on ∂Ω, is the Pohozaev identity.

Where it fails / hypotheses that matter. The integrated form needs enough regularity to give ∇u a boundary trace: u ∈ H^2(Ω) (or C^2 up to the boundary). A Dirichlet eigenfunction on a Lipschitz domain that is not convex (a re-entrant corner) need not belong to H^2(Ω), and the identity is then not available in this form without a separate justification. Without u = 0 on ∂Ω the tangential gradient contributes and the simplified boundary term (1/2)∫(x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 is wrong: the full bracket must be kept. The sign of x·ν is not fixed for a general domain, so conclusions that use x·ν ≥ 0 (star-shapedness, Pohozaev-type nonexistence) fail otherwise. In dimension n = 2 the interior term ((n−2)/2)∫|∇u|^2 vanishes. The identity is for the Laplacian; for a variable-coefficient operator div(A∇u) extra terms involving x·∇A appear.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:04:59.433232+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39be3c07534955c5163b8128720d3b73788c3c3481893d240c3fd2ff56867b28","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:ito-centered-lyapunov-differential of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Let \(p\geqslant2\), and assume the conditions of (assump:centered-decay of the paper).
Let
\[
    L_p(t):=L_p(\mathcal X_t^J,\mathcal V_t^J)
\]
denote the pathwise centered Lyapunov functional defined in
(equation eq:random-Lp-def of the paper) for \(p>2\), and in (equation eq:random-L2-def of the paper) for \(p=2\).

Define the local martingale \(M_{p,t}:=J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^J M_{p,t}^j\) by
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d M_{p,t}^j
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        2\left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac5\gamma
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        p|\hat Z_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac m\gamma |Y_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then there exists a local martingale \(M_{p,t}\) such that, in the sense of semimartingale differentials,
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\lambda_p L_p(t)\,\mathrm d t+\mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    \lambda_p
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        \frac{\min\{v_1,v_3\}}{c_2^{(2)}},
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        \frac{p\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{4\gamma},
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Here, for \(p=2\),
\[
    v_1:=\frac1{m\gamma}+\frac3{\gamma^3}-K_\sigma,
    \qquad
    v_3:=\frac{2\gamma}{m}-\frac3\gamma,
\]
and \(c_2^{(2)}\) is the upper norm-equivalence constant associated with \(\psi_2\).

Moreover, when \(p>2\), the stronger componentwise estimate holds:
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\widehat\lambda_Y
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |Y_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    -\widehat\lambda_Z
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |\hat Z_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    +
    \mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    &:=
    \frac1\gamma
    \left[
        C_{\mathrm{pos}}
        -
        \gamma\left(\frac2m+\frac1{\gamma^2}\right)
        \left(\frac4\gamma\right)^{p-1}
        +
        \frac{m(p-1)}{\gamma^2}
    \right],
    \\
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    &:=
    p\left(\frac\gamma m+\frac1\gamma\right)
    -
    \left(
        \frac{p-1}{2m}\gamma+\frac{p-1}{4\gamma}
    \right)
    -
    \frac{2m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    -
    \Lambda_p\sigma^{\frac{2p}{p-2}}\gamma^{\frac2{p-2}}\,,
    
\end{align}
where $C_{\mathrm{pos}} = 1-\frac{3\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{16} - \frac{m(p-1)(p-2)}p$ as defined from (equation eq:Cpos-def of the paper). Under (assump:centered-decay of the paper), these coefficients satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        a_p+\frac{m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    \right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        1+\frac{m}{p\gamma}
    \right).
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:52:08.670984+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39c92a21ce09e808fb46f2dd1cc54ccba0953444b48886fc35c59e2aadc175f0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 27 (Block contraction theorem) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Under the standing fixed-threshold application, fix \(\delta_0\geq c_0\).
There are constants
\[
        T_{\mathrm{blk}}<\infty,\qquad
        \eta_{\mathrm{blk}}>0,\qquad
        \theta_{\mathrm{blk}}>0,\qquad
        \Lambda_*<\infty
\]
with the following property.  The constants
\(\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\Lambda_*\) depend only on
\(K,\delta_0,N,\sigma\).  The start-time threshold \(T_{\mathrm{blk}}\) may
additionally depend on the fixed Bamler tail data \(T_B(c_0)\) and
\(\eps_B^{c_0}\) for the given flow.

Let \(p(\tau)\) be a parabolically rescaled \(\delta_0\)-large block starting
at \(S\geq T_{\mathrm{blk}}\), fix a torus fibration \(\pi:M\to S^1\), and put
\[
        q(1)=p(1),\qquad r(1)=\overline{q(1)}.
\]
Suppose that \(r(1)\) is Riemannian and, with
\[
 b=\|q(1)-r(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r(1))},
 \qquad d=d_{\TT^2}(r(1)),
\]
one has
\[
        b<\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        d<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r(1);\Lambda_*).
\]
Equivalently, \((q(1),r(1))\) is an admissible stage start in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-stage-start}, with constants
\(\Lambda_*,\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\theta_{\mathrm{blk}}\).
Then the invariant Ricci flow \(r\) and the Ricci--DeTurck flow \(q\) relative
to it exist on \([1,100]\).  At the rescaled endpoint, put
\[
        q^+(1)=100^{-1}q(100),\qquad
        \rho^+=100^{-1}r(100),\qquad
        r^+(1)=\overline{q^+(1)},
\]
and set
\[
        b^+=\|q^+(1)-r^+(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r^+(1))}.

Then \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian and
\begin{equation}
        b^+\leq\tfrac12 b,\qquad
        d_{\TT^2}(r^+(1))<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*).

Ricci flow corresponding to \(q\) is \(p\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.162189+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39ef52ee75249f5f440b1e1246bef6c63616758f5dffa470be1204a3dd78e398","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Cor 17 (\cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $A,b,C,d$ as in Theorem~\ref{t:hoffman} with $(b,d)\in F(A,C)$.
Let $B(M_0)$ denote the ball of radius $M_0$ in $\R^n$, centered at the origin.
\begin{enumerate}[a.]
\item  Suppose $(b',d')\in F(A,C)$, and
suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S_{A,C}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then
	\[d_H\Big(S_{A,C}(b,d),S_{A,C}(b',d')\Big)
	\le c\left\| \begin{pmatrix}
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$.
\item 
Now suppose we have $(A,b,C,d)'$ of the same dimensions,
with $(b',d')\in F(A',C')$. 
Suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S\equiv S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S'\equiv S_{A',C'}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then, for any $x'\in S'$ there exists $x\in S$ with
	\[\|x-x'\|_2
	\le c \left\| \begin{pmatrix} A-A'\\ C-C'\\
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\,,
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$, and on the right-hand side we treat $A$ and $C$ as vectors of length $mn$ and $qn$ respectively.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $x'\in S'$. Then
	\[
	Ax'-b
	=[A'+(A-A')] x'- [b' + (b-b')]
	\le (A-A')x'-(b-b')\,,
	\]
from which it follows that
	\[
	\|(Ax'-b)_+\|
	\le \| [(A-A')x'-(b-b')]_+\|
	\le \|A-A'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|b-b'\|\,.
	\]
Similarly, we can bound
	\[
	\|Cx'-d\|
	\le \|C-C'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|d-d'\|\,.
	\]
The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so the conclusion of part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty} follows.
Part \eqref{i:hoffman.rhs} then follows from part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The standard thirteen-graph cubic distance-regular classification.","The values are reported computations from the campaign record."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.364653+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_39f9c09b53339b708c3cfa454baf0d76df290fd6db9f1e7d7a2a93b62a11785e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14; values computed exactly from the intersection-array identity tau_0 = k sum_{i=1}^d (k_i+...+k_d)/(k_i c_i). That identity was checked against a direct linear-algebra solve on twelve graphs, among them the cubic graphs K_{3,3}, Q_3, Petersen, Heawood, Pappus, Desargues and the dodecahedron, with the complete graph and the cycle as independent controls.] This is the cubic case of Open Problem 7.31 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). For a finite connected simple distance-regular graph G with n vertices, let tau_0 = max_{x,y} E_x[T_y] for simple random walk. By the known classification, there are exactly thirteen cubic (valency-three) distance-regular graphs. Their (n, tau_0) values are: K_4 (4, 3); K_{3,3} (6, 6); cube Q_3 (8, 10); Petersen (10, 12); Heawood (14, 19); Pappus (18, 27); Desargues (20, 65/2); dodecahedron (20, 35); Coxeter (28, 45); Tutte-Coxeter (30, 48); Foster (90, 675/4); Biggs-Smith (102, 195); Tutte 12-cage (126, 234). Hence, given the classification, the maximum of tau_0/(n-1) over all cubic distance-regular graphs is 195/101 (about 1.9307), attained uniquely by the Biggs-Smith graph. This reproduces exactly the value Aldous and Fill attribute to Biggs and settles, for valency three, Biggs's outlined claim that it is the largest. The general O(n) conjecture over non-cycle distance-regular graphs is not settled by this computation. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}
