{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:10:07.529597+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7ba4a3df5386842b2c4221fb83a0783e036705f503467d2b1ca11633b8d4c27d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition eq:sparse-profile-net-bound of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:sharp-profile-energy}
Suppose that the random field satisfies \(({\rm PT})_p\).
Put
\[
 \pi_N(a):=
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1)}
 \mathbb P\{\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert\ge a\}.
\]
Put
\[
 \mathcal S_{N,k}
 =\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
       \abs{\operatorname{supp}x}\le k\},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_p=\frac{p^{p+1}}{p!}.
\]
For \(1\le k\le N\), \(a>0\), and
\(0<\delta<\Lambda_p^{-1}\),
\begin{align}
 &\mathbb P\left\{
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal S_{N,k}}\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert\ge a
 \right\}\notag\\
 &\qquad\le
 \binom Nk\left(1+\frac2\delta\right)^k

\end{align}
Consequently, if \(1\le k_N\le N\), \(k_N=o(N)\), and
\(a_N\to a>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb P\left\{
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal S_{N,k_N}}\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert
 \ge a_N\right\}
 \le-\frac{a^2}{2}.
\end{equation}
The same conclusions hold for the standard symmetric-coordinate model
whenever its field satisfies \(({\rm PT})_p\); the profile MGF and

{"assumptions":["Coupled n>=2 scalar h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), 0<a_i<b_i, b_i,kappa_i>0; logistic average loss; simultaneous Euclidean GD. A=mean h_i(p_bar)^2/4, B=mean h_i'(p_bar)/2, mean h_i(p_bar)=0. Exact normal linear-stability classification of every finite fixed point of joint-head factored-attention GD at every eta>0: the stationary curve v=0,kq=p_bar has tangent multiplier 1 and normal multipliers 1-eta lambda_+/- with lambda_+/-=(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2(k^2+q^2)))/2. One normal direction is always repelling; the other attracts exactly when k^2+q^2<(4/eta^2-2A/eta)/B^2, is neutral at equality, and repels beyond. Every positive fixed step loses the attracting normal direction at sufficiently unbalanced factorizations.

# Target 1: exact normal stability of the factored GD stationary curve

Version 1, proof unaudited. This is a linearized stability classification;
it does not claim a nonlinear flip bifurcation or a full-space GD basin theorem.

Assume precisely the n-example factored model of claim 010:
0<a_i<b_i, b_i,kappa_i>0, logistic average loss of
v h_i(kq), h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), and simultaneous Euclidean GD
with any fixed eta>0. Let p_bar<0 be the unique mean root and define

 A=mean_i h_i(p_bar)^2/4>=0,
 B=mean_i h_i'(p_bar)/2>0.

All finite stationary points, equivalently all GD fixed points, form the
curve E={v=0,kq=p_bar}. At such a point write S=k^2+q^2>=2|p_bar|.
The GD Jacobian has tangent multiplier 1 and normal multipliers

 mu_-=1-eta lambda_-, mu_+=1-eta lambda_+,
 lambda_+/-=(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2 S))/2.

Here lambda_-<0<lambda_+, hence mu_->1 everywhere: no point of E is
linearly attracting in all normal directions. The other normal direction is

* strictly attracting in the linearization when eta lambda_+<2;
* neutral with multiplier -1 when eta lambda_+=2;
* strictly repelling with multiplier less than -1 when eta lambda_+>2.

Let
 J_eta=(4/eta^2-2A/eta)/B^2.

The first case is EXACTLY S<J_eta, the middle case exactly S=J_eta,
and the last exactly S>J_eta. Equivalently, with C=k^2-q^2,
S=sqrt(C^2+4p_bar^2): there is an attracting normal direction only if
J_eta>2|p_bar|, and then precisely at

 |C|<sqrt(J_eta^2-4p_bar^2).

Equality gives neutral normal points when J_eta>=2|p_bar|. If J_eta
is smaller than 2|p_bar|, every point is repelling in both normal directions.
In particular, for EVERY eta>0, sufficiently unbalanced factorizations on
E are normally repelling in both directions. There is no positive constant
step that preserves the flow's one attracting normal direction uniformly
along the entire stationary curve. This does NOT imply an open basin of
cycles or disprove a full-space almost-everywhere GD endpoint theorem.

## Proof

The fixed-point condition is gradient L=0, classified in proof 008.
Its loss Hessian at E is
 [[A,-Bq,-Bk],[-Bq,0,0],[-Bk,0,0]].
The tangent vector (0,k,-q) is in its kernel. In the orthonormal basis
e_v=(1,0,0), e_s=(0,q,k)/sqrt(S) of the normal plane, the Hessian is
 [[A,-B sqrt(S)],[-B sqrt(S),0]].
The quadratic characteristic polynomial is lambda^2-A lambda-B^2 S,
which yields lambda_+/- and their signs. The GD Jacobian is I-eta Hessian,
proving the multipliers and their linear classifications.

For equivalence with J_eta, consider the polynomial
f(z)=z^2-Az-B^2 S, whose positive zero is lambda_+ and negative zero
lambda_-. Since 2/eta>0, lambda_+<2/eta is equivalent to
f(2/eta)>0, or S<J_eta; equality and the reverse inequality follow likewise.
This avoids squaring a potentially negative expression 4/eta-A.
Finally S^2=C^2+4p_bar^2 by algebra, and S is unbounded along E by
taking k->infinity, q=p_bar/k. All asserted threshold statements follow.

## Scope of the obstruction

The obstruction is to a PARTICULAR transfer from flow to GD: retaining
one attracting normal direction uniformly on every imbalance leaf at fixed
step. It is not an obstruction to every possible discrete-time proof.
The imbalance leaves themselves are not invariant under GD:
C_+=(1-eta^2 v^2 G^2)C. Both facts must be accounted for in further work.
Normal multipliers on the unit circle require separate nonlinear analysis;
no attracting two-cycle is claimed. Scalar genuine self-attention embeddings
of this family are supplied in claim 008.","status":"unverified"}

Failure at alpha = 0 (continuous right-hand side does not give a C^2 solution): in the plane put u(x) = (x_1^2 - x_2^2) (log(1/r))^{1/2} for 0 < r = |x| < 1/2, u(0) = 0. A computation with u = p g, p = r^2 cos(2 theta) harmonic and g = (log(1/r))^{1/2}, using Laplacian(p g) = 4 p g'/r + p (g'' + g'/r), gives Laplacian u = -cos(2 theta) ( 2 (log(1/r))^{-1/2} + (1/4)(log(1/r))^{-3/2} ), which extends continuously by 0 at the origin, while D_{11}u = 2(log(1/r))^{1/2} + o(1) blows up. Since u is C^1 and C^infinity off the origin, it solves Laplacian u = f distributionally on the ball with f continuous; no C^2 solution of Laplacian v = f exists near 0, because v - u would be harmonic hence smooth. (Consistently, this f is continuous but not Dini continuous, and Dini continuity is the correct substitute hypothesis.) Failure at alpha = 1: with q = x_1^3 - 3 x_1 x_2^2 and g = log(1/r), the function u = q g has Laplacian u = -6 q/r^2 = -6 r cos(3 theta), which is Lipschitz, while D_{111}u = 6 log(1/r) + O(1) is unbounded, so u is not in C^{2,1}. Failure at p = infinity: u = (x_1^2 - x_2^2) log(1/r) has Laplacian u = -4 cos(2 theta) in L^infinity while D_{11}u = 2 log(1/r) + O(1) is not bounded, so Laplacian u in L^infinity does not give u in W^{2,infinity} = C^{1,1}; the correct endpoint statement is Laplacian u in L^infinity implies D^2 u in BMO. Failure at p = 1: let f_k = rho_{1/k} be standard mollifiers and u_k = Gamma convolved with f_k, so Laplacian u_k = f_k with ||f_k||_{L^1} = 1 and ||u_k||_{L^1(B_2)} bounded; on B_1 minus the origin D_{12}u_k converges pointwise to D_{12}Gamma, whose size is comparable to |x|^{-n} and hence not integrable near 0, so by Fatou ||D^2 u_k||_{L^1(B_1)} tends to infinity. No estimate of the form ||D^2u||_{L^1} <= C(||Laplacian u||_{L^1} + ||u||_{L^1}) can hold; the correct endpoint statements are weak-L^1 bounds and the Hardy space result Laplacian u in H^1 implies D^2u in L^1. Practical consequence: from f merely continuous (or bounded) one gets u in W^{2,p}_loc for every finite p and u in C^{1,alpha}_loc for every alpha < 1, but not, in general, u in C^2 - the first example above is exactly the obstruction (for particular right-hand sides, a smooth f say, the solution is of course C^2).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Omega is a bounded open subset of R^N, N >= 2 (N >= 3 for the exponent N/(N-2) statements)","A(x) is measurable, uniformly elliptic and bounded: lambda |xi|^2 <= A xi . xi, |A xi| <= Lambda |xi|","homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition","part (I): f in L^m(Omega) with m > N/2","part (II): f in L^1(Omega) or a bounded Radon measure; solutions understood in Stampacchia's duality sense"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:23.250962+00:00","domain":"linear elliptic PDE, L^1 and measure data, regularity","id":"claim_7bba34209aa1de121daefe005a5bb783e1eb800331b4e677d6dbdf6096168f4d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Setting: $\\Omega \\subset \\mathbb{R}^N$ bounded open, $N \\geq 2$; $A(x)$ a measurable matrix field with $\\lambda|\\xi|^2 \\leq A(x)\\xi\\cdot\\xi$ and $|A(x)\\xi| \\leq \\Lambda|\\xi|$ for some $0 < \\lambda \\leq \\Lambda$ (uniform ellipticity, bounded measurable coefficients, no regularity); the Dirichlet problem $-\\operatorname{div}(A(x)\\nabla u) = f$ in $\\Omega$, $u = 0$ on $\\partial\\Omega$. (Stampacchia, Ann. Inst. Fourier 1965.) (I) $L^\\infty$ estimate. If $f \\in L^m(\\Omega)$ with $m > N/2$ (so $f \\in H^{-1}$ and the weak solution $u \\in H_0^1(\\Omega)$ exists and is unique), then $u \\in L^\\infty(\\Omega)$ and $\\|u\\|_{L^\\infty} \\leq C\\,\\|f\\|_{L^m}$ with $C = C(N, \\lambda, m, |\\Omega|)$. Sharp edge: the exponent is sharp - for $N \\geq 3$ there are $f \\in L^{N/2}(\\Omega)$ (even for $A = I$) whose solution is unbounded, e.g. $u = \\log|\\log|x||$ near the origin, whose Laplacian lies in $L^{N/2}$ but $u \\notin L^\\infty$; for $f \\in L^{N/2}$ one only gets $u$ in the Orlicz class $\\exp L$ (and $u \\in L^q$ for all $q < \\infty$). (II) $L^1$ and measure data. If $f \\in L^1(\\Omega)$ (or more generally $f = \\mu$ is a bounded Radon measure on $\\Omega$), there exists a unique DUALITY solution: a function $u \\in L^1(\\Omega)$ with $\\int_\\Omega u\\,g\\,dx = \\int_\\Omega w_g\\,d\\mu$ for every $g \\in L^\\infty(\\Omega)$, where $w_g \\in H_0^1(\\Omega) \\cap L^\\infty(\\Omega)$ is the weak solution of the adjoint problem $-\\operatorname{div}(A^{T}\\nabla w_g) = g$ (bounded by part (I), which is all that is needed to pair with $f \\in L^1$); for MEASURE data one needs $w_g$ continuous on $\\overline\\Omega$ so that $\\int w_g\\,d\\mu$ makes sense - interior continuity is De Giorgi-Nash-Moser, continuity up to the boundary requires a mild regularity of $\\partial\\Omega$ (e.g. Lipschitz, or an exterior cone condition), which is then an extra hypothesis in the measure case. This $u$ satisfies: $u \\in W_0^{1,q}(\\Omega)$ for EVERY $q < N/(N-1)$ with $\\|u\\|_{W_0^{1,q}} \\leq C(N,\\lambda,\\Lambda,q,\\Omega)\\,\\|\\mu\\|_{\\mathcal{M}}$ ($= \\|f\\|_{L^1}$ for $L^1$ data); $|\\nabla u|$ lies in the Marcinkiewicz (weak-$L$) space $M^{N/(N-1)}(\\Omega)$ and, for $N \\geq 3$, $u \\in M^{N/(N-2)}(\\Omega)$; $u$ is the strong $W_0^{1,q}$ limit of the weak solutions $u_n$ with smooth data $f_n \\to f$ in $L^1$ (or $f_n \\to \\mu$ weakly-* with $\\|f_n\\|_1$ bounded); $u$ solves the equation in the sense of distributions, $\\int A\\nabla u\\cdot\\nabla\\varphi = \\int \\varphi\\,d\\mu$ for $\\varphi \\in C_c^\\infty(\\Omega)$; and $T_k(u) \\in H_0^1(\\Omega)$ for every $k$ with $\\lambda\\int|\\nabla T_k(u)|^2 \\leq k\\|\\mu\\|$. Sharp edges: (a) $q = N/(N-1)$ is excluded and cannot be reached - for $\\mu = \\delta_0$ and $A = I$ the Green function has $|\\nabla u| \\sim |x|^{1-N}$, which is in $L^q$ near 0 iff $q < N/(N-1)$; (b) uniqueness holds among DUALITY solutions (equivalently among limits of approximations, or entropy/renormalized solutions), NOT among all distributional solutions in $W^{1,q}$, $q < N/(N-1)$: for merely measurable uniformly elliptic $A$ Serrin (1964) constructed, for any $1 < q < 2$, a nonzero $u \\in W^{1,q}(B)$ on a ball $B$ with $\\operatorname{div}(A\\nabla u) = 0$ distributionally and $u \\notin H^1_{loc}$ (a 'pathological solution'), so a distributional $W^{1,q}$ solution is not determined by its data without a selection principle such as duality, approximation, or the entropy/renormalized formulation; (c) with $L^1$ data the solution is in general NOT in $H_0^1$ (its energy is infinite), so the Lax-Milgram framework does not apply directly - the estimates are obtained on approximations via the truncation method and passed to the limit.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The affine-scaled free convolution powers converge weakly to C_1.","Free convolution is weakly continuous, and unimodal measures are weakly closed."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.365034+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7bd214bfc3c4fa222b61d570e908b0f27536370c30f308cdc774fd9de22b26b6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked] This is the proved attraction-domain extension of the partial answer to Problem 3.11 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A law lambda is freely strongly unimodal when lambda boxplus nu is unimodal for every unimodal nu. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

# Balanced opposite-head two-cycles: complete implicit parametrization

T328-W698-017 v1, Target 1, proof (unaudited).

Consider L(v,k,q)=log(1+exp(-v h(kq))), h(s)=a+b*tanh(kappa*s),
0<a<b, kappa>0 and simultaneous Euclidean GD with fixed eta>0.
For this scalar signed link, every balanced period-two orbit whose heads have
opposite signs is covered by the following construction, up to interchanging
the two phases and simultaneously negating both factors. The construction
parametrizes cycles across the data/step parameters; for prescribed a,b,kappa,
eta these parameter equalities are necessary and sufficient, not a claim that
every prescribed model has such a cycle.

## Construction from four positive parameters

Choose 0<r<1 and T,y0,kappa>0. Define

    A=tanh T, B=tanh(r^2*T),
    D=cosh(T)^2/cosh(r^2*T)^2,
    sig(y)=1/(1+exp(-y)), f(y)=y*sig(y)^2.

There is a unique y1>0 solving

    f(y1)=f(y0)/(r*D).

Indeed f'(y)=sig(y)^2*[1+2y*(1-sig(y))]>0 on y>0,
and f increases continuously from 0 to infinity. Put

    g0=sig(y0), g1=sig(y1), c=g0/g1,
    t=y1/(y0*c),
    v0=sqrt((1-r)*(A-B)/((1+t)*(1+c)*kappa*sech(T)^2)),
    H0=y0/v0, H1=c*H0,
    b=H0*(1+c)/(A-B), a=b*A-H0,
    eta=v0*(1+t)/(g0*H0), w=sqrt(T/kappa).

All denominators are strictly positive. Also a/b=(c*A+B)/(1+c) lies
strictly between B and A, hence 0<a<b. These parameters give the exact
period-two orbit

    (v0,w,-w) <-> (-t*v0,r*w,-r*w).

The two signed margins are -y0 and -y1. In particular the logistic factors
are exactly g0 and g1, not factors obtained from a limiting approximation.

## Verification

h(-w^2)=-H0 and h(-r^2*w^2)=H1. Thus g0*H0=g1*H1 and
the two head increments are respectively -v0*(1+t) and v0*(1+t).
Let d0=b*kappa*sech(T)^2, d1=b*kappa*sech(r^2*T)^2=D*d0.
The first factor coefficient is

    delta0=eta*v0*g0*d0
          =v0^2*(1+t)*(1+c)*kappa*sech(T)^2/(A-B)=1-r.

For the second coefficient, the scalar equation gives

    t*(g1/g0)*D = y1*g1^2*D/(y0*g0^2)=1/r.

Consequently delta1=eta*(-t*v0)*g1*d1=-(1-r)/r=1-1/r.
On k=-q the factor multipliers 1-delta0=r and 1-delta1=1/r
return the factors exactly. The head changes sign, so the orbit is nonfixed.

## Completeness within the stated class

Balance means k^2=q^2. If k=q, the product is nonnegative, h(kq)>0,
and the head strictly increases at every finite point, so there is no finite
cycle. If k=q=0 the same argument applies. Thus a balanced cycle must lie
on k=-q with nonzero k. Interchange phases so v0>0>v1 and simultaneously
negate both factors so k0=w>0. Since delta_j=eta*v_j*g_j*h'_j,
delta0>0>delta1. The returning-factor equation is

    (1-delta0)*(1-delta1)=1.

The second factor is >1; therefore 0<1-delta0<1. Write this number r.
It follows that k1=r*w and delta1=1-1/r. In particular no factor sign flip
is possible for an opposite-head balanced two-cycle in this class.
The head update v1-v0<0 forces h0<0, and the reverse update forces h1>0.
Set H0=-h0, H1=h1, t=-v1/v0, T=kappa*w^2,
y0=v0*H0, y1=t*v0*H1. These are positive. The equal and opposite
head increments imply H1/H0=g0/g1=c, whence t=y1/(y0*c).
Dividing the two factor coefficients gives r*D*f(y1)=f(y0).
The identities h1-h0=b*(A-B), delta0=1-r and the head increment then
recover precisely the formulas for b,a,v0,eta above. This proves completeness.

## Full Jacobian test and its present limit

The normal two-step multiplier is exactly

    mu_U=(1+delta0)*(1+delta1)=(2-r)*(2-1/r)=5-2r-2/r.

It satisfies |mu_U|<1 precisely for (3-sqrt(5))/2<r<1,
equals -1 at the left endpoint, and is <-1 below it. It is zero at r=1/2.
The other two multipliers are exactly the eigenvalues of J1*J0, using
the general balanced Jacobian given in proofs/014_opposite_head_cycles.md.
This is an exact formula for the full spectrum, but no uniform inequality
for that balanced block has been proved for unequal head magnitudes.

The reproducible script scripts/asymmetric_cycles.py sampled 576 choices:
r in {.1,.2,.35,.4,.5,.65,.8,.9,.98}, T in {.1,.3,.6,.9,1.3,2,3,5},
y0 in {.01,.1,.4,1,2,4,8,16}, with kappa=1. It solved the monotone
equation by floating-point bisection and differentiated the full 3D loss.
It found zero attracting candidates; the smallest observed full spectral
radius was approximately 8.9666956. The largest relative cycle residual was
approximately 2.56e-13. These are numerical evidence, not rigorous bounds,
and cannot establish instability throughout the parametrization.

Claim 016 proves full instability and the complete second-multiplier phase
diagram on the equal-head-magnitude subfamily r=1/2,
cosh(T)^2=2cosh(T/4)^2. The SINGLE remaining hard step for upgrading
the wider numerical finding to a theorem is a rigorous spectral-radius
inequality for J1*J0 throughout (r,T,y0)>0 with 0<r<1. This proof
does not claim that step or almost-everywhere factored-GD convergence.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:19:47.272105+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7c65d5f6b42d957359a385c83fae17c845d7b1786630ec0d59a0fd6787e8a37d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:pred_proj of arXiv:2601.09976, 'Stochastic Calculus as Operator Factorization:\\ An Operator--Covariant Derivative and Uni'] Assume that $\mathcal{H}_X$ consists of jointly measurable processes and that the predictable processes form a closed subspace of~$\mathcal{H}_X$. The \emph{predictable projection} $\Pi_X \colon \mathcal{H}_X \to \mathcal{H}_X$ is the orthogonal projection onto this subspace.

The closedness assumption is not automatic for an arbitrary energy space; it must be verified. In all examples of this paper, the predictable subspace is either all of~$\mathcal{H}_X$ (for It\^o integrals with respect to martingales and compensated Poisson processes, where $\mathcal{H}_X$ consists entirely of predictable processes) or is closed by standard results on conditional expectation.

For the integral-form energy spaces used throughout this paper---specifically, those where $u_t \in L^2(\Omega)$ for each~$t$ and the $\mathcal{H}_X$ inner product takes the form $\langle u, v \rangle_{\mathcal{H}_X} = \mathbb{E}[\int_0^T u_t v_t\, d\mu_t]$ for some positive measure $\mu$ on $[0,T]$ (possibly random, as with $d\langle X\rangle_t$)---the predictable projection admits the pointwise representation
\[
(\Pi_X u)_t = \mathbb{E}[u_t \mid \mathcal{F}_{t-}] \quad \text{for } t \in (0,T], \qquad (\Pi_X u)_0 = \mathbb{E}[u_0 \mid \mathcal{F}_0],
\]
where $\mathcal{F}_{t-}$ is the left-limit $\sigma$-algebra defined in Section~(sec:setup of the paper). This is the standard predictable projection of optional processes; see, e.g., [Revuz1999].","status":"unverified"}

(1D recurrence), and whether at those visits the second coordinate is 0 - not automatic. Great Picard theorem: if f is holomorphic on a punctured neighborhood of z_0 and z_0 is an essential singularity, then on every such punctured neighborhood f takes every complex value, with at most one exception, infinitely many times. The little theorem's transcendental case follows from the great one applied to g(z) = f(1/z) at its essential singularity 0.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:20:07.934802+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7c8804dc04acdd30b5c3268a49f84a533ce2ce1ac127821828d659a4897dd7ce","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:star of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Fix an atom $i$ and set $P_{ij}=\frac12p_jd_{ij}$ for $j\ne i$. Then
$\sum_jP_{ij}=1$, the valid star coefficients $B_{ij}$ lie on a real
two-dimensional affine plane through
$m_i$ with $\lVert m_i\rVert^2=\frac12|z_i|^2$, and
$\sum_jP_{ij}B_{ij}=m_i$; their variance is
$V_i=E+\frac{|z_i|^2}2-L_i$ where
$L_i=\sum_{j:t_j=t_i}p_j|z_j-z_i|^2\ge0$. Consequently there exist two star
neighbours whose segment contains a point $\delta$ with
\[
  \Wnorm\delta^2\ \le\ \frac E4+\frac{5|z_i|^2}8-\frac{L_i}4 ,

\begin{equation}
  \inf_{\substack{|\operatorname{supp} q|\le3\\ |\mu|<1}}C(q)\ \le\ \frac{7E}8,
  \qquad\text{so}\qquad \Gamma_3\le\frac78 .
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.019561+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7c8de4e093995b039958e81788fb199f30851900e52c191ad4bcea130ac5f8e8","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Write \(D(\cE)^*\) for the continuous anti-dual of the form domain.
With the preceding first-slot-linear convention, the standard Gelfand
triple is
\[
                 D(\cE)\subset L^2(\mathfrak m)\subset D(\cE)^*.
\]
Let $u:Z\to\C$ be holomorphic and globally Lipschitz.  For $s\le0$ set
\begin{equation}
                           U(s,x)=u(\Psi_{-s}x).
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
                         \|U(s)\|_{L^2(\mathfrak m)}\le Ce^{-s/2},
                         \qquad s\le0,
\end{equation}
and on every finite interval $[s_0,s_1]\subset(-\infty,0]$,
\begin{equation}
 U\in L^2([s_0,s_1];D(\cE)),\qquad
 \partial_sU+A_{\rm form}U=0\quad\text{in }D(\cE)^*,
\end{equation}
where $\langle A_{\rm form}v,\phi\rangle=\cE(v,\phi)$ is the form
operator.  On $\Dom A$, $A_{\rm form}$ agrees with the self-adjoint
operator $A$.
Moreover $s\mapsto U(s)$ is continuous into $L^2(\mathfrak m)$ and
\begin{equation}
                              U(0)=e^{sA}U(s),
                              \qquad s<0.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:02.100476+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7c94a0d85d142dec295206ada5fc9e7b7d34ab4ab7b51a8e359cab35f836e017","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 11 (CLT for the normalized traces) of arXiv:2604.26499, 'Spectrum of Random Matrices with Exploding Moments'] Let $C_N$ be the random circulant matrix satisfying

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:04:07.028572+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7ca31d3826e184062766df94b9df84d479b8435345ed91593519cc909daa6147","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:ising-cavity of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] On the tree of Definition~(def:ising-rpc of the paper), let

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:30:08.198444+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7ca84d2e39642a45d6c97a354b7bbc5a7ab036ae56c67400b50142b3c153ec7e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary of arXiv:2608.13452, 'Wasserstein stability of the zero cell of a Poisson hyperplane tessellation under directio'] Let $\hat{f}^{(1)}_{\gamma, n}$ and $\hat{f}^{(2)}_{\gamma, n}$ be the estimators of a density $f$ as defined in Proposition (prop:density-robust of the paper).

    $\hat{g}_{\gamma,n}^{(1)}$ and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.224684+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7cbb3f38cc9008fe5190d9cf358dd75d03cff1d730d6ac392c830054f5a49e49","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 14 (Asymptotics via Taylor Expansion) of arXiv:2608.14143, 'Mod-$\phi$ convergence for random variables with cyclotomic generating functions'] Let $s_N \in \N$ be a sequence of natural numbers and, for each $N\in\N$, let $(a_{N,j})_{j=1}^N$ be a sequence of natural numbers. Let $h(w, z) := \log\bigl(\frac{1-e^{zw}}{-zw}\bigr)$ for $w \neq 0$ and $h(0, z):=0$. For each $N \in \N$, set $\delta_{N,j} := a_{N,j}/s_N$. Assume that $\max_{1\le j \le N} \delta_{N,j} \to 0$ as $N\to\infty$ and that the limit
\[
\Sigma := \lim_{N\to\infty} \sum_{j=1}^N \delta_{N,j}

\[

\]
uniformly for $z\in K$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.179126+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7ceb1b95c0e64951a2d9f8f4b1393598463871053d23b3f68d1d750a84d515da","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 90 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recalling \eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym} and Definitions \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}--\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, we have
	\[\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha) \subseteq \sM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.\]

\begin{proof}
Consider any $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$, as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym}. 
    By Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.Lip.to.Lip.sym}, we can find $\tilde\mu \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha)$ with $\sym(\tilde\mu) = \mu$.
It was shown in the \hyperlink{p:thm.control.problems.main}{proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:control.problems.main}} that $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha) = \sM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0)$, so $\tilde\mu \in \sM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0)$.
Therefore, for any $\epsilon>0$ we can find $L>0$ and controls 
    \beq
        
        (q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
    \eeq
such that (recalling that $\sym$ is a contraction) we have
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu, \mu^{\sym}(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)\Big)
        \le\bbW_2\Big(\tilde \mu, \mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)\Big)
         \le \epsilon\,.
    \]
We see from Definitions~\ref{d:SDE.classification} and \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}
that the sets of controls $\Adm^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ and $\Adm^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ are in fact identical, so the controls \eqref{e:Lip.general.in.IAMP.sym.controls} belong to $\Adm^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$, and 
    \[
        \mu \in \cB_\epsilon\Big(\cM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\Big)\,.
    \]
    Since for all $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $L > 0$ so that this holds, we conclude $\mu \in \sM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0)$.
    As this holds for all $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$, the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H is a Hilbert space","T is a bounded linear operator on H"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:46.571526+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, operator ideals","id":"claim_7d3da9c3c18db6a4a1b175a83b3a4853fd1bc3c0008d3153ce0be80e2db8b984","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H be a Hilbert space. A bounded operator T on H is trace class (nuclear) if it is compact and ||T||_1 := sum_n s_n(T) < infinity. Equivalently: sum_i <|T| e_i, e_i> < infinity for some (hence every) orthonormal basis (e_i), where |T| = (T*T)^{1/2}, and this sum then equals ||T||_1; equivalently, T = AB with A and B Hilbert-Schmidt operators. The trace of a trace-class T is tr T = sum_i <T e_i, e_i>; this series converges absolutely for every orthonormal basis and its sum does not depend on the basis. The trace-class operators S_1(H) form a two-sided ideal of B(H) and a Banach space under ||.||_1, with ||T|| <= ||T||_2 <= ||T||_1; finite-rank operators are ||.||_1-dense in S_1(H); under the pairing (T, B) -> tr(TB), S_1(H) is isometrically the dual of the compact operators K(H) and the predual of B(H). For a positive operator T >= 0 the sum sum_i <T e_i, e_i> in [0, infinity] is basis-independent and is finite exactly when T is trace class; for operators that are not positive, convergence (even absolute convergence) of sum_i <T e_i, e_i> in one basis does not imply trace class.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:09:23.970559+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7d866816abb2b2313aa7d616a31898808b56fba17a93a631553e530e89563a86","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 (Anti-diagonal equilibria and stability) of arXiv:2607.22438, 'A deterministic scalar reduction for the phase transition in two interacting urns'] Let \(\alpha>1\). The point \(\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)\) is an equilibrium for every
\(p\in[0,1]\). 
If $0\le p<\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}$,
then there is a unique \(u_{\alpha,p}\in[0,1/2)\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 u=(1-p)h(u)+\frac p2 .
\end{equation}
The corresponding off-center anti-diagonal
equilibria are exactly
\[
 (u_{\alpha,p},1-u_{\alpha,p})\text{ and }
 (1-u_{\alpha,p},u_{\alpha,p}).
\]
If $ p\ge \frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}$,
there is no off-center equilibrium on the anti-diagonal.

Furthermore, there exists a unique number
\[
 p_{\mathrm{ad},*}=p_{\mathrm{ad},*}(\alpha)
 \in\left(0,\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}\right)
\]
such that, for \(0\le p<(\alpha-1)/\alpha\),
\[
 \lambda_+(u_{\alpha,p},1-u_{\alpha,p})
 \begin{cases}
 <0, & \text{if }0\le p<p_{\mathrm{ad},*},\\
 =0, & \text{if }p=p_{\mathrm{ad},*},\\
 >0, & \text{if }p_{\mathrm{ad},*}<p<\dfrac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Consequently, the off-center anti-diagonal equilibria are asymptotically stable for
\(0\le p<p_{\mathrm{ad},*}\) and unstable for
\(p_{\mathrm{ad},*}<p<(\alpha-1)/\alpha\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Counterexample: F(p,z,x) = p_1 (equation u_x = 0), Γ = {y=0}","Noncharacteristic condition: D_pF(p0,z0,x0)·ν(x0) ≠ 0","Compatibility (admissibility): F(p0,z0,x0) = 0 and p0 agrees with the tangential gradient of g on Γ","Even when the conditions hold, the conclusion is only local in a neighbourhood of the point"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.418512+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: first-order equations, method of characteristics","id":"claim_7d8c544f22ddfa6bc426587ded0c72b9450163a966ed4890aa02b90253645958","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: local solvability of F(Du,u,x) = 0 with u = g on Γ requires D_pF(p0,z0,x0)·ν(x0) ≠ 0, i.e. the characteristic direction must be transversal to the data surface; and the initial triple must be admissible (the tangential derivatives of g must match p0). If the surface is characteristic, existence can fail outright and uniqueness can fail catastrophically. Counterexample: the equation u_x = 0 in R^2 (F(p,z,x) = p_1, so D_pF = (1,0)) with data on Γ = { y = 0 }, whose normal is ν = (0,1): D_pF·ν = 0, so Γ is characteristic — indeed the characteristics are the horizontal lines y = const, which lie IN Γ. Every C^1 solution satisfies u(x,y) = u(0,y), so u(·,0) must be constant: if g is not constant there is NO solution in any neighbourhood of a point of Γ; if g ≡ c there are infinitely many solutions u(x,y) = h(y) with h ∈ C^1 arbitrary and h(0) = c. The same pathology occurs for u_t + u_x = 0 with data prescribed on the characteristic line { x = t }. Auditor's check: before invoking local existence by characteristics, compute D_pF·ν at the point in question; for quasilinear equations a(x,u)·Du = b this is a(x0,g(x0))·ν(x0) ≠ 0, and for the Cauchy problem u_t + H(x,Du) = 0 on { t = 0 } it is automatic (the coefficient of u_t is 1).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:52:08.664699+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7d8db8fd4c67bde605a9b558b98bcad5b75ed77bb6f06554007dda7f09dc8a1c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(M\) be a closed connected three-manifold which admits a locally
homogeneous metric modeled on one of \(\RR^3\), \(\Nil\), or \(\Sol\), and let
\(g(t)\), \(0\leq t<\infty\), be any immortal Ricci flow on \(M\).  In all
three cases, for every basepoint \(\widetilde m\in\widetilde M\) in the
universal cover, the lifted blowdown flows
\((\widetilde M,\widetilde m,s^{-1}\widetilde g(s\tau))\), \(\tau>0\),
converge as \(s\to\infty\) in the pointed Cheeger--Hamilton sense to a
homogeneous expanding Ricci soliton solution.  The compact
and lifted limits are as follows.
\begin{enumerate}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:10:07.424632+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7d922fc74e165300d4137e2753b638ed7631e6a80e9f43ecedeb9ceeee2e31a4","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem eq:bounded-block-max of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:bounded-block-counterexample}
Fix \(p\ge3\) and an integer \(r\ge2\).  There is a symmetric,
compactly supported probability law \(\mu\) with a \(C^\infty\) density
such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item \(\mu\) matches the standard Gaussian moments through order \(r\)
(hence is centered and has variance one);
\item for i.i.d.\ ordered-tensor entries with common law \(\mu\), there
is a compact interval \(B\subset(0,\infty)\) for which
\begin{align}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^J(B)
 &>\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^G(B),\\
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_N^J(B)
 &>\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_N^G(B).
\end{align}
The reflected local-minimum inequality holds on \(-B\).
\end{enumerate}
In particular, for every fixed \(\varepsilon\in[0,1/2)\),
\begin{equation}
 \max_{I\in[N]^p}|J_I|\le N^{1/2-\varepsilon}
 \qquad\text{almost surely for all sufficiently large \(N\)}.
\end{equation}
Thus an \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) entrywise cutoff, or even an
 \(N\)-independent entry bound, does not restore universality of the
 unregularized annealed count.  The obstruction in this theorem is a
 coherent block involving on the order of \(N^{1/p}\) coordinates,
 rather than a single quadratic-scale entry. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

In words, there is a flip $h_{t}(i)= h_{t-}(i)+2$ if and only if the Poisson clock at $\pi(i, h_t(i))$ rings at times $t$, and $h_t(j)=h_{t-}(i)+1$ for $j\in \{i-1, i+1\}\cap \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$.

        By using the same set of Poisson clocks, we get a coupling of half-space TASEPs with boundary parameter $\alpha$, started from all initial configurations and all times.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:09:41.184234+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_7dc9240e7c8f566b6d3327ed7f7de8dd0a953ebde0983e3fddd09748b5993bf7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In real analysis, the Riemann integral is a rigorous definition of the integral of a function on an interval. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:20.880849+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7dcb93c91b72dbbc704681fcb49b1f1be63d1effc3db4273f0d92be16d174472","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 17 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Let $\delta>0$ and, for $j\in\{1,2\}$, let $\chi_j : \C \to[0,1]$ be smooth functions such that 
\[
\1\{V\le \mu-\delta\} \le \chi_2 \le \1\{V\le \mu-\tfrac12\delta\}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\1\{|V- \mu| \le 2\delta\}\le  \chi_1 \le \1\{|V- \mu| \le 3\delta\}.
\]
Let $f : \C \to \R$ be a smooth bounded function, and let ${\rm f}_j:= f \chi_j$ for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ where \[\chi_3 :=(\chi_1+\chi_2-1)\1\{V<\mu\}.\] 
Then, for every $\alpha>0$,
\[\begin{aligned}
\Upsilon(f;\Pi_N) = \Upsilon({\rm f}_1;\Pi_N)+ \Upsilon({\rm f}_2;\Pi_N) - \Upsilon({\rm f}_3;\Pi_N) + \O(e^{-\alpha \sqrt{N}}). 
\end{aligned}\]
By construction, ${\rm f}_1 ,{\rm f}_3$ are smooth, supported in the bulk $\{V\le \mu-\tfrac12\delta\} $, and ${\rm f}_2$ is smooth, supported in a neighborhood of the boundary $\{|V- \mu| \le 3\delta\}$.","status":"unverified"}

	\[
	\E'\Big[\|\vX(1)-\vX^\trstar(1)\|^2\Big]
	\le O(\epsilon) + o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
uniformly in $N$.

\begin{proof} 
For $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$ we have $X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,a)=X^\sigma(\tau(a),a)$, with $\tau$ the stopping time defined by \eqref{e:trstar.stopping.time}. It follows that, for $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$, we have
	\[

	\le O(1)

	\max_{0\le d\le \dmax}

	\le O(\epsilon) +o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
where the last bound is by Proposition~\ref{p:max.X.process.on.trstar.stopped.event}. Similarly,
	\[
	\E'\Big[( X^\Ising(1)-X^{\trstar,\Ising}(1))^2\Big]
	\le O(1)
	\E'\bigg[
	\max_{0\le d\le \dmax}
	X^\Ising(q_d)^2;\tau^\Ising<1\bigg] 
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
again by Proposition~\ref{p:max.X.process.on.trstar.stopped.event}. The conclusion follows.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.302319+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7e31600f9d01adbc27be70f4366d322c49e3e0208945ef424711bec597ce2ad9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop nonlinear-regression-regularity of arXiv:2608.30382, 'Convergence rates for the RMSprop optimizer with full control of the hyperparameters'] Let $\mathcal V\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be nonempty and compact,
let $ r \in ( 0, \nicefrac{ 1 }{ 2 } ) $, $ \delta \in (0, \infty ) $,
and suppose that there exist nonempty compact sets
$ K_Z \subseteq \mathcal Z $ and $ K_Y\subseteq {\mathbb R}^m $ and a constant
$ B \in (0,\infty) $ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

\item
The random variables are compactly supported in the sense that
\begin{align}\begin{split} 
  {\mathbb P}\bigl( Z \in K_Z , \, Y \in K_Y \bigr) = 1 .
 \end{split}\end{align}

\item
For $ {\mathbb P}_Z $-almost every $ z \in K_Z $, the conditional law of $ Y $
given $ Z = z $ has a Lebesgue density~$ p_z $ satisfying
\bas{

  \| p_z \|_{ L^\infty } \le B .
}

\item
The map $ ( \theta, z ) \mapsto \Gamma^{ \theta }( z ) $ and, for every
$ i \in \{ 1, \dots, d \} $,
the map
$
  ( \theta, z ) \mapsto\frac{\partial\Gamma^\theta}{\partial\theta_i}( z )
$
are continuous on $ \mathcal V \times K_Z $.

\item
The coordinate derivatives satisfy the uniform moment lower bound
\bas{

D_r
=
\inf_{ \substack{ \theta \in \mathcal V } }
\inf_{
  1 \le i \le d
}
{\mathbb E}\biggl[
\Bigl|
\frac{\partial\Gamma^\theta}{\partial\theta_i}(Z)
\Bigr|^{r}
\biggr]
\ge \delta.
}
\end{enumerate}
Choose $R\in(0,\infty)$ such that $K_Y\subseteq B(0,R)$, let
$\omega_{m-1}$ denote the volume of the unit ball in ${\mathbb R}^{m-1}$, use the
convention $\omega_0=1$, and set
\bas{
\mu_r
&=\frac{\delta^{1/r}}{2B\omega_{m-1}R^{m-1}}
\left(\frac{1-2r}{1-r}\right)^{(1-r)/r},\\
C_X
&=\max_{\substack{\theta\in\mathcal V,\ z\in K_Z,\ y\in K_Y\\1\le i\le d}}
\left|
\left\langle
\frac{\partial\Gamma^\theta}{\partial\theta_i}(z),
\Gamma^\theta(z)-y
\right\rangle
\right|.
}
Then $\mu_r,C_X\in(0,\infty)$. The innovation $(X,U)$ defined in
(equation eq:nonlinear-regression-loss-innovation of the paper) is $(c_r,q_r)$-regular on
$\mathcal V$ with
\bas{
c_r
=\frac{(1-e^{-1})\mu_r^3}{8C_X},
\qquad
q_r=\frac{(1-e^{-1})\mu_r}{2C_X}.
}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Erdos-Renyi, or configuration-model-type with matching degree-tail conditions, random graph in the critical window p ~ 1/n + O(n^{-4/3})","a valid exploration (depth-first search) encoding of the graph as a walk whose excursions correspond to components","appropriate moment conditions, such as finite third moment of the degree for configuration models, for the walk-to-Brownian-motion scaling limit","the specific n^{2/3} spatial and n^{-1/3} time-window scaling matching the model's universality class"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.994489+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7e5a315b29b381b59e06b86854cbebd0263352263eaab7d90c296b7dfdfe42ac","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For the Erdos-Renyi random graph G(n,p) near the critical window p = 1/n + lambda n^{-4/3}, Aldous's exploration process encodes a depth-first search of the graph as a random-walk-like process Z_n(t) whose excursions above past running minima correspond exactly to the connected components, with excursion lengths equal to component sizes. After rescaling space by n^{-2/3} and time correspondingly, this process converges to a limiting process W(t) = B(t) + lambda t - t^2/2, a Brownian motion with parabolic drift, whose excursions above its running minimum encode the limiting rescaled sizes of the largest components in the critical window; the associated merging dynamics of component sizes as edges are added form the \"standard multiplicative coalescent\", a Markov process on sequences of masses matching the excursion structure. This gives the precise scaling limit, order n^{2/3} for the largest components with an explicit limiting joint law, for the Erdos-Renyi critical phase transition. It does not extend directly to other random graph models without re-deriving an analogous exploration or walk encoding, which may not exist in closed form, and the specific n^{2/3} spatial and n^{-1/3} time-window scaling is particular to models in the Erdos-Renyi (mean-field) universality class. Typical failure: Applying the Erdos-Renyi n^{2/3} critical scaling window and multiplicative-coalescent limit directly to a random graph model with heavy-tailed degrees, infinite third moment, or strong local clustering, where the correct scaling exponents and even the limiting process, as established for configuration models with power-law degree exponent tau in (3,4) by Bhamidi, van der Hofstad and van Leeuwaarden, differ substantially; universality of the Erdos-Renyi picture is a theorem for specific model classes, not a generic property of all critical random graphs. Canonical reference: Aldous, 1997, Annals of Probability; Aldous and Limic, 1998, Electronic Journal of Probability; Bhamidi, van der Hofstad and van Leeuwaarden, 2010, Annals of Probability.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.244384+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7e849a89e05e586e829dfdb4382ad9ba3072f135e4c510b8814e90ebaa811b30","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 (coefficient calculus) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $\Psi$ be real-analytic near the origin in a finite-dimensional matrix space. There is
$\delta_\Psi=\delta_\Psi(\Psi,n,s,v_{\rm A})>0$ such that, if
$\|M_1\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}+\|M_2\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}\le\delta_\Psi$, then
\begin{equation*}\tag{P}
\|\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(M_2)\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}
\ \le\ C_\Psi\|M_1-M_2\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}.
\end{equation*}
In particular
$\|\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(0)\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}\le C_\Psi\|M_1\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}$.

In addition, suppose that the pointwise ranges of $M_1,M_2$ lie in a fixed
compact convex set $\mathscr K$ on a neighbourhood of which $\Psi$ is defined and
$C^1$.  Then, for every $1\le p\le\infty$,
\[
\|\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(M_2)\|_{L^p}\le C_{\Psi,\mathscr K}\|M_1-M_2\|_{L^p},
\]
and, separately, for every $\partial\in\{\partial_t,\partial_a\}$, $1\le a\le n$,
for which the indicated weak derivative of $M_1$ belongs to $L^1_{\rm loc}$,
\[
\partial\Psi(M_1)=\Psi'(M_1)\partial M_1\quad\text{in }\mathcal D'.
\]
Consequently, the same difference estimates hold with $C_tL^p$ in place of
$L^p$. If $M\in C_tY^{s-1,1}$, then
$\Psi(M)-\Psi(0)\in C_tY^{s-1,1}$; more generally, differences
$\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(M_2)$ are continuous there by
\eqref{eq:coeff-lipschitz}. This formulation is necessary because
$Y^{s-1,1}$ is nonunital when $\Psi(0)\ne0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.846224+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7ef6b8e9936ab2976b58c7861992030f5119aeb057eec364910e878977342b29","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] There exist sequences $(A_i)_{i}, (J_i)_{i}, (\mathcal{L}_i)_{i}$ with the following properties:

    \item  $J_i\subset \mathbb Z_+^{2i}$ is an index set.

    where the square root is the principal branch, positive on \((0,\infty)\). Consequently,
    \[
      \mathcal G_\star(x)\longrightarrow-\infty,
      \qquad x\to+\infty.

  \item

    \begin{equation*} 
      \begin{pmatrix}

        x^{1/4}\left(
        -\dfrac{1}{\mathcal G_\star'(x)}-2\sqrt{x}
        \right)
      \end{pmatrix}
      \Longrightarrow
      \mathcal N\!\left(
        \begin{pmatrix}0\\0\end{pmatrix},
        \frac1\beta
        \begin{pmatrix}
          1&-1\\
          -1&2
        \end{pmatrix}
      \right).
    \end{equation*}
    Moreover, almost surely,
    \[
      \mathcal G_\star'(x)
      =
      -\frac1{2\sqrt{x}}+o(x^{-1}),
      \qquad
      \mathcal G_\star''(x)
      =
      \frac1{4x^{3/2}}+o(x^{-2}).
    \]
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["The two cylinders must be separated in time, past on the left of the inequality","Nonnegativity is required on the entire cylinder","Time-slice and reversed-time versions are false","Cylinders must respect the parabolic scaling t ~ r^2"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.107085+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations / Harnack inequalities","id":"claim_7f4575933b50f01a827886bdb34f32f9b2fc796f45ba59f43b34b0e99f0abc08","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Moser's inequality reads $\\sup_{Q^-}u\\le C\\inf_{Q^+}u$ with $Q^-$ strictly earlier than $Q^+$. Three hypotheses are load-bearing, and all three fail for the naive elliptic-style statement. (1) No inequality at a single time: on $\\mathbb R^n$ the positive solution $u_k(x,t)=e^{kx_1+k^2t}$ has, on $B_1\\times\\{t\\}$, $\\sup u_k/\\inf u_k=e^{2k}\\to\\infty$, so $\\sup_{B_1\\times\\{t\\}}u\\le C\\inf_{B_1\\times\\{t\\}}u$ cannot hold with $C$ independent of the solution; the same family (or the shifted heat kernel $\\Phi(x-y,t+\\varepsilon)$ as $\\varepsilon\\downarrow0$) shows that even the elliptic Harnack constant for the Laplacian does not transfer. (2) The time direction cannot be reversed: $\\sup_{Q^+}u\\le C\\inf_{Q^-}u$ is false, since $u_k$ grows like $e^{k^2t}$; information propagates forward in time only. Intuitively, a heat distribution can be large now and tiny in the past. (3) Nonnegativity on the whole cylinder is needed, not just on $Q^-\\cup Q^+$: the inequality is applied to $u$ and to $\\sup u-u$ in the derivation of Holder continuity, and both must be nonnegative on the full cylinder $B_{2r}\\times(t_0-4r^2,t_0)$. Also parabolic, not Euclidean, scaling governs the geometry: the cylinder for radius $r$ must have time length comparable to $r^2$, so an auditor should check that a cited Harnack inequality is applied on cylinders of the correct aspect ratio, with the two sub-cylinders separated in time by a fixed multiple of $r^2$.","status":"unverified"}

 \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:10.024473+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7ff648b1ad13a29750e4071b56e7aad088f5d88db4f78464b0d906781b9b4c7d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 12 (Local-to-global Wasserstein contraction) of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] Let $(E,D)$ be a compact geodesic metric space and let $K$ be a Markov kernel on $E$. Let $W_D$ denote Wasserstein distance with cost $D$. Suppose that, for some $\rho>0$ and $\lambda\in[0,1)$,
\be
W_D(K(x,\cdot),K(y,\cdot))\leq \lambda D(x,y)
\qquad \text{whenever }D(x,y)\leq \rho.
\ee
Then, for all $x,y\in E$,
\be
W_D(K(x,\cdot),K(y,\cdot))\leq \lambda D(x,y).
\ee
Consequently, for all probability measures $\mu,\nu$ on $E$,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:52:51.769461+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7ffd3c4bb7834fa556325f35b86faf9407db1835cd805aaf06b216cf1c2fcadf","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi defn:MRSC of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] The $d$-dimensional multi-parameter random simplicial complex model with vertex set $[n]$ and probability parameters $\\bm{p} = (p_1, \\dots, p_d) \\in [0,1]^d$ is constructed recursively as follows. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:15:27.869314+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_800182846141774e70b9296f79e5eab92b4ed12261fc2c10ba2ec3e50d8353b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"FIRES WHEN a source, or your own reading of one, states a stochastic dominance between two random variables that you can check have equal means. MINIMAL COUNTEREXAMPLE, or rather the minimal IMPOSSIBILITY: if X >= Y in the usual stochastic order and E X = E Y < infinity, then E(X - Y) = integral (P(X > t) - P(Y > t)) dt = 0 with a nonnegative integrand, so the survival functions agree everywhere and X and Y are equal in law. There is no example to find; the hypothesis is already the conclusion. CONDITION UNDER WHICH THE ROUTE FAILS: equal means. WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: the intended relation is the CONVEX or dilation order, under which the variance inequality c^2 >= 1 is immediate. In the E0078 case this is a reading issue in the source's own statement, not a mathematical obstacle - and reading it as the usual stochastic order would have made Conjecture 4.2 imply Conjecture 4.1 for a trivial and wrong reason. The lesson generalises past this problem: when a claimed ordering would be vacuous under a moment identity the problem also asserts, the ordering has been mis-transcribed.","status":"unverified"}

# C006: prior-averaged Gaussian log-loss generalization

Claim T336-w727-C006 v1. Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: bound.
Target: none (reviewer-authorized generalization half of the T336 statement).
This is an explicit adaptation of standard covering and exponential-moment
arguments, not a claim of a new learning-theory principle or a new solver.
The hardest step is uniform concentration for the unbounded query loss.

## 1. Statistical statement

Let (W_i,Y_i), i=1,...,m, be independent identically distributed tasks, m>=1.
W contains the context and query features, including all information on which
the predictive is conditioned. Assume the conditional law is exactly

    Y | W ~ N(a(W), b(W)), |a(W)|<=M, 0<b(W)<=V,

where M>=0 and V>0 are fixed. The law of W is otherwise arbitrary. In
particular no independence between the query and context features is required.
For the GP application this conditional-law premise must be checked; it is
not inferred just from a marginal GP label law or an arbitrary feature-selection
mechanism. A fixed GP, exogenous input design, and rejection of tasks based only
on their context labels satisfy it. Conditioning on query labels would not.

Assume the token encoding of W is measurable. Let H be the family of clipped
transformer predictions described in Section 2,
with outputs mu_theta(W) in [-U,U] and v_theta(W) in [v0,v1], where
U>=0 and 0<v0<=v1 are fixed. Define the normalized negative log loss

    ell_theta(W,Y) = (1/2)log(v_theta/v0)
                    +(Y-mu_theta)^2/(2v_theta).

The usual Gaussian negative log density differs by the same constant
(1/2)log(2 pi v0) for every theta, so its ERM and excess risk are identical.
Let R(theta)=E ell_theta and Rhat(theta)=m^(-1) sum_i ell_theta(W_i,Y_i).
An approximate ERM satisfies Rhat(thetahat)<=inf_theta Rhat(theta)+xi,
with xi>=0. No efficient algorithm for finding it is asserted.

For gamma>0 and alpha in (0,1), use the explicit architecture quantities
P,Lambda from Section 2 and set

    q = max(1,ceil(2 Wmax Lambda/gamma)), J=(q+1)^P,
    D0=M+U,
    C=(1/2)log(v1/v0)+D0^2/v0, A=V/v0, K=4(C+A),
    u=log(4J/alpha), t=log(4m/alpha),
    T=M+sqrt(2V t),
    Q=1/(2v0)+(D0+sqrt(V))/v0+(D0^2+V)/v0^2,
    L_T=1/(2v0)+(T+U)/v0+(T+U)^2/(2v0^2),
    beta=4sqrt(2) K sqrt(u/m)+2K u/m,
    E_m=beta+gamma(Q+L_T).

Then, with probability at least 1-alpha, simultaneously for all theta,

    |R(theta)-Rhat(theta)| <= E_m,
    R(thetahat) <= inf_theta R(theta)+2E_m+xi.             (1)

Let P_W=N(a(W),b(W)) and h_theta=N(mu_theta(W),v_theta(W)). Subtracting
the integrable conditional Gaussian entropy gives equivalently

    E_W KL(P_W || h_thetahat(W))
       <= inf_theta E_W KL(P_W || h_theta(W))+2E_m+xi.   (2)

For (2), assume also b(W)>=b0>0, as in the noisy-GP application. This
makes the conditional entropy finite and justifies subtracting it. Without
that lower bound (1) still holds, but (2) is not asserted via subtraction
of potentially infinite entropies.

## 2. Explicit parameter entropy for normalized ReLU attention

Fix N tokens, token dimension D>=1, L>=0 residual attention layers, at
most H>=1 heads per layer, and a linear two-output readout. No trainable
tokenwise MLP, softmax, or layer normalization is included in this architecture.
Pad unused heads by zero matrices. There are

    P=3HLD^2+2D

trainable scalar entries, all in [-Wmax,Wmax], with Wmax>=1. The encoding
of W into tokens is fixed and has every scalar coordinate bounded in
absolute value by K0>=1. One layer is exactly

    h_i^+ = h_i + N^(-1) sum_heads sum_j
                    ReLU(<Q h_i,K h_j>) V h_j.

Optionally apply a fixed coordinatewise clip onto [-Kcap,Kcap] after each
attention layer, with Kcap>=K0. This is fixed tokenwise ReLU postprocessing,
not a trainable MLP or layer normalization. For this variant use K_l=Kcap
for every l in the recurrences below instead of the growing K recurrence.
Clipping is nonexpansive, so the same E recurrence remains valid.

The readout acts on one fixed token. Apply coordinatewise interval clipping
to its two outputs. This postprocessing uses fixed, nontrainable constants;
each scalar clip is representable by two ReLUs. Count P as the trainable
parameters, not as every fixed scalar in this postprocessing.

Define deterministic nonnegative recurrences

    K_{l+1}=K_l+H D^4 Wmax^3 K_l^3,       K_0=K0,
    E_0=0,
    E_{l+1}=(1+3H D^4 Wmax^3 K_l^2) E_l
                       +3H D^4 Wmax^2 K_l^3,
    Lambda=D Wmax E_L+D K_L > 0.

For any two parameter vectors theta,theta' in the cube at sup distance
rho, the outputs obey

    sup_W max(|mu_theta-mu_theta'|,|v_theta-v_theta'|)
        <= Lambda rho.                                  (3)

To verify this, use the sup norm across all tokens and coordinates. Each
transformed coordinate Qh has magnitude <=D Wmax K_l; each score has
magnitude <=D^3 Wmax^2 K_l^2; each Vh coordinate has magnitude
<=D Wmax K_l. The normalized sum cancels N and proves the K recurrence.

At fixed weights, changing inputs by d changes one head by at most
3D^4 Wmax^3 K_l^2 d: two terms differentiate the score and one term
the value; ReLU is 1-Lipschitz. At fixed inputs of size K_l, changing
matrix entries by rho changes a head by at most
3D^4 Wmax^2 K_l^3 rho, by the same three-term product split. Splitting
the joint change into these two changes and adding the residual proves
the E recurrence by induction. The readout change is bounded by
D Wmax E_L rho+D K_L rho. Clipping is 1-Lipschitz, proving (3).
These estimates compare actual heads directly, and require no independence
among tokens or between successive layers.

Divide [-Wmax,Wmax] into q equal intervals. There are q+1 grid values;
each parameter has a grid value within 2Wmax/q<=gamma/Lambda.
Thus the full grid has J elements and gives a gamma cover in the output
metric of (3). It is fixed before seeing the training tasks. In particular
log J <= P log(2+2Wmax Lambda/gamma) except when the max with 1 is active;
in that case q=1 and the same bound still holds since 2+2Wmax Lambda/gamma>=2.

## 3. A uniform exponential moment and finite-cover concentration

Write Z=(Y-a(W))/sqrt(b(W)). Its conditional law given W is standard
normal, hence Z is independent of W. For every theta,

    0 <= ell_theta <= C+A Z^2.

Indeed |Y-mu_theta|<=D0+sqrt(V)|Z| and (r+s)^2<=2r^2+2s^2.
Since C/K<=1/4 and A/K<=1/4, Gaussian integration yields

    E exp(ell_theta/K)
       <= exp(C/K)(1-2A/K)^(-1/2)
       <= exp(1/4)sqrt(2) < 2.                           (4)

The last inequality follows from log(2)>1/2 (integrate 1/x on [1,2]).
It follows from the nonnegative exponential series that
E ell_theta^k <= 2 k! K^k for every integer k>=1. For
X=ell_theta-E ell_theta, convexity gives

    E|X|^k <= 2^k E ell_theta^k <= 2^(k+1) k! K^k.

For |z|<1/(2K), the centered exponential series therefore gives

    log E exp(z X) <= 8K^2 z^2/(1-2K|z|).              (5)

Interchange of expectation and the series is justified by the absolute
moment series, which converges at these z. Independence across the m
tasks gives for their centered sum the same bound with 8mK^2 in
the numerator. Chernoff's inequality and (5) give each one-sided tail

    Pr(|Rhat(theta)-R(theta)| >
                  sqrt(32)K sqrt(u/m)+2K u/m) <= 2exp(-u).

For completeness, the generic bound log E exp(z S)<=v z^2/[2(1-cz)]
implies Pr(S>=sqrt(2vu)+cu)<=exp(-u): substitute
z=r/(1+cr), r=sqrt(2u/v), into the exponential Markov bound.
Here v=16mK^2, c=2K; apply it also to -S and divide by m.
No bounded-label assumption has been used.

A union bound on the J fixed grid predictors, with u=log(4J/alpha),
shows all their risk deviations are <=beta except on probability alpha/2.

## 4. From the grid to every parameter

For two clipped predictors within gamma in both output coordinates,
the elementary log derivative and a difference-of-squares split give

    |ell_theta(W,Y)-ell_theta'(W,Y)| <= gamma L(Y),
    L(Y)=1/(2v0)+(|Y|+U)/v0+(|Y|+U)^2/(2v0^2).       (6)

In detail, the log term costs gamma/(2v0). Hold v fixed and vary the
mean to get gamma(|Y|+U)/v0. Hold the new mean fixed and vary 1/v to
get gamma(|Y|+U)^2/(2v0^2). Both denominators use the common positive
floor v0. Thus E L(Y)<=Q: E|Y|<=M+sqrt(V) and
E(|Y|+U)^2<=2D0^2+2V.

The standard-normal exponential integral E exp(zZ)=exp(z^2/2), followed
by exponential Markov at z=x, gives Pr(|Z|>x)<=2exp(-x^2/2).
For t=log(4m/alpha), a union bound gives |Y_i|<=T for all i except
on probability alpha/2. On that event the empirical average of L(Y_i)
is at most L_T. Combine this event with the grid concentration event.
For each theta choose a grid point theta' satisfying (3). Insert
R(theta') and Rhat(theta') and use (6) to obtain the first line of (1).
The approximate-ERM inequality then gives the second line of (1).
The same event works for all approximate ERMs, without a union over
their potentially data-dependent choice. This proves (1) and (2).

## 5. GP comparator and scope

For the finite-rank noisy GP in C002, with supplied features bounded by R,
context length <=n and context labels bounded by B, one can use

    M=nR^2 B/s, V=s+R^2.

Take a desired comparator accuracy eps_c>0, U=M+sqrt(s eps_c),
v0=s, v1=V+s min(1/2,sqrt(eps_c)). C002's scalar error estimates
ensure its outputs lie in these intervals and its expected forward KL
is <=eps_c. Its padded encoding has K0=max(1,R,B,s), width D=7p+4,
at most H=5 heads and L=T_c+2 layers. The construction gives fixed
explicit matrices and readout. Choose Wmax at least 1 and their largest
absolute scalar entry; this is an explicitly computable maximum of the
finite matrices specified by C002 Section 4, independent of task data.
The class of Section 2 then contains that comparator, and (2) implies

    E_W KL(P_W || h_thetahat(W)) <= eps_c+2E_m+xi.        (7)

One may use the internally clipped variant with the explicit common cap

    Kcap=max(1,R,B,s,2nRB/s,2R/s,U,v1).

It preserves the C002 comparator exactly: its feature and query registers
are bounded by R; for every Chebyshev iteration j, |r_j(lambda)|<=1,
so the mean-solve iterates have norm <=2nRB/s and the variance-solve
iterates have norm <=2R/s. The previous-iterate registers have the same
bounds. Initialization, broadcast, constants, and final output registers
are covered by the other displayed terms. Thus clipping changes none
of its states. For this class the parameter Lipschitz recurrence uses a
constant Kcap, and log Lambda grows at most linearly with depth, avoiding
the very loose cubic growth of the unclipped K recurrence. The statistical
bound (7) is consequently explicit for a class containing the comparator
with either choice of internal clipping. All added clipping parameters
are fixed, so P still counts exactly the trainable entries.

For R=0 use a constant exact comparator instead of C002's formulas that
divide by R. The class can contain it by initializing a constant coordinate
and choosing a readout that outputs (0,s).

If training uses rejection to enforce bounded context labels, (7) concerns
the resulting conditioned task distribution. It is not silently a theorem
for the original unconditioned GP context law. With unconditioned contexts,
the C002 comparator guarantee and this bounded-input parameter cover do
not apply as stated. This is the precise remaining distributional scope
issue, separate from the unbounded Gaussian query labels handled above.

All constants here are explicit but loose. The parameter cube and finite
cover give a statistical ERM guarantee, not SGD convergence, efficient
enumeration of the cover, a finite-bit realization theorem for the original
solver, or a claim that Chebyshev depth beats Newton-type solvers.

## 6. Sources and status

Bai, Chen, Wang, Xiong and Mei, arXiv:2306.04637v2, Section 5.1,
PDF pages 14-15, define pretraining ERM for square loss and give Theorem 20.
That is the related parameter-entropy/ERM framework, not a citation for
the Gaussian log-loss bound above. Sections 2-4 provide its proof directly.
C002 v1 supplies the independently checked uniform-KL comparator.
This extension itself remains unaudited. No novelty is claimed.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.593058+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_80ed7ce8bcd053f18c5f0449417c6ae0439ff84ff77bd1666aa15a0c0e560405","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] The divisible sandpile on $\\Z^d$ starts from i.i.d.\\ masses at each site, and, in each discrete time step, a site with mass above one keeps one unit and sends the excess equally to its neighbors. \\citet*{LMPU} showed that at mean one this process explodes, with every site emitting infinite mass. We show that the mass emitted from a site by time $t$ is of order $t^{(4-d)/4}$ for $d\\leq3$, of order $\\log t$ for $d=4$, and a tail-dependent, divergent rate for $d\\geq5$. We further show that the mass emitted, after diffusive rescaling, converges to a Brownian optimal-stopping value for $d\\leq3$ and to tail-dependent, weighted membrane fields for $d\\geq5$, while at the critical dimension $d=4$, after superdiffusive rescaling, it converges to the membrane model. Using these estimates, we prove that, for every $d\\geq2$, the set of sites that topple contains an infinite component at some mean below one, hence it has a non-trivial percolation phase transition. This answers a variant of a question of \\citet*{FMR}. The proof adapts ideas from the theory of level-set percolation of strongly correlated Gaussian fields.","status":"unverified"}

If $k$ is odd then $\\mathbb{P}_2[k]$ is empty. Given a function $u$ on $[k]$ and a pair partition $\\nu\\in\\mathbb{P}_2[k]$ we say that $u$ is compatible with $\\nu$, and write $u\\sim\\nu$ if for all sets $(i,j)\\in\\nu$ we have $u(i)=u(j)$. Given even $k=2p$ and a partition $\\nu\\in\\mathbb{P}_2[2p]$ we define the $\\nu$-assignment $u_\\nu:[2p]\\to[p]$ as the surjective function that is compatible with $\\nu$ and no other partition. Any of the $p!$ such functions works for our purposes, but we pick the first in lexicographic order.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.262604+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8141784e79bfd76210974fc592feec85c90d41012c5ff98c50e424fb88284459","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2609.01114, 'Unbalanced spectral Tur\'an problem for color-critical graphs with prescribed large maximu'] Fix $p\ge2$. The following claims hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item If a complete multipartite graph has positive part sizes $s_1,\ldots,s_p$, then its spectral radius is the unique positive solution of
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{i=1}^{p}\frac{s_i}{\lambda+s_i}=1 .
\end{equation}
\item For fixed $D$ and $p$, the graph $(n-D)K_1\vee K_{m_1,\ldots,m_p}$ with $\sum_{i=1}^{p} m_i= D$ has maximum spectral radius when $m_1,\ldots,m_p$ are as equal as possible, and equality occurs only for such a balanced choice, up to permutation of the parts.
\item For fixed $n$, define the function $f_{n,p}(D):=\rho(S_{n,D,p})$, where $\left\lceil\frac{p}{p+1}n\right\rceil\le D\le n-1$.

Then $f_{n,p}(D)$ is strictly decreasing in $D$.
\item Denote $\eta_p:=\frac{2p-1}{p(p-1)}$.

There are constants $\beta_p\in(0,(100p^2)^{-1}]$ and $C_p>0$ such that, uniformly for $(1-\beta_p)n\le D\le n$,
\begin{equation}
        \left|\rho(S_{n,D,p})-\rho(T(n,p))-\eta_p(n-D)\right|
        \le C_p\left(\frac{(n-D)^2}{n}+1\right).
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
        \rho(S_{n,D,p})-\rho(T(n,p))
        =\eta_p(n-D)+O_p((n-D)^2/n)+O_p(1).
\]
\item For fixed $D$ and $p$, define $g_{D,p}(N):=\rho(S_{N,D,p})$, where $N\geq D+1$.

Then $g_{D,p}(N)$ is strictly increasing in $N$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.368593+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_81a0efb068e72e9d6907e4745271428844146c50426a309ac9bdcc1a1fc13fd0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition properties of r of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] i.) The stopped process $r_{j\wedge\tau}$ is homogeneous and Markov. The transition probabilities of $r_j$ when both cards $n-1$ and $n$ have not been shown are 
\begin{equation}
    P(r_{j+1}=i\,|\,r_j=k,\,\tau>j)=\frac{\binom{i-k-1}{0}+\binom{i-k-1}{n-k-1}}{2^{i-k}}=\frac{1_{\{k+1\leq i\leq n\}}+1_{\{i=n\}}}{2^{i-k}}
\end{equation}

ii.) $\tau-1$ has a $\text{Binomial}(n-2,\,1/2)$ distribution.

iii.) After the $n-1$st or $n$th card is shown, the cards are deterministic and their order is given uniquely by $K_{\tau}$, if $\tau=\tau^n$. If $\tau=\tau^{n-1}$, then $r_{\tau+1}=n$ a.s. and the remaining cards, in order, are given by $K_{\tau}$. That is,
\[P(r_{\tau+m}=i\,|\,\tau=\tau^{n})=1_{\{K_{\tau}^m=i\}}\]
and
\[P(r_{\tau+1}=n\,|\,\tau=\tau^{n-1})=1, \;\;\;\;P(r_{\tau+m+1}=i\,|\,\tau=\tau^{n-1})=1_{\{K_{\tau}^m=i\}}\]

\begin{proof}

    First we prove i.). Fix $j<\tau$ and $k$ such that $p_{k,j}>0$. Recall that cards go to the top and the bottom of the pile via a $\text{Bernoulli}(1/2)$ distribution. Let $N_k$ be the number of cards at the top up to and including when card $k$ is selected. Then, $N_k$ is $\text{Binomial}(k,\,1/2)$. Observe that $\{r_j=k\}=\{N_k=j\}$ as events (intersected with $\{j<\tau\}$). Also notice that the number of cards that have not gone to the top is $k-N_k$. So we are left with a shuffle of $n-(N_k+k-N_k)=n-k$ cards according to the distribution from Theorem $(positionmatrix of the paper)$, with card $k+1$ at the top of the deck. This proves i.). 

    To prove ii.), we first notice that cards $n-1$ and $n$ always appear consecutively in the deck, with both orderings having probability $1/2$. Label this block of two cards $B$ and shuffle the remaining $n-2$ cards. Then $\{\tau=k\}$ if and only if $k-1$ cards have been selected, each with probability $1/2$, to go above $B$. Hence, 
    \[P(\tau=k)=\frac{\binom{n-2}{k-1}}{2^{k-1}}\]
    so that 
    \[P(\tau-1=k)=\frac{\binom{n-2}{k}}{2^k}\]
    showing ii.). 

    As for iii.), we note that after card $n$ is shown, the cards are almost surely in strictly decreasing order. This is because cards are drawn from the bottom of the deck. There is one unique arrangement of the remaining cards in decreasing order, namely, by removing the already selected cards from $[n]$ and reversing. This is exactly as in the construction of $K_{j\wedge \tau}$, proving iii.).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X is a compact metric space","T is a homeomorphism of X (bijective, continuous, continuous inverse)","the expansive constant delta is strictly positive and depends on the metric"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:23.250591+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, expansive maps","id":"claim_81a7ef561e0af1f85a9f7f77df488257576c032550ed3b546d86f1abbe6a19db","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $(X,d)$ be a compact metric space and $T: X \\to X$ a homeomorphism. $T$ is called expansive if there is a constant $\\delta > 0$ (an expansive constant) such that for every pair of distinct points $x \\neq y$ in $X$ there exists an integer $n \\in \\mathbb{Z}$ (positive, zero or negative) with $d(T^n x, T^n y) > \\delta$. Equivalently: two orbits that stay within distance $\\delta$ of each other for all times $n \\in \\mathbb{Z}$ are the same orbit, i.e. the same point. Any $\\delta' < \\delta$ is again an expansive constant; on a compact metric space the property (though not the constant) does not depend on the choice of a compatible metric. A map $T$ (not necessarily invertible) is positively expansive if the same holds with $n$ restricted to $n \\geq 0$. Examples: the full shift on $k$ symbols and every subshift (with $\\delta$ below the distance between two sequences differing in the zeroth coordinate); hyperbolic toral automorphisms; Axiom A restricted to a basic set. Non-examples: the identity, any isometry (e.g. a circle rotation), any map with a nontrivial equicontinuous factor of the same type. Warning: the definition uses two-sided time for homeomorphisms; a homeomorphism of an infinite compact metric space is never positively expansive.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:39:41.442291+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_81ecedcf9027ab2eb28dc45a41cba276d2abf045d2d0f17986054dd6fe69d60f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] Let $(X_t)_{t\in \mathbb{N}}$ be a birth-death chain over state space $\Omega=\{0,\dots,d\}$ with transition probabilities from some $x\in \Omega$,
  \begin{align*}
   P(x+1,x) &= p_x\\
   P(x-1,x) &= q_x\\
   P(x,x) &= r_x = 1 - p_x-q_x\\
   P(x,y) &= 0, \quad \forall y \not\in\{x,x+1,x-1\}
  \end{align*}
  Additionally, assume that $p_x$ and $q_x$ are affine in $x$. That is, there exists $\alpha,\beta,\xi,\eta\in \mathbb{R}$ such that,
  \[p_x = \alpha + \beta x \quad \text{and} \quad q_x = \xi + \eta x\]
  Finally, let $(K_m)_{m=0}^d$ be a sequence of degree $m$ polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to $\langle\cdot ,\cdot \rangle_\pi$ where $\pi$ is the stationary distribution. Then, $(K_m)_{m=0}^d$ are the eigenfunctions of $P$.
  \begin{proof}
   Let $x\in \Omega$ and $j\in \{0,\dots,d\}$ and consider,
   \begin{align*}
      (PK_j)(x) &= \sum_{y\in \Omega} P(x,y)K_j(y)\\
      &= P(x,x+1)K_j(x+1) + P(x,x-1)K_j(x-1) + P(x,x)K_j(x)\\
      &= q_{x+1} K_j(x+1) + p_{x-1} K_j(x-1) + r_x K_j(x)\\
      &= (\xi + \eta (x-1))K_j(x+1) + (\alpha + \beta (x+1))K_j(x-1) +(1 -(\alpha +\xi) - (\beta + \eta)x) K_j(x)
   \end{align*}
   Now, let $c$ be the coefficient of $x^{j}$ in $K_j(x)$. That is,
   \[K_j(x) = cx^j + o(x^{j-1})\]
   At this point, we examine the coefficient of $x^{j+1}$ in $(PK_j)(x)$. Using the above form and considering only relevant terms we have
   \begin{align*}
   (PK_j)(x)&= (\xi -\eta + \eta x)K_j(x+1) + (\alpha + \beta + \beta x)K_j(x-1) +(1 -(\alpha +\xi) - (\beta + \eta)x) K_j(x)\\
   &= \eta xc(x+1)^j + \beta x c(x-1)^j - (\beta + \eta)x cx^j + o(x^j)\\
   &=  \eta  cx^{j+1}+ \beta cx^{j+1} - (\beta + \eta)cx^{j+1} +  o(x^j)\\
   &= 0\cdot x^{j+1} + o(x^j)
   \end{align*}
   Thus, the coefficient of $x^{j+1}$ in $(PK_j)(x)$ is $0$. Also, notice that $(PK_j)(x)$ has no terms of order larger than $x^{j+1}$. This implies that $PK_j \in \mathbf{P}_j$ where $\mathbf{P}_j$ is the vector space of polynomials with degree at most $j$. This means that $\mathbf{P}_j$ is an invariant subspace with respect to $P$. Now, for any fixed $m\in \{0,\dots,d\}$, we know that $\{K_0,\dots K_{m-1}\}$ are orthogonal and therefore linearly independent. Thus, $\{K_0,\dots K_{m-1}\}$ span $\mathbf{P}_{m-1}$. Hence, any polynomial in $\mathbf{P}_j$ where $j < m$ is also orthogonal to $K_m$ by linearity of the inner product. Thus, $PK_j \in \mathbf{P}_j$, is orthogonal to $K_m$. That is,
   \[\langle K_m, PK_j \rangle_\pi = 0\]
   Hence, by Lemma \ref{self_ajoint},
   \[\langle PK_m, K_j\rangle_\pi=0 \quad \text{for}\quad j<m\]
   Finally, $PK_m \in \mathbf{P}_m$ so it admits the following presentation,
   \[PK_m = a_0 K_0 + a_1 K_1 + \cdots + a_m K_m\]
   where $a_0,\dots, a_m$ are constants. Hence,
   \begin{align*}
   0&= \langle PK_m, K_j\rangle_\pi\\
   &= \langle a_0 K_0 + a_1 K_1 + \cdots + a_m K_m, K_j\rangle_\pi\\
   &= a_0\langle K_0, K_j\rangle + \cdots + a_m\langle K_m, K_j\rangle_\pi \tag{by linearity}\\
   &= a_j\langle K_j, K_j\rangle_\pi \tag{by orthogonality}
   \end{align*}
   Therefore, $a_j = 0$ for all $j<m$. Thus,
   \[PK_m = a_m K_m\]
   and therefore, $K_m$ is an eigenfunction.
   \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:31:14.256315+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_820719bc83c90691b921a0ae38b2e62a5f170f162c557fc47cc59c4801e41694","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn def:3.1 of arXiv:2606.16237, 'The Backward Stochastic Partial Differential Integral Equations: Solvability and Compariso'] A triple of processes \((u, q, r) \in \mathbb{S}^2(H^0) \cap \mathbb{H}^1 \times \mathbb{H}^0 \times \mathbb{H}^{\nu,0}\) is called a weak solution to BSPDIE (equation eq:2.1 of the paper) if, for any \(t \in [0, T]\) and test function \(\eta \in C_0^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\),
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} u(t, x) \eta(x) \, dx \nonumber\\
&=& \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x) \eta(x) \, dx + \int_t^T \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \Bigg(

&&+ \int_Z \Big[ r(s, x + k(s, e, x)) - r(s, e, x) \Big] \eta(x) \nu(de)
\Bigg)dxds \nonumber\\
&&- \int_t^T \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} q(s, x) \eta(x)dxdW_s - \int_t^T \int_Z \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} r(s, e, x) \eta(x)dx\tilde{\mu}(de, ds).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:04:07.031866+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_820c04f673315ac99852b11fcb2ec0a74b5f557e6bf9efdd033c31863cc224b0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:one-point-conditional-determinant of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Under the hypotheses and notation of
		Proposition~(prop:one-point-conditional-hessian of the paper), the following
		hold for \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\):
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item
			\begin{equation}
				\begin{aligned}
					\frac1N
					\log\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{m},f_N}
					\left|\det\nabla_\sigma^2F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})\right|
					={}&
					-\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N
					\log\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i)
					+\frac{\xi''(q)}2
					\left(
					\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N
					\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i)

					+o(1)\\
					\longrightarrow{}&
					-\mathbb{E}\log\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(q,X_q)

				\end{aligned}
			\end{equation}
			In the \(\varepsilon\)-window above, the error in
			(equation eq:one-point-conditional-determinant of the paper) is
			\(o_\varepsilon(1)+o_N(1)\).
			
			\item
			Suppose that, for some \(\kappa_0>0\) and \(L<\infty\),
			\[
			\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N
			\exp\{(8+\kappa_0)|b_i|\}\le L.
			\]
			Set
			\[
			D_{\mathbf{m},\sigma}
			:=
			\det\nabla_\sigma^2F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m}).
			\]
			There are \(c_L>0\) and a deterministic \(r_N=o(N)\) such that
			\begin{equation}

				|D_{\mathbf{m},\sigma}|
				<e^{-r_N}\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{m},f_N}|D_{\mathbf{m},\sigma}|
				\right)
				\le e^{-c_LN}.
			\end{equation}
			Moreover, the estimate is uniform over the same window, subject to the

			with \(\rho_{\det}(\varepsilon)\downarrow0\), and there are nonnegative
			deterministic numbers \(r_{N,\varepsilon}=o_N(N)\) such that
			\begin{equation}

				<

				\right)
				\le e^{-c_LN}.
			\end{equation}
			Here \(r_{N,\varepsilon}/N\to0\) for fixed \(\varepsilon\), and \(N\to\infty\)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.062222+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_820c14f4ca750886855473e99424ed13207a5aa6e25e1a960020d1e5dc5d90e8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] A densely defined form $\mathfrak a$ is sectorial with vertex
$\omega\in\mathbb R$ and semi-angle $\alpha<\pi/2$ if
\[
  \mathfrak a[f]-\omega\|f\|^2\in\overline{\Sigma_\alpha},
  \qquad f\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak a).
\]
Equivalently, after a real shift, its imaginary part is controlled by its real
part: there is $C<\infty$ such that
\[
  |\Im \mathfrak a[f]|
  \leq C\bigl(\Re\mathfrak a[f]-\omega\|f\|^2\bigr),
  \qquad f\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak a).
\]
If $\omega=0$ and $\Re \mathfrak a[f]\geq0$, the form is called
accretive.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:10:07.530537+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_822f72fb1f054f857e35ef63ee43aa23d5de594a709bb80758a2d4037c68d332","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Conjecture eq:sparse-lower of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[conjecture]{conj:sparse-lower}
For smooth centered unit-variance entry laws satisfying the preceding large-deviation hypothesis and stability of the conditional critical-point exponent under an \(o(1)\) perturbation of the exposed block,
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 \ge\sup_{r\ge0}\sup_{\substack{A\in\mathbb R^{[r]^p}:\\ \mathcal J_\mu(A)<\infty}}
 \left\{\underline\Phi_{p,\mathrm{sf}}^{J,A}(V)-\mathcal J_\mu(A)\right\}.
\end{equation}
Under the additional hypothesis (equation eq:deformed-background-univ of the paper),
the right-hand side could be written with the Gaussian spike-free
pressure, but the preceding bounded example shows that this hypothesis
is not available under finite moment matching and entrywise cutoff.
The \(r=0\) term is merely the cutoff residual branch: for bounded
disorder it equals the full non-Gaussian pressure and already contains
the mesoscopic obstruction.  Thus the conjecture is informative only
when that residual branch has been controlled separately.  The
one-entry instance proved in (thm:one-spike of the paper) is a coarse form of
the bound; general \(A\) allows localized clusters and mixed
spike--bulk critical points. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)","status":"unverified"}
