{"assumptions":["f is 1-periodic and Lebesgue integrable over one period"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.262136+00:00","domain":"Fourier series on the circle","id":"claim_82389d4e8f4fb9ac13809cff86a8079ad0ec59befe3fccefb0bd229569f870b4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $\\mathbb{T}=\\mathbb{R}/\\mathbb{Z}$, identified with $[0,1)$ with Lebesgue measure, and $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb{T})$. The Fourier coefficients are $\\hat f(n)=\\int_0^1 f(x)e^{-2\\pi i n x}\\,dx$, $n\\in\\mathbb{Z}$, with $|\\hat f(n)|\\le\\|f\\|_1$; the Fourier series is $\\sum_n\\hat f(n)e^{2\\pi i n x}$. Convolution on $\\mathbb T$ is $(f*g)(x)=\\int_0^1 f(x-y)g(y)\\,dy$ and $\\widehat{f*g}(n)=\\hat f(n)\\hat g(n)$. The symmetric partial sums are $S_Nf(x)=\\sum_{|n|\\le N}\\hat f(n)e^{2\\pi i n x}=(f*D_N)(x)$ with the Dirichlet kernel $D_N(x)=\\sum_{|n|\\le N}e^{2\\pi i n x}=\\sin((2N+1)\\pi x)/\\sin(\\pi x)$; $D_N$ is even, $\\int_0^1 D_N=1$, but it changes sign and its Lebesgue constants $\\|D_N\\|_{L^1(\\mathbb T)}=\\frac{4}{\\pi^2}\\log N+O(1)$ tend to infinity. The Fejer (Cesaro) means are $\\sigma_Nf=\\frac{1}{N+1}\\sum_{k=0}^N S_kf=f*F_N$ with the Fejer kernel $F_N(x)=\\frac{1}{N+1}\\left(\\frac{\\sin((N+1)\\pi x)}{\\sin(\\pi x)}\\right)^2=\\sum_{|n|\\le N}\\left(1-\\frac{|n|}{N+1}\\right)e^{2\\pi i n x}$; $F_N\\ge0$, $\\int_0^1F_N=1$, and $F_N(x)\\le\\min\\{N+1,\\;1/((N+1)\\sin^2(\\pi x))\\}$. Periods other than 1 are handled by rescaling (for period $2\\pi$: $\\hat f(n)=\\frac1{2\\pi}\\int_{-\\pi}^{\\pi}f(t)e^{-int}dt$).","status":"unverified"}

Consider the marked point process $\dbtilde\mathcal{P}=\sum_{x \in \mathcal{P}} \delta_{(x,V(x))}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d\times \mathbb{K}'$ where $V(x) := \xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})$.

we have
\begin{align} \nonumber
& \Big| \mathbb {E} _{\bk x1{p+q}}[f(\bk V1{p})g(\bk V{p+1}{p+q})]\rho^{(p+q)}(\bk x1{p+q}) -
\mathbb {E} _{\bk x1p}[f(\bk V1p)] \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1{p}) \; \mathbb {E} _{\bk x{p+1}{p+q}}[g(\bk V{p+1}{p+q})]\rho^{(q)}(\bk
x{p+1}{p+q}) \Big|
\\

\phi( \frac{s}{2})\sum_{l=1}^\infty \frac{w_0^l}{l!}  C_{l+p+q}

 $\dbtilde\mathcal{P}$ satisfies the inequality~(equation e.Bmppmixing of the paper)  in Definition~(B-omega-mixing of the paper)(Bmixing of the paper)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-07T14:01:11.606209+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82b243bfd1bdebcf927fafa46de1d7d9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 2.5 of arXiv:2512.19517v1, 'Spiking and Resetting' (Cédric Bernardin and Vsevolod Vladimirovich Tarsamaev); numbered Proposition 6 in the earlier card; corrected to the increment form]

## Proposition 2.5 (increment form)

Assume the standing hypotheses of Section 1: (f,h\in C^2([0,1])), (f(1)<0<f(0)), (h(1)=0), (h'(1)\ne0), and (h(x)>0) on ([0,1)). Let

\[
e_1^\varepsilon=\inf\{t\ge0:X_t^\varepsilon>y_*^\varepsilon\},\qquad
e_2^\varepsilon=\inf\{t\ge e_1^\varepsilon:X_t^\varepsilon=0\},
\]

and define the post-(e_1^\varepsilon) holding time

\[
d_2^\varepsilon:=e_2^\varepsilon-e_1^\varepsilon.
\]

Then, for every (t\ge0),

\[
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\mathbb P(d_2^\varepsilon>t)=e^{f(1)t},
\]

so (d_2^\varepsilon\Rightarrow \operatorname{Exp}(-f(1))).

The proof in the paper restarts the deterministic flow at (e_1^\varepsilon) with local time (s=0); its displayed survival integral is therefore for (d_2^\varepsilon), not the absolute epoch (e_2^\varepsilon). The source says that after the stopping time “the process evolves deterministically until the next reset” (v1 HTML lines 252-257), which is precisely an increment statement.

## Later alternating holding-time sentence

For the recursively defined epochs (e_k^\varepsilon), the strong Markov property applies to the increments

\[
e_{2k+1}^\varepsilon-e_{2k}^\varepsilon,
\qquad
e_{2k+2}^\varepsilon-e_{2k+1}^\varepsilon,
\]

not to the increasing absolute epochs themselves. The alternating increments are the quantities that can be independent and have the two respective holding-time laws. Any downstream card should preserve this distinction.

## Why the absolute-time statement cannot hold as written

For every (\varepsilon), (e_2^\varepsilon\ge e_1^\varepsilon), hence

\[
\mathbb P(e_2^\varepsilon>t)\ge\mathbb P(e_1^\varepsilon>t).
\]

This stochastic order must persist at continuity points of any weak limits. Yet the paper permits (f(x)=1-3x) and (h(x)=1-x), for which (f(0)=1) and (f(1)=-2). Its two displayed absolute-time limits would require (e^{-2t}\ge e^{-t}) for (t>0), an immediate contradiction. No additional relation between (f(0)) and (f(1)) is present in the standing hypotheses.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T14:24:13.477078+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_82bf60ef29eb019353b57d9cb9b4acf8aa885aaabf0b0cca759d50f62863a1a2","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"A standard Brownian motion, or Wiener process, is a real-valued stochastic process (W_t)_{t >= 0} on a probability space such that (i) W_0 = 0 almost surely; (ii) for 0 <= s < t the increment W_t - W_s is normally distributed with mean 0 and variance t - s; (iii) increments over disjoint time intervals are independent; (iv) almost every sample path t |-> W_t is continuous. Existence is Wiener's theorem (constructed for instance by the Levy-Ciesielski series or as the Kolmogorov-extension limit with continuity from Kolmogorov's criterion, since E|W_t - W_s|^4 = 3 (t - s)^2). Consequences packaged with the definition: the covariance is E[W_s W_t] = min(s, t); paths are almost surely nowhere differentiable and have unbounded variation on every interval, with quadratic variation t; Brownian scaling c^{-1/2} W_{c t}, time inversion t W_{1/t}, and reflection are again Brownian motions; W is a continuous martingale and a Markov process with transition density the Gaussian kernel. Conditions (i)-(iii) characterise the finite-dimensional laws; (iv) selects the continuous version, which is the object meant in every theorem about paths.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:13:22.513685+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8311a7454b8bc517593c2e5d2443f81f8d93fbe7c44dfa12d993ef75ca467d82","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn localization of measure of arXiv:2505.16093, 'Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system'] Let $\Omega \subsetneq \mathbb{C}$ be a simply connected domain, and let $u$ be a marked boundary point. Let $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ be distinct prime ends of $\partial \Omega$, and let $U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n$ be disjoint closed neighborhoods of $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ in $\Omega$ such that $u \notin U_j$ for all $j$ and $U_i \cap U_j = \emptyset$ for $1 \leq i < j \leq n$. 

We consider probability measures
\[
\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}
\]
on $n$-tuples of unparametrized continuous curves, where each curve starts at $z_j$, is contained in $U_j$, and exits $U_j$ almost surely. 

A family of such measures, indexed by different choices of neighborhoods $\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)$, is called \emph{compatible} if for all $U_j \subset U_j'$, the measure $\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}$ is obtained from 
\[
\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1', U_2', \ldots, U_n'\right)}
\]
by restricting each curve to the portion before it first exits the smaller domain $U_j$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:07:56.709839+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_832623f4fb151fca5d4960658b8dfc5c81436aea135e9b4afa95c31912cd2cb3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:vary of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\mathcal W$ be a white noise with respect to some filtration $\mathcal F$. Let $\overline{\delta}$ be a drift function with respect to $\mathcal F$. We call a collection of continuous processes $\mathcal S=(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in {\mathbb R},a\ge 0}$ a ${\rm BESQ}(\overline{\delta})$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$ if 
   
    (1) The restriction of $\mathcal S$ to each $A_i$ is a ${\rm BESQ}^{\delta_i}$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$.

    (2) The regularity conditions of Definition (def:BESQflow of the paper) hold.
 

If $E$ is a (possibly random) Borel set, we call $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow killed on $E$ the flow obtained from the $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow by absorbing the flow line $\mathcal S_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at $0$ at time $\inf\{x \in E\cap (r,\infty) \,:\, \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0\}$.

 If $E={\mathbb R}$, we will simply say that $\mathcal S$ is a killed  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow. We call general  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow a $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow or a  killed $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:11:44.460227+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8326bce44c888e2b0437f2230fd0425e811f63e685f49590fb6fb1fa97d42591","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Let $V$ be a $k[H]$-module. Let $R$ be such that it contains $R_s$. Let $t\in\mathbb Z\setminus p\mathbb Z$. Let $o$ be the order of $[t]_{p^s}\in (\mathbb Z/p^s\mathbb Z)^{\times}$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} The following statements are equivalent.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (1.a)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is cyclic.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.b)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is indecomposable.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.c)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is strongly indecomposable.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.d)} We have $\imath_V\in\{0,1\}$.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.e)} Each lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ is cyclic.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.f)} Each lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ is cyclic and strongly indecomposable.

\medskip
{\bf (2)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ has a lift $\mathcal H$ to $R$ which is an end-hull of $V$ and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules. Moreover, if $\jmath_V=0$, then we can also assume that $r_{\mathcal H}=0$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} Suppose that $V$ is cyclic. Let $\mathcal V_1$ and $\mathcal V_2$ be two lifts of $V$. Then the $R[H]$-modules $\mathcal V_1$ and $\mathcal V_2$ are isomorphic if and only if the $B[H]$-modules $\mathcal V_1\otimes_R B$ and $\mathcal V_2\otimes_R B$ are isomorphic.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} The $k[H]$-modules $V$ and $V^{(t)}$ are isomorphic.

\smallskip
{\bf (5)} The following statements are equivalent.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (5.a)} There exists a lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ which is $t$-invariant and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules (resp.\ which is $t$-invariant and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules with $r_{\mathcal V^H}=0$).

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (5.b)} For each $b\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket\setminus o\llbracket1,\lfloor\frac{p^s}{t}\rfloor\rrbracket$ such that $\mu_V(b)\neq 0$, $\mu_V(b)$ is a sum of cardinals of orbits of the action of $[t]_{p^s}$ on $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$ (resp.\ $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s^{\ast})$), equivalently of subsets $\Phi$ of $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$ (resp.\ $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s^{\ast})$) with $[t]_{p^s}\cdot\Phi=\Phi$.

\medskip
{\bf (6)} Suppose that $p$ is odd, $[t]_{p^s}=[p^s-1]_{p^s}$ (equivalently, $o=2$) and $\dim_k(V)$ is even. Then $V$ has a lift to $R$ which is a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules and is $t$-invariant.

\medskip
{\bf (7)} Suppose that $p$ is odd, $[t]_{p^s}=[p^s-1]_{p^s}$, $\mu_V(d)$ is even for each odd $d\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$, and $\jmath_V=0$. Then $V$ has a lift $\mathcal V$ to $R$ which is a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules and is $t$-invariant with $r_{\mathcal V}=0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the prescribed zeros form a sequence with no finite accumulation point (|a_n| → ∞ if infinite)","the integers p_n satisfy Σ_n (r/|a_n|)^{p_n+1} < ∞ for every r > 0","multiplicities are encoded by repetition in the list"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.483061+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_8351e8110eb79c81b9035b42e43878b64a0b2a5e2f562abb232805d1c7984b15","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Define the elementary factors E_0(w) = 1 - w and, for p ≥ 1, E_p(w) = (1 - w) exp(w + w^2/2 + ... + w^p/p). Choose nonnegative integers p_n such that the series Σ_n (r/|a_n|)^{p_n + 1} converges for every r > 0 (the choice p_n = n - 1 always works). Then the product P(z) = z^m Π_n E_{p_n}(z/a_n) converges absolutely and uniformly on compact subsets of C and defines an entire function whose zero set is exactly {0} (with multiplicity m, omitted if m = 0) together with the points a_n, each with multiplicity equal to the number of times it is listed. {"assumptions":["H is a complex Hilbert space","in (a): A is self-adjoint, not merely symmetric","in (b): U(t) unitary for every real t, group law on all of ℝ, and strong (or weak) continuity"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.771144+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, spectral theory, quantum dynamics","id":"claim_83536995a52f9d6f74e19531f52ed168e8c98c144cb0af2e28337b9615d9255d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H be a complex Hilbert space. (a) If A is self-adjoint on H, then U(t) = e^{itA} (Borel functional calculus) defines a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: U(t + s) = U(t)U(s), U(0) = I, U(t)* = U(−t), and t ↦ U(t)x is continuous on ℝ for each x. Moreover D(A) = {x ∈ H : lim_{t→0} (U(t)x − x)/t exists} and for x ∈ D(A) that limit equals iAx; D(A) is invariant under each U(t). (b) Conversely, let (U(t))_{t ∈ ℝ} be a family of unitary operators with U(t + s) = U(t)U(s), U(0) = I, and t ↦ U(t)x continuous for each x ∈ H. Then there is a unique self-adjoint operator A with U(t) = e^{itA} for all t, namely Ax = lim_{t→0} (U(t)x − x)/(it) on the set where the limit exists. (c) Weak continuity suffices in (b): if t ↦ ⟨U(t)x, y⟩ is continuous for all x, y, the group is strongly continuous, since ‖U(t)x − x‖² = 2‖x‖² − 2Re⟨U(t)x, x⟩. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:12:13.585474+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_83be08c5ce16833d709f234da619c98fc2dfe15d587232719c2deb8fd78585ee","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 43 (Finite-dimensional relative entropy chain rule) of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Fix \(N\geq1\). \begin{equation}
    \partial_tP_t^N
    =
    -\nabla\cdot(b_t^NP_t^N)+\varepsilon\Delta P_t^N,

satisfy
\[
    \|b_t^N(X)\|+\|\bar b_t^N(X)\|

{"assumptions":["f in L^1(R^d) for the weak (1,1) bound; f in L^p for the strong bound","Lebesgue measure on R^d (the doubling property of the measure is what the proof uses)"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751428+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis","id":"claim_83dc1a42b76b6de69325a6175207b7e1669093bf0f53df5985f5dc3e5cdce959","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For f in L^1_loc(R^d) define the centred maximal function Mf(x) = sup_{r > 0} (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy. Then M is of WEAK type (1,1): for every f in L^1(R^d) and every lambda > 0, |{x : Mf(x) > lambda}| <= 3^d ||f||_1 / lambda. For 1 < p <= infinity, M is bounded on L^p: ||Mf||_p <= C(d,p) ||f||_p, with C(d,p) blowing up like p/(p-1) as p decreases to 1. M is NOT bounded on L^1: if f is not almost everywhere zero then Mf(x) >= c_d ||f||_1 / |x|^d for |x| large, which is not integrable, so Mf is in L^1 only when f = 0 a.e. The uncentred maximal function (supremum over all balls containing x) is comparable to the centred one, with constants depending only on d. [standard; e.g. Stein and Shakarchi, Real Analysis, Theorem 1.1 and Chapter 3]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X takes values in a finite set of size m","X_hat is a function of Y alone, so X -> Y -> X_hat is a Markov chain","P_e = Pr(X_hat != X)"],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236127+00:00","domain":"information theory","id":"claim_83dc491008b3e031d0e3a0ac5475fb48986b2f077baf5876dcd333a684d89f6b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a discrete random variable taking values in a finite set of size m, let Y be any random variable jointly distributed with X, and let X_hat = g(Y) be any estimator of X computed from Y alone, so that X -> Y -> X_hat forms a Markov chain. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:36:12.177577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84005a70176ace5fabd3383c9436c04a93fc7c065d2fbc235871053976c83d35","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 106 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{f(k)}$, and $x = \sum_{k\in K}f(k)$.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] Let $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{g(k)}$. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(f(k) + g(k)) = x + \sum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \item[(ii)] Let $\mf B$ be an HTM and $\varphi\colon\mf A\to\mf B$ be a continuous homomorphism. Then $\sum_{k\in K} \varphi(f(k)) = \varphi(x)$.   
  \item [(iii)] Suppose $\mf A$ is an HTG. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(-f(k)) = -x$.
  \item [(iv)] Suppose $\mf A$ is an HTG and $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{g(k)}$. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(f(k) - g(k)) = x - \sum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["iid edge weights in [a,b] with 0<a<=b<infinity","Fixed distinct endpoints in Z^2 and measurable canonical topmost geodesic selection","Deterministic edge partition; independent same-law block redraws and independent uniform reveal labels"],"created_at":"2026-10-07T04:14:29.906219+00:00","domain":"probability/first-passage-percolation","id":"claim_8410cbafacdae75cb85f1a69ed227c34","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider bond first-passage percolation on Z^2 with iid edge weights supported in [a,b], where 0<a<=b<infinity, and fixed distinct vertices u,v. Let X=T(u,v) and choose a measurable canonical topmost minimizing geodesic (atoms and ties are allowed). Partition the edges into deterministic blocks Lambda. For each block independently redraw its weights from the original law, independently of the environment, and write X^Lambda for the passage time with only that block replaced. Let U_Lambda be the event that the original chosen geodesic uses an edge in Lambda. Give the blocks iid Uniform[0,1] labels tau_Lambda independent of all original and redrawn weights. F_t reveals each labeled block and its original/redrawn weight pair when tau_Lambda<=t; equivalently, for the probabilities of U_Lambda one may reveal only original weights. Define A2=sum_Lambda E[1_U_Lambda (X^Lambda-X)^2], A2plus=sum_Lambda E[((X^Lambda-X)^+)^2], A4=sum_Lambda E[1_U_Lambda ((X^Lambda-X)^+)^4], and Pbar(kappa)=sum_Lambda E[P(U_Lambda|F_(1-kappa))^2]. For every 0<kappa<1, Var(X)<=kappa A2plus+sqrt(A4 Pbar(kappa))<=kappa A2+sqrt(A4 Pbar(kappa)). Positivity and boundedness localize all relevant paths to a deterministic finite edge set, so only finitely many blocks contribute. The proof needs independent blocks, off-geodesic monotonicity and conditional expectations; isotropy and FKG are not assumptions.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:00:45.292667+00:00","domain":"QA-corrected (round 3, audit-driven)","id":"claim_84220182395705cf6378464acbdfd51cdbf89cb6cfa954237e328a2e10157f50","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Taylor's theorem: Let k >= 1 and let f be k times differentiable at the point a, and set P_k(x) = sum_{j=0}^{k} f^{(j)}(a) (x - a)^j / j!, the k-th order Taylor polynomial of f at a (the unique polynomial of degree at most k agreeing with f in value and in the first k derivatives at a). Lagrange form: if in addition f is k+1 times differentiable on an open interval I containing a, then for each x in I there is a point xi strictly between a and x with f(x) - P_k(x) = f^{(k+1)}(xi) (x - a)^{k+1} / (k+1)!. The case k = 1 is the linear approximation and k = 2 the quadratic approximation; for a smooth f, P_k is the truncation at order k of the Taylor series of f at a.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236543+00:00","domain":"numerical analysis","id":"claim_8448b322d9af94267599948f7ac8e35e7642de9c07050163cb44f14c3c789388","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"An explicit s-stage Runge-Kutta method for the initial value problem y' = f(t,y), y(t_0) = y_0, advances y_n to y_{n+1} = y_n + h * sum_{i=1}^{s} b_i * k_i, where k_i = f( t_n + c_i*h, y_n + h*sum_{j<i} a_{ij}*k_j ), and the coefficients a_{ij}, b_i, c_i (the Butcher tableau) typically satisfy c_i = sum_{j<i} a_{ij}. The method has order p if, for sufficiently smooth f, its Taylor expansion in h agrees with the Taylor expansion of the exact solution through the h^p term (equivalently, the local truncation error is O(h^{p+1})). Matching these Taylor expansions imposes polynomial equations on (a_{ij}, b_i, c_i) called order conditions: for example, order 1 requires sum_i b_i = 1, and order 2 additionally requires sum_i b_i*c_i = 1/2. In Butcher's rooted-tree theory there is one order condition per rooted tree up to order p, and the number of independent conditions grows faster than the number of stages s, which is why, for instance, no explicit Runge-Kutta method can reach an order equal to its stage count once the order exceeds 4.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:26:26.806861+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_844c22baeaba6f901d972e29c6601591ad476c0e7355eaae940012895c644523","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:poisson-difference-cc of arXiv:2608.06159, 'Majority Dynamics on Resampled Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi Graphs:\\[0.5ex] Gaussian Winner '] Let \(P_X\sim\Pois(\lambda_X)\) and

\qquad

{"assumptions":["The allocations are defined along sizes with positive conditioning probability.","0 < nu < lambda and the boundary-tilted law pi has generating-function radius one."],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_844ce3c8e953cf9771d011278dae7176f5cf70c2fb67a2cf71d54183386d59e7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked; reduction plus asserted conditional, not a solution] Svante Janson's Problem 18.39 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510, asks whether Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability is possible in the condensation regime 0 < nu < lambda. Janson conjectures that it is not possible for the full sequence and, more strongly, that there are always epsilon > 0 and a subsequence along which Y_(1) >= epsilon n w.h.p. (Example 18.36 gives Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability along a subsequence.) Setting: let w_k >= 0 with w_0 > 0, let Phi(z) = sum_k w_k z^k have radius rho in (0,infinity) with Phi(rho) < infinity, and put pi_k = w_k rho^k/Phi(rho), a law with generating-function radius one and finite mean nu > 0. Let m_n/n -> lambda > nu. (Y_1,...,Y_n) is n i.i.d. pi variables conditioned on sum m_n, Y_(1) = max_i Y_i, and M = (lambda-nu)n. Heuristic rate: carrying M in r = M/a boxes of size a has class weight binomial(n,r) pi_a^r up to the bulk's fluctuation, giving log P = M Lambda(a) + o(M) with Lambda(a) = [log pi_a + log(a/(lambda-nu)) + 1]/a. For pi_k ~ c k^(-beta) and for pi_a = exp(-a^gamma), 0<gamma<1, Lambda increases on large a, so the optimum is a = M (one box), matching the known condensation picture. Since limsup_a Lambda(a) = 0 and Lambda < 0 for large a, Lambda has infinitely many upper records a_1 < a_2 < ... (Lambda(a_j) > Lambda(a) for all a < a_j) exactly when Lambda(a) < 0 for every a; if Lambda(a) >= 0 for some a the maximum is attained and there are finitely many records (Lambda(1) = log pi_1 + log(1/(lambda-nu)) + 1 is positive once lambda - nu < e pi_1). The record asserts, as author-checked and with no proof given beyond reference to an analogous step for Problem 18.40 in a companion memo, the following Proposition: if for some epsilon > 0 and every C, along infinitely many records, Lambda(a_j) - max_{a <= epsilon a_j} Lambda(a) > C a_j^(-1/2), then along n_j = a_j/(lambda-nu), P(Y_(1) >= ((lambda-nu)/2) n_j) -> 1, so the conjecture holds. Caveat: the only derivation offered is the heuristic rate with an o(M) error, which is coarser than the order sqrt(a_j) resolution this hypothesis requires, so the record does not establish the Proposition. The record poses the open Question whether, for every law pi on Z_{>=0} with radius one and finite mean, [log pi_a + log a]/a has infinitely many records with gap exceeding a_j^(-1/2) below max_{a <= epsilon a_j} for some fixed epsilon > 0. This is not a proved equivalence with the conjecture. A negative answer would only give a candidate counterexample, still requiring proof that the allocation spreads. The Question's normalisation and fixed threshold also differ from the Proposition's hypothesis. The problem remains open. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the group is the two-element Cayley group; the claim is a counterexample, not a general theorem","relaxation time is 1/(1 - lambda_2), the standard spectral-gap convention","the target is the geometric-time law of the base walk at tilt p"],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:15:27.869264+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_8494f2b7e60391b8ead2ab87b96e7454cadc38307316484de8264628972059fc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: author_checked_limited_argument - a first-pass structural calculation; no independent review, prior art unverified, and the other questions in the source are untouched] For Metropolis chains targeting a geometric-time law on a Cayley group, the source asks whether the relaxation time decreases monotonically in the tilt p. CLAIM: NO, and the counterexample is the smallest possible one - the two-element group - with relaxation defined the standard way as 1/(1 - lambda_2). (i) NONLAZY BASE. The base walk flips the two states; the target is mu_p = (1/(2-p), (1-p)/(2-p)); the Metropolis matrix is [[p, 1-p],[1, 0]], whose second eigenvalue is p - 1, so tau(p) = 1/(2 - p), STRICTLY INCREASING in p. (ii) LAZY BASE, which removes the convention ambiguity because its spectrum is nonnegative. The base matrix has all entries 1/2, mu_p = ((1+p)/2, (1-p)/2), the Metropolis off-diagonal rates are (1-p)/(2(1+p)) and 1/2, and tau(p) = 1 + p, again increasing. (iii) If laziness is imposed AFTER forming the nonlazy Metropolis kernel, tau(p) = 2/(2 - p), still increasing. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it refutes the literal monotonicity direction only. It does not answer the source's other universal-bound questions and does not resolve its undefined tau(infinity). CONVENTION CAVEAT recorded with the result: if 'relaxation' meant the inverse absolute spectral gap of a nonlazy chain, that convention differs - the lazy example exists precisely to remove the ambiguity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Normalized random-walk rho","Infinite connected d-regular Cayley graph","Sufficient criterion, not equivalence"],"created_at":"2026-10-10T09:11:38.048103+00:00","domain":"Bernoulli bond percolation on graphs","id":"claim_84a5edcb56cb3e3ab5affe7a2fef6535bd7b550c252ea1c6a2dfcdf5fcf9bcaf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"DRAFT source-backed correction, pending referee check. {"assumptions":["Omega is a bounded open subset of R^n","A is measurable, bounded and uniformly elliptic: alpha|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi.xi and |A(x)| <= Lambda","f is in L^p(Omega) with p > n/2 (any p > 1 when n = 2)","u is in H^1_0(Omega) and solves the equation in the weak (distributional, H^1_0-tested) sense","n >= 3 for the stated form of the exponents"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:13:10.395913+00:00","domain":"elliptic PDE, regularity of weak solutions","id":"claim_84be9b126c53ea76ef648ad1432c521b08e53b7112e61244437e9ab9a5acaef4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Omega be a bounded open subset of R^n with n >= 3, and let A be a measurable matrix field on Omega with |A(x)| <= Lambda and A(x)xi.xi >= alpha|xi|^2 for all xi in R^n and a.e. x, with alpha > 0 (bounded measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients; no continuity is assumed). Let f be in L^p(Omega) with p > n/2, and let u in H^1_0(Omega) be the weak solution of -div(A grad u) = f, i.e. integral_Omega A grad u . grad v = integral_Omega f v for all v in H^1_0(Omega). Then u is in L^infinity(Omega) and ||u||_{L^infinity} <= C ||f||_{L^p}, where C depends only on n, p, alpha and |Omega| (not on Lambda and not on any regularity of A). For n = 2 the same conclusion holds for every p > 1. WHERE IT FAILS: the exponent threshold is sharp. At p = n/2 the conclusion is false: on the unit ball of R^n, n >= 3, the function u(x) = log log(1 + 1/|x|) lies in H^1, is unbounded near the origin, and its Laplacian lies in L^(n/2); the borderline case only yields exponential integrability (Brezis-Merle type), not boundedness. Boundedness of Omega is used through the measure |Omega| in the constant. The estimate is one-sided in nothing: it bounds |u| because the argument is applied to u and to -u alike. Ellipticity is essential; for a degenerate A the truncation argument loses the Sobolev inequality it needs.","status":"unverified"}

The multiplier module $\J(\omega_X,\Gamma)$ is defined as
\[ \J(\omega_X,\Gamma):=\bigcap_{\pi:Y\rightarrow X} \Image ({\Tr}_{\pi}:\pi_{*}{\omega}_{Y}(-\lfloor \pi^{*}\Gamma \rfloor) \hookrightarrow {\omega}_{X}(- \lfloor\Gamma\rfloor)),\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.167045+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_850de73ac6eb3c2fe320556c061f49862952ca361103b46dec82b2ce36983d7b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 53 (controlled processes and endpoint measures) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $q_0 \in [0,1)$ and $q_* \in [q_0,q_0+\epsilon]$, define the following mutually independent random variables.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.353526+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_852b0d4dc9f07b4a7615f1f6a29dbffaeb09c786792fcf84fedbb2a651fa5708","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 204 (spatial rerandomization for spherical perceptron) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We use the buckets from Definition~\ref{d:buckets} to
 define a new process $\vY\equiv\vY^{\RomI:\RomIII}$, as follows. First let $a(q_0)$ be sampled uniformly at random from $[M]$. Then, conditional on $a(q_0), \ldots, a(q_d)$, we let $a(q_{d+1})$ be sampled from the measure $\bP$ conditional on the bucket at time $q_d$, that is,
    \[a(q_{d+1})
    \sim \bP
    \bigg( a = \cdot \,\bigg|\, 
    a\in B(q_d,a(q_d)) \bigg)\,.
    \]
We then let $\vY(q_d)$ be the average of $\vX^\trunc$ over all the particles in the bucket containing $a(q_d)$, 
    \beq
    \vY(q_d)
    =
    \sum_{a\in B(q_d,a(q_d))}
    \frac{\vX^\trunc(q_d,a)}{|B(q_d,a(q_d))|}
    \,.
    \eeq
Informally, $\vY$ is the process $\vX^\trunc$ with ``spatial rerandomization at scale $\eta$.'' It is easy to check (by induction) that each $a(q_d)$ is marginally uniform on $[M]$, which implies that $\vX^\trunc(q_d)$ and $\vY(q_d)$ are within $W_{\infty}$ distance $O(\eta/\delta)$ for each fixed $d$.  Likewise, we define $\vY^\frozen\equiv\vY^{\frozen,\RomI:\RomIII}$ to be the spatial rerandomization of $\vX^\frozen$ at scale $\eta$, with random indices $a^\frozen(q_d) \in[M^\frozen]$
and buckets $\mathcal{B}^\frozen(q_d)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. rows with finite eighth moments (mean zero, or centered)","p/n -> gamma in (0, infinity)","loss is the scaled Frobenius norm tr(A A^T)/p"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:37:33.911486+00:00","domain":"multivariate statistics","id":"claim_856459c0e30e1791fc55427a5987d2b06eff22f3cf10fd5350dd6c9ef3854d04","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $x_1, \\dots, x_n \\in \\mathbb{R}^p$ be i.i.d. with mean zero, covariance $\\Sigma$ and finite eighth moments, $S = \\frac{1}{n}\\sum_i x_i x_i^T$, and let $\\mu = \\operatorname{tr}(\\Sigma)/p$, with the scaled Frobenius norm $\\|A\\|^2 = \\operatorname{tr}(A A^T)/p$. Define $\\alpha^2 = \\|\\Sigma - \\mu I\\|^2$, $\\beta^2 = E\\|S - \\Sigma\\|^2$, $\\delta^2 = E\\|S - \\mu I\\|^2 = \\alpha^2 + \\beta^2$. THEOREM (Ledoit and Wolf, 2004). Among all estimators of the form $\\rho_1 I + \\rho_2 S$ with nonrandom $\\rho_1, \\rho_2$, the expected loss $E\\|\\hat\\Sigma - \\Sigma\\|^2$ is minimized by $$\\Sigma^* = \\frac{\\beta^2}{\\delta^2}\\, \\mu I + \\frac{\\alpha^2}{\\delta^2}\\, S,$$ a convex combination of the sample covariance and the scaled identity, with expected loss $\\alpha^2 \\beta^2 / \\delta^2$. The constants have consistent plug-in estimates under general asymptotics $p/n \\to \\gamma \\in (0, \\infty)$: $\\hat\\mu = \\operatorname{tr}(S)/p$, $\\hat\\delta^2 = \\|S - \\hat\\mu I\\|^2$, $\\hat{\\bar b}^2 = \\frac{1}{n^2}\\sum_i \\|x_i x_i^T - S\\|^2$, $\\hat\\beta^2 = \\min(\\hat{\\bar b}^2, \\hat\\delta^2)$, $\\hat\\alpha^2 = \\hat\\delta^2 - \\hat\\beta^2$, and the resulting estimator $\\hat\\Sigma^* = \\frac{\\hat\\beta^2}{\\hat\\delta^2}\\hat\\mu I + \\frac{\\hat\\alpha^2}{\\hat\\delta^2} S$ has the same asymptotic loss as $\\Sigma^*$, is always well conditioned and invertible, and is uniformly no worse than $S$. The shrinkage target is the scaled identity, so the estimator pulls all eigenvalues of $S$ toward their mean $\\hat\\mu$; when one eigenvalue of $\\Sigma$ dominates the trace (a strong spike), $\\hat\\mu$ is dominated by that spike and the target is far from the small eigenvalues.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.714585+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_858fb757b1666fb26e2d0df71b35bebe4def8be329564f7d3dfa42cf98c8c08a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem Tauberianthm of arXiv:2603.24499, 'A central limit theorem for connected components of random coverings of manifolds with nil'] Let $b(t)$ be a measurable function $[0,\infty)\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ which is bounded on finite intervals, and such that
\[
G(s):=\int_0^{\infty}b(t)e^{-st}{\rm d}t
\]
converges (in Lebesgue sense, i.e., absolutely) for all $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with ${{\rm Re}(s)}>0$. Suppose also that there exists an integer $m\ge 1$ and there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that
\[
\lim\limits_{t\rightarrow\infty}tb(t)
\int_{0}^{\varepsilon_0}u^{m-1}e^{-tu}{\rm d}u=1\ .
\]
Let $a(t)$ be a nondecreasing function $[0,\infty)\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$. Suppose there is some $\alpha>0$ such that
\[
f(s):=\int_0^{\infty}a(t)e^{-st}{\rm d}t
\]
converges (absolutely) for all $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with ${{\rm Re}(s)}>\alpha$.

Suppose that for some constant $c_0>0$, the function 
\[
F(s):=f(s)-c_0 G(s-\alpha)
\]
can be rewritten as
\[
F(s)=\frac{g(s)}{(s-\alpha)^{m-1}}+h(s)\ ,
\]
where $g(s)$ is a polynomial of degree at most $m-2$ if $m\ge 2$, or identically zero if $m=1$, and where $h(s)$ is a function which is continuous on ${\rm Re}(s)\ge \alpha$
and holomorphic on the domain ${\rm Re}(s)>\alpha$.

Then, the previous hypotheses imply the asymptotics
\[
a(t)=(c_0+o(1))\ e^{\alpha t}\ b(t)\ ,
\]
as $t\rightarrow\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f measurable and a.e. finite","|E| < infinity (or E sigma-finite, applied piecewise)","the measure is Borel regular, so that inner regularity by closed sets is available"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T17:07:35.550181+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_85c2d201a83f46e0b6df467d153d01f4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f : R^d -> C be Lebesgue measurable and finite almost everywhere, let E be a measurable set of FINITE measure, and let eps > 0. Then there is a compact (hence closed) set F contained in E with |E \\ F| < eps such that the RESTRICTION of f to F is continuous. Moreover one may take g in C_c(R^d) with g = f on F and sup |g| <= sup |f|. The theorem does not assert that f is continuous AT the points of F as a function on R^d: the indicator of the rationals is nowhere continuous on R, yet it agrees with the zero function off a set of measure zero, and Lusin's F can be taken to be any closed set of irrationals of nearly full measure. Finiteness of |E| may be relaxed to sigma-finiteness by exhausting E, at the price of stating the conclusion with |E \\ F| < eps for each piece. [standard; e.g. Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Theorem 2.24]\n\nConverse (Lusin's criterion): let E be a Lebesgue measurable subset of R^d of finite measure and let f:E->C be a function. If for every eps>0 there is a closed F contained in E with |E\\F|<eps such that f restricted to F is continuous, then f is Lebesgue measurable on E. Thus measurability of an a.e.-finite function on such E is equivalent to continuity of its restriction on closed subsets missing arbitrarily small measure. Applied on every bounded measurable piece, this gives the local criterion on R^d.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H: R^n → R finite, convex, superlinear (continuity is automatic from finiteness and convexity)","L = H* so that L is finite, convex and superlinear and L* = H","g: R^n → R Lipschitz continuous","for (iv): g in addition bounded, and uniqueness asserted only among bounded Lipschitz viscosity solutions","(ii) asserts the equation only at points of differentiability; a.e. solutions are not unique, so (ii) alone does not characterize u"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.416738+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: Hamilton-Jacobi equations","id":"claim_8605a80c7ba9fce3f915b195f020fd3a05f4b232377c21c08db9a93c7b73dcf5","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H: R^n → R be convex and superlinear (H(p)/|p| → ∞), let L = H* be its Legendre transform, and let g: R^n → R be Lipschitz. Define u(x,t) := min_{y ∈ R^n} ( t L((x-y)/t) + g(y) ) for t > 0, u(x,0) := g(x). Then: (i) the minimum is attained, u(·,t) is Lipschitz with constant at most Lip(g) for every t > 0, and |u(x,t) - g(x)| ≤ C t with C = max( |L(0)| , max_{|p| ≤ Lip(g)} |H(p)| ); hence u is Lipschitz on R^n × [0,∞) and attains the initial data continuously. (ii) u is differentiable almost everywhere in R^n × (0,∞), and at every point of differentiability u_t(x,t) + H(Du(x,t)) = 0. (iii) u is a viscosity solution of u_t + H(Du) = 0 in R^n × (0,∞) with u(·,0) = g. (iv) If in addition g is bounded, then for every T > 0, u is the unique viscosity solution of this Cauchy problem in the class of bounded Lipschitz functions on R^n × [0,T].","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["uniform (or explicitly known-bias) product measure on {-1,1}^n or {0,1}^n","f in the relevant L^p space, typically boolean or bounded","the noise parameter rho within the sharp Bonami-Beckner range 0<=rho<=sqrt((p-1)/(q-1))","a well-defined Fourier-Walsh expansion, i.e. finite n or a suitable limiting argument"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_86063f9f24404906faff8dccae23920ac77de9a52eff3e621a2ee47cbdd749e7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For f: {-1,1}^n -> R with Fourier-Walsh expansion f = sum_S hat{f}(S) chi_S and the noise operator T_rho, which independently resamples each coordinate to a fresh uniform sign with probability 1-rho (equivalently, flips each coordinate with probability (1-rho)/2, so that each coordinate keeps correlation rho with the input), the Bonami-Beckner inequality states ||T_rho f||_q <= ||f||_p whenever 1 <= p <= q and 0 <= rho <= sqrt((p-1)/(q-1)). Equivalently, T_rho f = sum_S rho^{|S|} hat{f}(S) chi_S, and the inequality forces the Fourier weight of f on high-degree levels to decay geometrically once rho<1, giving sum_S rho^{2|S|} hat{f}(S)^2 <= (E[|f|^p])^{2/p} for suitable p. This is the central tool converting L^2 Fourier information into higher-moment (typically L^4) control, and it underlies the Kahn-Kalai-Linial theorem on the existence of an influential coordinate, the Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm noise-sensitivity theorems, and Friedgut's junta theorem for low-influence functions. It does not directly give influence bounds without further combination with such machinery, and the sharp constant and range of rho given here hold for the uniform measure on {-1,1}^n; biased-p product measures or non-product (dependent) measures require different, generally weaker, p-biased or dependency-adjusted hypercontractive inequalities. Typical failure: Applying the sharp uniform-measure {-1,1}^n hypercontractive constant to a biased-p product measure or to a dependent measure such as the random-cluster or Ising Gibbs measure without switching to the correct p-biased or dependency-adjusted hypercontractivity inequality, whose constants generally degrade as p approaches 0 or 1; this silently invalidates quantitative noise-sensitivity conclusions claimed for critical percolation at p != 1/2 or for genuinely non-product models. Canonical reference: Bonami, 1970, Annales de l'Institut Fourier; Beckner, 1975, Annals of Mathematics; O'Donnell, Analysis of Boolean Functions, 2014, Cambridge University Press.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:23:05.300110+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_860687168ce8d3ce7102561892b7fb672e35da044784d3b34cc4c16e8d539e1d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 15 (Matched-spectrum orientation dependence) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Let $X_0\sim\calN(0,\Sigma)$ with eigenvalues
$\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d>0$, let $1\le d_y\le d$, let
$A\in\R^{d_y\times d}$, and let $R_A=AX_0+\varepsilon$ with
$\varepsilon\sim\calN(0,\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y})$.  Assume
$AA^\top=\Id_{d_y}$.  Thus every admissible $A$ has the same nonzero singular
values; isotropic measurement noise leaves orientation relative to \(\Sigma\)
as the only design variable.  Define
\[
C_\gamma=(\Sigma^{-1}+\gamma\Id_d)^{-1},
\qquad
\Sigma_A^{\rm post}
=
(\Sigma^{-1}+\sigma_y^{-2}A^\top A)^{-1},
\qquad
\psi_\gamma(\lambda)
=
\frac12\log
\frac{\sigma_y^2+\lambda}
{\sigma_y^2+\lambda/(1+\gamma\lambda)}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}

\mathcal M_\gamma(A)=\MI(R_A;Y_\gamma)
=
\frac12\log
\frac{\det(\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y}+A\Sigma A^\top)}
{\det(\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y}+AC_\gamma A^\top)}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, among all row-orthonormal rank-$d_y$ measurements,
\begin{align}

\frac12\sum_{i=d-d_y+1}^{d}
\log\!\left(1+\frac{\lambda_i}{\sigma_y^2}\right)
&\le \MI(X_0;R_A)
\le
\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{d_y}
\log\!\left(1+\frac{\lambda_i}{\sigma_y^2}\right),\\

2\MI(X_0;R_A)
&=
\log\frac{\det\Sigma}{\det\Sigma_A^{\rm post}},\\

\sum_{i=d-d_y+1}^{d}\psi_\gamma(\lambda_i)
&\le \mathcal M_\gamma(A)
\le
\sum_{i=1}^{d_y}\psi_\gamma(\lambda_i).
\end{align}
For every $\gamma>0$, $\psi_\gamma$ is strictly increasing.  Equality in the
upper (respectively, lower) bounds is attained by choosing the row space of
$A$ to be the span of the largest (respectively, smallest) $d_y$ prior
eigenvectors.  If the boundary eigenvalue is repeated, the extremizing row
space need not be unique: the required dimensions may be chosen arbitrarily
within that eigenspace.  Hence equal operator
singular values do not determine clean
measurement information, posterior covariance-volume contraction, or
reverse-path assimilation once the prior is anisotropic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Real finite data with 1<=rank(X)=q<n; hidden width h>=min(m,n)","Euclidean continuous gradient flow; unrestricted linear-regression comparator","Effective imbalance delta_eff>0, with the precise zero-padded eigenvalue indices"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T20:55:59.752362+00:00","domain":"Linear-network gradient flow and LoRA initialization","id":"claim_86480a93c006d4288d3376eeb3e6b4c4235f9c037c4718b56ca06aab516c37c7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a real N-by-n design of rank q>=1 with q<n, Y an N-by-m response matrix, and hidden width h>=min(m,n). Consider continuous Euclidean gradient flow on L(U,V)=||Y-X U V^T||F^2/2, U n-by-h, V m-by-h. Choose an orthonormal basis Phi1 of the data row space, set U1=Phi1^T U, and let a=lambda_q(X^T X)>0 be the smallest positive design-covariance eigenvalue. The latent imbalance D=U1^T U1-V^T V is constant along the flow. Using decreasing eigenvalues with lambda_i=0 when i exceeds the matrix dimension, define delta_eff=max(lambda_q(D),0)+max(lambda_m(-D),0). If delta_eff>0 at initialization, the excess over the unrestricted linear-regression optimum obeys L(t)-L_star<=exp(-2a delta_eff t)(L(0)-L_star) for every t>=0. This is the sufficient-imbalance specialization of Min, Tarmoun, Vidal and Mallada, Convergence and Implicit Bias of Gradient Flow on Overparametrized Linear Networks, arXiv:2105.06351, Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 (printed pp.9-10), with the zero-padding convention on p.4 and delta_eff in equation (20), p.8. Positive definiteness of the h-by-h D alone is insufficient when q>h: its q-th eigenvalue is zero by convention, while all eigenvalues of -D are negative (or zero-padded). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:42:55.336004+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_869349968fe908617457a152b589c043b2199dfadd126b1ad64f1e5eb9e4f4d4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The comparison and rigidity arguments used below are collected in the following proposition.

\textup{(i)} Assume that for some compact interval $K$, $\delta>0$ and $W\ge1$,
\[
W(x)\to+\infty,\; (\cA_\R+\lambda)W\le-\delta W\;\hbox{in }\R\setminus K.
\]
Let $U$ be one of the two components of $\R\setminus K$. If $u\in C^1(U)$ extends continuously to the interaction collar of $U$, satisfies $u^+=o(W)$ at the infinite end, $(\cA_\R+\lambda)u\ge0$ in $U$, and $u\le0$ on the finite interaction collar of width $R_J$, then $u\le0$ in $U$.

\textup{(ii)} Let $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$. Assume that there exist a compact interval $K$, $\delta>0$ and $W\in C^1(\R)$ such that $W\ge1$, $W(x)\to+\infty$, and
\[
(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)W\le-\delta W\;\hbox{in }\R\setminus K.
\]
Suppose that every positive eigenfunction associated with $\lambda_p$ is $o(W)$. Then every such eigenfunction has $W$-minimal growth, and $\lambda_p$ is simple in the positive cone: any two positive eigenfunctions associated with $\lambda_p$ are proportional.

\textup{(iii)} Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}. Let $u>0$ satisfy $u=o(W)$ and $(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)u\le0$ in $\R$, where $\lambda_p=\Lp(\R)$. Then $u$ is a positive multiple of the principal eigenfunction. In particular the inequality is necessarily an equality.

\textup{(iv)} Under the same hypotheses, let $f\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $f\ge0$ and $f\not\equiv0$. There is no positive $u\in C^1(\R)$ with $u=o(W)$ satisfying $(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)u=-f$ in $\R$.

\textup{(v)} Assume the Lyapunov hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}. Let $u,v>0$, $u=o(W)$, $v=o(W)$, satisfy
\[
(\cA_\R+\lambda_p)u\ge0,\qquad (\cA_\R+\lambda_p)v\le0.
\]
If $u\le Cv$ on one compact interaction collar containing the Lyapunov core, then $u\le Cv$ on $\R$. If equality of the optimal constant is attained at one point and both differential inequalities are equalities, then $u$ and $v$ are proportional.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:10:07.448983+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_86a001531250df0f32c57191dcebd574ecb4174b22edb3dac30086bc48aa9860","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary No finite-moment determination of annealed complexity of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[corollary]{cor:no-finite-moment}

{"assumptions":["X_1, ..., X_n independent (not necessarily identically distributed)","f(X) square-integrable","no boundedness or Lipschitz assumption; those are needed only for the exponential tail (McDiarmid), not for the variance bound"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.049339+00:00","domain":"concentration of measure (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_86cf1e9337e554632973d7e667c68acea223b8cc18e958d4dd1752b1136526fa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables and f a square-integrable function of them, Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n). Let X_1', ..., X_n' be an independent copy of the X_i and Z_i' = f(X_1, ..., X_i', ..., X_n) the value with the i-th coordinate resampled. Then Var(Z) <= (1/2) sum_{i=1}^n E[(Z - Z_i')^2] = sum_{i=1}^n E[(Z - E_i Z)^2], where E_i denotes expectation over X_i alone (Efron and Stein 1981; Steele 1986 for the constant 1/2). Equivalently Var(Z) <= sum_i E[Var_i(Z)]. The inequality is tight for linear f. {"assumptions":["the domain is reflexive for the converse direction","compactness always implies complete continuity, with no reflexivity needed","terminology must be checked in older sources, where 'completely continuous' can mean 'compact'"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:46.573661+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, compact operators, Banach space theory","id":"claim_8709e389c807abb0604721e0033898acf007e6902456fe85b7b0c2585491a096","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Compact operators are completely continuous: they send weakly convergent sequences to norm convergent ones. The converse needs the domain to be reflexive, because the proof runs 'bounded sequence -> weakly convergent subsequence -> norm convergent image', and the first arrow is exactly reflexivity (with the Eberlein-Smulian theorem). The counterexample is the identity of l^1: by Schur's property, every weakly convergent sequence in l^1 converges in norm, so the identity is completely continuous, yet it is not compact because l^1 is infinite-dimensional. A related trap in the other direction is the use of weak sequential compactness of the unit ball: in a nonreflexive space such as c_0 or L^1([0,1]) a bounded sequence need not have any weakly convergent subsequence, so arguments of the form 'the sequence is bounded, so pass to a weakly convergent subsequence, and then apply compactness of T' are invalid there. Also note that the older literature uses 'completely continuous' as a synonym for 'compact'; when reading a classical source, check which meaning is in force before transporting a statement.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.684375+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_872275d9465d671e04c6a26b80dfce8663fa08fc9e3ab19fa8af73023d3c07f6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Classification of entire logarithmic signatures) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $\gamma:[0,T]\to V$ be continuous and of bounded variation, and put
\[
\overline\gamma_t=\gamma_t-\gamma_0,
\qquad
 g=S(\gamma),\qquad l=\log g,\qquad v=\gamma_T-\gamma_0.
\]
Assume $R(l)=\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $v=0$, then $g=1$; equivalently, $\gamma$ is tree-like.
\item If $v\neq0$, there is $t_*\in[0,T]$ such that, with
\[
\alpha=\overline\gamma|_{[0,t_*]},
\qquad a=S(\alpha),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
S(\gamma)=a\e^v a^{-1}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Conversely, if $a$ is a bounded-variation signature, then $a\e^v a^{-1}$ has an entire logarithmic signature for every $v\in V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.163448+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_87759836e81f17895efdf77150cc0707d64729d7d8cfffca25cd91b8db896b68","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Ppn 26 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall $F^{\riv}$ from \eqref{e:F.iv}, and
$F^{\rv}$ from \eqref{e:F.rv}. 
    For sufficiently large $N$, we have for all $t\in \R$
    \[
    \P(F^{\riv} \ge t)
    \le \P\bigg(
    F^{\rv}+ \frac{\epsilon'}{5}
    \ge t
    \bigg) + e^{-cN} \,.
    \]
That is, $F^{\rv}$
approximately stochastically dominates
$F^{\riv}$.

\begin{proof}
For each $j\in[r]$, let
    \[\bv_1(B_j)\equiv
    \frac{\bz(B_j)}{\|\bz(B_j)\|}\,,\]
and complete this to a (Haar random)
orthonormal basis
$(\bv_a(B_j) : 1\le a \le |B_j|)$
of $\R^{|B_j|}$. Let $\tau_j \equiv \|\bz^{B_j}\|^2 / |B_j|$. Then we can rewrite \eqref{e:F.v} and \eqref{e:bar.F.U} as
    \begin{align*}
    F_v(\bG,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j}{MN}
        \sum_{a=1}^{|B_j|}
        (
         \bv_a(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2
         \,,\\
    \bar{F}_U(\bG,\bz,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\tau_j \hU_j}{MN}
        ( \bv_1(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2\,.
    \end{align*}
If we split off the $a=1$ term of $F_v$ and combine it with $\bar{F}_U$, then we see that $F_v+\bar{F}_U$ is the same as the sum of the two terms
    \begin{align*}
    F_{v\setminus1}(\bG,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j}{MN}
        \sum_{a=2}^{|B_j|}
        (
         \bv_a(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2
         \,,\\
    \bar{F}_{U+}(\bG,\bz,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j+
            \tau_j \hU_j}{MN}
        ( \bv_1(B_j),\bG^{B_j} \by)^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Fix arbitrary representatives $a_j \in B_j$, and denote
    \begin{align*}
    \acute{F}_{v\setminus}
    (\bG,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j}{MN}
        \sum_{a\in B_j\setminus a_j}
        (\bg^a,\by)^2
    \le F_v(\bG,\by)\,, \\
    \acute{F}_{U+}
        (\tbmeta,\by)
    &= \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{\hv_j+
            \tau_j \hU_j}{MN}
    (\tbmeta^{r+j},\by)^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Recalling $F_w$ from \eqref{e:F.w} and
$\bar{F}_B$ from \eqref{e:bar.F.B}, define
    \begin{align*}
    \acute{F}_-(\bG,\tbmeta,\by)
    &\equiv F_w(\by)
    +\acute{F}_{v\setminus}
        (\bG,\by)
    +\bar{F}_B(\tbmeta,\by)
    +\acute{F}_{U+}
        (\tbmeta,\by)
    \\
    &\le F_w(\by)
    +\acute{F}_v(\bG,\by)
        +\bar{F}_B(\tbmeta,\by)
        +\acute{F}_{U+}
        (\tbmeta,\by)
    \equiv\ddot{F}(\bG,\tbmeta,\by)
    \end{align*}
By gaussian rotational invariance,
$\bar{F}$ has the same distribution (as processes indexed by $\by$) as $\acute{F}_-$, which in term is dominated by $\ddot{F}$. Finally, the difference between $\ddot{F}$ and $\acute{F}$
is bounded, for all $\|\by\|^2=N$, by
\[
        \bigg|\sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{(\tau_j-1) \hU_j}{MN}
        (\tbmeta^{r+j}, \by)^2\bigg|
        \le \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{|\tau_j-1| |\hU_j|}{M}
        \|\tbmeta^{r+j}\|^2\,.
    \]
It holds with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$ that
    \[|\tau_j-1| \le \frac{\alpha \iota \epsilon'}{20r},\quad
    \max_{j\in[r]}
    \frac{\|\tbmeta^{r+j}\|}{N^{1/2}}
     \le 2\,.
    \]
On this event, the above quantity is bounded by 
    \[
        r \cdot \frac{\alpha \iota \epsilon'}{20} \cdot \frac{\|\hU\|_\infty}{M} \cdot 4N 
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:fp-normalization-bd}}{\le} \frac{\epsilon'}{5}\,,
    \]
which concludes the proof.\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu_1 and mu_2 strictly positive on a common finite distributive lattice closed under meet and join","the pointwise Holley ratio condition mu_1(x v y) mu_2(x ^ y) >= mu_1(x) mu_2(y) holding for all pairs x, y","events being compared are increasing with respect to the same partial order used to define the lattice"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.972949+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8778e7a65e49c4be1f23175bfeb78103a14f5cdd5ed03f4f8cc84200ea1e4687","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let mu_1, mu_2 be strictly positive probability measures on a common finite distributive lattice (e.g. {0,1}^E ordered coordinatewise). If the Holley condition holds, mu_1(x v y) mu_2(x ^ y) >= mu_1(x) mu_2(y) for all configurations x, y, then mu_1 stochastically dominates mu_2, meaning mu_1(A) >= mu_2(A) for every increasing (monotone) event A. This is a purely combinatorial, pointwise sufficient condition for stochastic domination between two measures that need not be product measures, and it strictly generalizes the FKG inequality, which is recovered as the special case mu_1 = mu_2. It is the standard tool for comparing Gibbs measures with different boundary conditions or parameters in the Ising model, the random-cluster model, and other lattice systems, and for monotone-coupling arguments more generally. The theorem does not establish the Holley condition itself, which can be as hard to verify as the comparison one is trying to prove; it gives only qualitative stochastic domination, with no quantitative bound on the total-variation distance between mu_1 and mu_2; and it requires strict positivity of both measures on the entire lattice. Typical failure: Assuming the Holley condition holds because mu_1 looks larger than mu_2 in some averaged or marginal sense; the condition is a pointwise, multiplicative statement that must hold for every pair of configurations including their join and meet, and it can fail even when mu_1 does stochastically dominate mu_2 for unrelated reasons, or when only checked on a generating set of configurations rather than genuinely all pairs. Canonical reference: Holley, 1974, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Georgii, Haggstrom and Maes, 2001, in Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomena, vol. 18, Academic Press.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:22:46.462522+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8799228f51664a63a96697e1e1b421fa75b84701342c09e29dfb0fd72c5e5f0c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 23 of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] [The geometric wave-transport-divergence-curl formulation of the compressible Euler equations]

	Above, the main terms $\mainnullform_{(\VortVort)}^i$ and $\mainnullform_{(\DivGradEnt)}$

Let $\phi = \phi_N : V_N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be a test function of the form
	\[ \phi (x,y) = \sum_{k=2}^K \alpha_k(y) f_k^N(x) \]

Let $\varphi = \varphi_N : V_N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be the extension
	\[ \varphi (x,y) \coloneqq \phi \Big( x , \frac{y}{a_N} \Big)\,, \qquad (x,y) \in V_N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} \,, \]
with $a_N$ as in~(equation eq:aN of the paper). Assume that Assumption~(a:spectral of the paper) holds for each $2 \leq k \leq K$, and that
	\[ a_N \gg \log N + \log_+ a_N \qquad \text{as } N \to \infty\,. \]

	\[ \sigma^2(\phi) \coloneqq \sum_{k=2}^K \alpha_k(y_0)^2 \, \frac{1 - e^{-2\g_k y_0}}{2\g_k} \,\geq\, 0\,. \]
Then, with $T = N \lfloor y_0 a_N \rfloor$,
	\begin{equation}
	 \frac{1}{\sqrt{Na_N}} \langle \! \langle D_T , \varphi \rangle \! \rangle \Rightarrow
	\mathcal{N} \big( 0\,,\, \sigma^2(\phi) \big)
	\end{equation}
as $N\to\infty$.

Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on

such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.  Then, there exists a constant 
$C = C(u_0,\ell_0)$ such that, for $\ell \geq  \ell_0$, and a function
$h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}   
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}}h(s,x)\\

\Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}\big[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)\big] 
-\frac{1}{2} \tilde f''(u_0) \Big((\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x) - u_0)^2- \tfrac{{\rm var}(u_0) }{2\ell +1}\Big)\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big]

\int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in \T_N}|h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times\Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)] 
-\tilde f'(u_0)
\big(\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)-u_0\big) \Big\} ds\Big|^p\Big] 
\notag  \\
& \hskip 10mm
 \leq \ CT^{p-1} N^p \ell^{-p} \|f\|^{p}_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})} \int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in \T_N}|h(t,x)|^p dt.  \notag

{"assumptions":["Omega open in R^n (bounded for the global space)","k >= 0 integer","0 < alpha <= 1"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:46.146895+00:00","domain":"function spaces for PDE","id":"claim_87b428ba115e4106c40672432530cf35b534ad47a8d140e4c6e4bfa9dc7929da","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Omega in R^n be open, k >= 0 an integer and 0 < alpha <= 1. For a function v on a set S, [v]_{alpha;S} = sup over x, y in S with x != y of |v(x) - v(y)| / |x - y|^alpha. For bounded Omega, C^{k,alpha}(closure of Omega) is the space of u in C^k(Omega) such that every derivative D^beta u with |beta| <= k extends continuously to the closure and ||u||_{C^{k,alpha}} = sum_{|beta| <= k} sup_Omega |D^beta u| + sum_{|beta| = k} [D^beta u]_{alpha;Omega} is finite; it is a Banach space. The local space C^{k,alpha}(Omega) consists of u in C^k(Omega) with u in C^{k,alpha}(closure of U) for every open U with compact closure in Omega. C^{0,1} is the Lipschitz class; C^{1,1} (bounded second difference quotients, equivalently W^{2,infinity} locally) is strictly larger than C^2. A bounded open set Omega is a C^{k,alpha} domain if every boundary point has a neighborhood U such that, in suitable rotated coordinates, Omega intersected with U = {x in U : x_n > g(x_1, ..., x_{n-1})} for some g of class C^{k,alpha}. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.143238+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88171b3bff4767675288df1575dfdfc282982120431430153abd723045933ee1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:constant-overshoot-families of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] Consider the first passage of an additive mean-zero walk above an integer level.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Bounded integer up-steps (C1).} If the increments take integer values with maximal up-step $+1$, the walk lands exactly one unit above the level, so $\omega=1$. (For any such $X$, $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>0]=1$.)
\item \emph{Geometric positive increments (C(2,$\cdot$)).} If the positive increment has the geometric law on $\{1,2,\ldots\}$ with success probability $q\in(0,1)$, namely $\mathbb{P}(X=k)=q(1-q)^{k-1}$, then by the memorylessness of the geometric the conditional overshoot is again geometric with the same law, and $\omega=1/q$. (Equivalently, the companion's parametrization gives $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>k]=k+p/(1-p)$ in the decay-ratio convention; see (rem:geometric-param of the paper).)
\item \emph{Exponential right tail (C(3,$a$)).} If the positive increment has an exponential right tail, $\mathbb{P}(X>y)=c e^{-ay}$, then by the memorylessness of the exponential the overshoot is exponential with mean $\omega=1/a$, and $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>y]=y+1/a$ (the constant $c$ is irrelevant).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T16:46:51.519522+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_881cc0825a27c3b2e8c5d0212f5b4813ca1a41b021b0e5c2c36188af50956696","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In probability theory, the central limit theorem states that, under certain circumstances, the probability distribution of the scaled mean of a random sample converges to a normal distribution as the sample size increases to infinity. Under stronger assumptions, the Berry–Esseen theorem, or Berry–Esseen inequality, gives a more quantitative result, because it also specifies the rate at which this convergence takes place by giving a bound on the maximal error of approximation between the normal distribution and the true distribution of the scaled sample mean. The approximation is measured by the Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance. In the case of independent samples, the convergence rate is n−1/2, where n is the sample size, and the constant is estimated in terms of the third absolute normalized moment. It is also possible to give non-uniform bounds which become more strict for more extreme events.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:53:54.888533+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88368d75eb5a59bca5dc6a2ec013a50b28c97bace5b9a2fccc14390eebcf798f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2607.17087, 'Transportation-cost inequalities for invariant measures of stochastic reaction-diffusion e'] Let $p>2$, let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, and let $(e_k)_{k\geq 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $H$. Let $W$ be an $H$-cylindrical Wiener process.
Let
\[
\Phi: [0,T]\times\Omega \longrightarrow \mathcal{L}\big(H,L^p([0,1])\big)
\]
be an operator-valued progressively measurable process. Assume that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\int_0^T \Vert G(t)\Vert_{L^p([0,1])}^2\,dt <\infty,
\end{equation}
where
\[
G(t,x):= \bigg( \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \big|\big(\Phi(t) e_k \big)(x) \big|^2 \bigg)^{1/2}, \qquad x\in[0,1] .
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E} \left\Vert \int_0^T\Phi (t)\,dW(t) \right\Vert_{L^p([0,1])}^2
\leq (p-1) \mathbb{E}\int_0^T \Vert G(t)\Vert_{L^p([0,1])}^2\,dt.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(X,d) is a compact metric space","T: X -> X is continuous","for the non-compact extension, T is uniformly continuous and the entropy is taken as a supremum over compact subsets, and then depends on the uniform equivalence class of d"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:07:38.814666+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, entropy","id":"claim_885e1c5ce5a142a5b0817a051568e1c6290d72f8e2a8225eed7dad76bf607388","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T: X -> X continuous. For n >= 1 define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max_{0 <= i <= n-1} d(T^i x, T^i y). A set E contained in X is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if d_n(x,y) > eps for all distinct x, y in E; let s_n(eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n, eps)-separated set. A set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if for every x in X there is y in F with d_n(x,y) <= eps; let r_n(eps) be the smallest cardinality of an (n, eps)-spanning set. Both are finite by compactness. THEOREM (Bowen, Dinaburg): h_top(T) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log s_n(eps) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log r_n(eps), and this common value coincides with the Adler-Konheim-McAndrew topological entropy defined through open covers. The limits in eps exist in [0, +infinity] because s_n(eps) and r_n(eps) are nonincreasing in eps, so the inner quantities are nonincreasing in eps. The two counts are comparable at shifted scales: r_n(eps) <= s_n(eps) <= r_n(eps/2). SHARP EDGES. (a) The order of the limits is not negotiable: for a FIXED eps the quantity limsup_n (1/n) log s_n(eps) is in general strictly smaller than h_top(T) (it is the 'entropy at scale eps'), and it is only after eps -> 0 that one gets the entropy. The single exception worth remembering is an expansive homeomorphism, where any eps below the expansive constant already gives the answer. (b) Compactness is used to make the counts finite and to make the value a topological invariant. Bowen's extension to a uniformly continuous map of a possibly non-compact metric space, taking the supremum of the above over compact subsets, defines a quantity h_d(T) that depends on the METRIC and not only on the topology: uniformly equivalent metrics give the same value, but merely topologically equivalent ones need not, so on non-compact spaces 'the topological entropy' is not well defined without naming the metric. (c) Separated and spanning counts measure ORBIT distinguishability over a finite time window; they say nothing by themselves about invariant measures. The link to measures is the variational principle, h_top(T) = sup over T-invariant Borel probabilities mu of h_mu(T), which is a separate theorem and is not proved by the counting argument below. (d) The definition uses only forward iterates 0, ..., n-1, and for a homeomorphism this already gives the entropy of T; the two-sided window max over |i| <= n gives the same number, not twice it.","status":"unverified"}

Assume
\[

\[
        h_n=o(b_n),\qquad b_n\mu_n\to0,

and such that the following two assumptions hold.

\end{enumerate}

\[
        \mu_n T_{A_n}\Rightarrow \Exp(1)
\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:33:11.957227+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88f589c614dce080d582de2c67c899001235973ddf37062cd739b20c516e639c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary Weak Simplex Conjecture of arXiv:2607.14087, 'Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution of the Weak Simplex Conjecture'] \label[corollary]{cor:wsc}
Let $m=d+1$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ be unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let the
message $I$ be uniform on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$.  Under the channel
\[
  Y=\lambda x_I+Z,
  \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d),\quad \lambda>0,
\]
the average probability of correct maximum-likelihood decoding is no larger
than for a regular simplex.  For every fixed $\lambda>0$, equality holds if
and only if the $x_i$ form a regular simplex.  Thus the regular simplex is the
unique maximizer up to rotation and relabeling. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.258899+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_894d63647a3652d93a61cb3ba7aba6bd142d16cec67bf95caa5a78e59ce5c7f5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 11 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $p \in S^m(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d)$. Let $U, V$ be two open sets of $\Rr^d$, $V$ being convex, and let $\chi : U \to V$ be a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying $\|\Jac \chi^{-1} - I_d\|_{L^{\infty}(V)} <1$. 
Let $\psi \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}_c(V)$ and $\rho \in \mathcal{C}_c^{\infty}(U)$ 
such that~\(\rho\) is equal to~\(1\) on a neighborhood of $\chi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp} \psi)$. If~\(f\) is compactly supported in~\(V\) set~\(C_\chi f\) the function corresponding to~\(f\circ \chi\) on~\(U\) and~\(0\) outside~\(U\). Operator~\(C_\chi\) is a bijection between functions compactly supported in~\(V\) and functions compactly supported in~\(U\).
Set 
\[
Q = \psi C_{\chi}^{-1} \rho \Op(p) \rho C_{\chi}\psi,
\]
and define $J(x,y)=\displaystyle\int_0^1 \Jac \chi^{-1}(tx+(1-t)y)^\top\mathrm{d}t$ for $x, y \in V$.

Then, there exists $q\in S^m(\Rr^d \times \Rr^d)$ such that $Q=\psi\Op(q)\psi$, and 
moreover, $q$ admits the following asymptotic expansion on a neighborhood of $\supp \psi$ included in~\(V\):
\begin{equation}
    
        q(x,\xi) \sim \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} \frac{\rho(\chi^{-1}(x))}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !} \partial_y^\alpha \left.\partial_{\xi}^\alpha \left(\rho(\chi^{-1}(y))p\left(\chi^{-1}(x),J(x,y)^{-1}\xi\right)\left\vert\frac{\det \Jac \chi^{-1} (y)}{\det J(x,y)}\right\vert\right)\right\vert_{y=x}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.242501+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_895cfe1f7a99a92e12ef6e3745b0d8f821e23c4dd41df6ec46a73ebf705ad4e4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 (the constant-field Fourier representation) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] With $(\tau,\xi)$ the spacetime Fourier variables, $\lambda$ as in
\eqref{eq:Bmult}, and $\tau_\pm=\tau\pm\lambda$, one has

 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal A^+f}=\mathrm i\tau_+\widetilde f,

 \widetilde{\mathcal A^-f}=\mathrm i\tau_-\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\Box f}=-\tau_+\tau_-\widetilde f .
\end{equation}
Consequently $D_\pm=-\mathrm i\mathcal A^\pm$ are commuting self-adjoint
operators on $L^2(dt dy)$ and, for every Borel function $\Phi$,

 \Phi(D_+,D_-)f

\]
so these groups are isometries on every $L^p$ and unitary on $L^2$.  In particular,

 [\Lambda^{\sreg},\mathcal B]=0
 \qquad(\sreg\in\Real),

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:05:52.484342+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_897545b1017e10badef5805f077410e9b9e1d44598ace109762acb07fefe50bb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition lemma:frechet of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Suppose $F : L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ has continuous partial derivatives with respect to the standard

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.340351+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89ac5cad7b954e6da1ebf203c7018e3caa1dbffa166a9f1a94566752511ba361","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Averaged macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(d\ge 3\), let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, and let \(p_{d,n}\) denote its law. Assume
    \[
    d>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(\lambda>0\), and let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). Assume
    \[
    \lambda>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\), that is, the pairing model conditioned on simplicity. Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho.
    \]
    If
    \[
    \rho>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr),
    \]
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:26:20.492151+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89e168f74bd653d83855c27b98aadbf0f050b5d8f604388903e34be3896d57b7","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem lemma:delta-map of arXiv:2411.11676, 'Surface sums for lattice Yang--Mills in the large-$N$ limit'] Let $s = (\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_n) \in \mathcal{S}_o$ be a non-null string, and let $\delta = \delta(s)$. For each positive splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, we have that there is some $1 \leq h_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - h_{s'}, h_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto h_{s'}$ on the domain $\mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$ can be chosen to be injective. 

Similarly, for each negative splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, either 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - 2, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n),\qquad \Big(\delta(s') \leq (\delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n)\quad  \text{if}\quad \delta_1 = 2\Big),$$ 
or there is some $1 \leq g_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that  
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - g_{s'}, g_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto g_{s'}$ (whose domain is a suitable subset of $\mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$) can be taken as injective.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:24:20.957928+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a200e155b746988852d7a3cdc34ec1f89cfa5cbba2b8068d868f5e293e2c9f0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm2.7 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] {\rm (Cuny and Lin)}.
 
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a real strictly stationary, 
{\bf reversible} Markov chain that satisfies $\alpha$-mixing with 
$\alpha_X(n) \to 0$ at least exponentially fast as $n \to \infty$.  
Suppose
$h: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$  is a Borel function such that
\begin{equation}
\label {eq2.71}
0\ <\ E[\, [h(X_0)]^2]\ <\ \infty \indent  {\rm and} \indent E[h(X_0)]\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}
Then $\sigma^2 := E[\, [h(X_0)]^2] + 2 \cdot \sum_{k=1}^\infty E[h(X_0) \cdot h(X_k)]$
exists in $(0, \infty)$, with the sum converging absolutely (in fact with the summands
decaying at least exponentially fast); and
$n^{-1} \textrm{\rm Var}(\sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)) \to \sigma^2$ as $n \to \infty$.
Further, $(1/(n^{1/2}\sigma)) \sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k) \to N(0,1)$ in distribution as $n \to \infty$.  

   Thus, letting $\sigma_n(h) := \|\sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)\|_2$ for each $n \in \mathbb N$, 
one has that $[\sigma_n(h)]^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^n h(X_k)$ converges in distribution
to $N(0,1)$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H is a complex Hilbert space","A and B are self-adjoint","A + B is essentially self-adjoint on D(A) ∩ D(B) (in particular this intersection is dense)","for the semigroup form: A, B bounded below and Q(A) ∩ Q(B) dense"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.771844+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, operator semigroups, quantum dynamics, Feynman path integrals","id":"claim_8a42ecd9291b18c555dbdf4b4b8eeec51666c9820d4d30934c9988c54e0e2269","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let A and B be self-adjoint operators on a complex Hilbert space H and suppose that A + B, defined on D(A) ∩ D(B), is essentially self-adjoint (for example self-adjoint) there; write C for its closure. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:37:28.987837+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a48bd521f6f52464529287b734e464b9721a1edd5f8442b903c535c7608e913","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:phi-psi of arXiv:2412.01015, 'Classical beta ensembles and related eigenvalues processes at high temperature and the Mar'] Let $\{h_n\}_{n \ge 0}$ and $\{p_n\}_{n \ge 0}$ be two sequences with $h_0 = p_0 = 1$. \[
